summary: Prettier forces blank lines around top-level `<!-- bkit:tracker -->` markers (unremovable at source); two-digit steps silently escape their list item
description:
- **Category:** tooling
- **Symptom:** `.bkit/workflows/*.md` carry blank lines around every `<!-- bkit:tracker ... -->` marker. Stripping them and running `pnpm format` puts them straight back (verified: 82 removed from `bkit-build.md` -> prettier re-added exactly 82, restoring the file byte-for-byte). The render strips the marker LINES but leaves the surrounding blanks, so the `.claude` / `.cursor` / `.opencode` command mirrors get doubled blank lines AND the single `> [!CAUTION]` execution-protocol blockquote is split into three separate blockquotes - only the first keeps the CAUTION admonition. `.claude/` etc are in `.prettierignore`, so nothing downstream cleans it up. Separately, under two-digit steps (`10.`) the step body silently escapes its list item.
- **Root cause:** Two independent prettier-markdown behaviours, split by marker indent. **(1) Top-level markers (indent 0, 158 of them):** prettier separates a block-level HTML node from an adjacent blockquote with a blank line and reverts any attempt to close the gap. NOT author style - unremovable at source. Exception: an html node directly after another html node on the very next line keeps its adjacency, which is why `github end` + `linear start` are the one pair that never gets separated. **(2) Indented markers (inside list items):** prettier PRESERVES whatever is there; blanks are author-written. But looseness is per-item and contagious - a list item is loose if it contains a blank line OR is followed by one, and prettier then propagates blank lines to EVERY block boundary inside that item. So ONE blank between step 9 and step 10 (nothing to do with markers) explodes blanks around every marker inside step 9. **(3) Escaped two-digit steps:** when a step number crosses `9.` -> `10.` the required content indent goes 3 -> 4. Body left at indent 3 is no longer part of the item; prettier prints the AST it actually parsed, dedenting the body to column 0 and stranding the `<!-- end -->` markers at indent 3. Step 10's body is not inside step 10 and the ordered list fragments.
- **Fix or rule:** Do NOT try to de-blank top-level markers at source - prettier reverts it; that damage can only be fixed render-side (collapse orphaned blanks when stripping a marker line). DO tighten indented markers: drop blanks inside marker-bearing list items AND the blanks BETWEEN their numbered steps (a tight list still renders each step on its own numbered line - this is not a wall of text). Gate any such sweep on an AST diff that normalises `spread`/`loose` away and compares everything else - blank-line edits can silently merge paragraphs. Two traps when automating: a body-boundary scan must be FENCE-AWARE (a `### heading` inside a ```comment block will otherwise terminate the scan mid-fence and corrupt the fence), and a marker predicate must match markers that sit AFTER a list bullet (`9. <!-- bkit:... -->`), not just at line start - missing that leaves the item loose and prettier re-adds everything. Applied 2026-07-15: indented blank-adjacent markers 124 -> 42, 143 blank lines removed, 6 escaped two-digit steps in `bkit-build.md` re-indented 3 -> 4; content verified identical (every text / inline-code / fenced-block / marker value, in document order) across all 8 files; 1 blank deliberately kept in `bkit-design.md` where removal merged a paragraph into a nested list.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** medium
- **Scope:** bkit-repo
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** `.bkit/workflows/*.md` (source of the `.claude`/`.cursor`/`.opencode` command mirrors); `.prettierignore` managed block; render-side blank-collapse fix still OPEN (the 158 top-level markers + the CAUTION split).

summary: A prune gated on identity destroys rows the dedup fold dropped — friction keys truncate to ~68 chars and collide, so two distinct entries share one identity and only one is ever stored
description: Found while making bkit harvest MOVE consumer friction (#343). fold() is last-write-wins per identity(), so colliding rows collapse to ONE stored row. An identity-gated prune then deletes EVERY colliding row from the consumer while the store kept one — the loser exists nowhere. Reproduced against live consumer-a data: 'Plan Step 11: close-workflow STRAY guard rejects protocol-mandated docs/pending.md edit' (ts 1783944967776) and a different entry about docs/decisions.md + docs/pending.md edits truncate to the byte-identical key 'friction-plan-step-11-close-workflow-stray-guard-rejects-protocol-ma'; the first was destroyed. Harmless under the old copy-only harvest, fatal the moment harvest deletes. Second instance of the same shape: identity() has no default branch, so rows whose kind is outside VALID_KINDS all collide on undefined — live data has kind:'tool-failure' and kind:'agent-rework' rows in consumer-a friction, and the newer evicted the older from the store.
rootCause: identity() is a lossy projection of a row (kind+repo+key, or ts when key is absent), and fold() treats an identity match as an upsert. Anything gating a DELETE on that projection deletes rows the projection cannot distinguish. Two independent sources of collision: (1) friction keys are truncated at write time, so distinct content yields identical keys; (2) identity() returns undefined for kinds outside VALID_KINDS, mapping every unknown-kind row onto a single fold slot.
remediation: Gate any destructive drain on byte-for-byte row CONTENT read back off disk, never on identity — a row the fold dropped is then retained at source and reported (bkit-harvest RETAINED log line). Fix the lossy key truncation upstream, and give identity() a total mapping for unknown kinds. General rule: an identity used for dedup/upsert is NOT safe as a delete gate.

summary: Rows migrated from the legacy friction.md carry transport values on some axes — severity is a documented unknown->neutral placeholder, step is the transport on 76 rows, and recurrence is structurally uncountable
rootCause: mapLegacySeverity defaults every row to MEDIUM because friction.md never had a Severity field (an explicit unknown->neutral mapping, NOT a claim about the row). The pre-fix migrator also stamped step with the transport (bkit-telemetry-migrate) and ts with a synthetic baseTs+idx. Recurrence fragments because a recurrence is titled differently, so stableKey mints a NEW key and it folds to a SEPARATE entity — an entity count counts REPORTS, not OCCURRENCES.
remediation: ts is fixed: parseTitleDate reads the legacy heading date and the row builder prefers it over baseTs+idx; harvest/friction.jsonl was backfilled on 183 of 257 rows (span 2026-05-24..2026-07-15). severity is NOT repairable and NOT a defect — re-triage on next touch, never read P0/P1 out of it. step remains the transport on 76 rows (only ~25 carry a recoverable hint) — low value. Frequency needs a schema change, not a data repair. Do NOT infer cluster size from row counts: 101 of 156 entities are two rows that differ only in references/ts/status — a create plus a triage stamp, not a second occurrence.

summary: `pnpm test` at default vitest thread concurrency intermittently times out heavy integration suites (bkit-slop-type-suppression, bkit-check-opencode, bkit-upgrade) on resource-constrained machines; not a code regression
rootCause: vitest defaults to CPU-count worker threads; several *.integration.test.ts files spawn real subprocesses (tsx, git, jq) with a 5s per-test timeout. Under full-suite parallel load on a constrained machine, those subprocess spawns intermittently exceed 5s and time out — the failures are non-deterministic and clear when concurrency is reduced.
remediation: Before treating a `pnpm test` failure in one of these integration files as a real regression, re-run just that file in isolation (`npx vitest run <file>`) or the full suite with `--maxWorkers=2`; if it passes there, it is this flake, not a defect in the change under review. Not fixed at the infra level here (no vitest pool/timeout config change) — that is a shared-infra decision out of scope for a single gap-remediation task.

summary: OpenCode Go premium models (kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus) are invisible to the /zen/v1/models REST probe — Zen and Go are two separate models.dev providers with different endpoints; models.dev is the source of truth
description:
- **Category:** provider-integration / model-curation
- **Symptom:** curating bkit's opencode model column against `curl https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` reported Kimi K3 as 'not live on OpenCode Go' when the opencode app's model selector clearly listed 'Kimi K3 (2x usage)' under OpenCode Go. Adding auth (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`) to the same endpoint did NOT change the result (55 ids, no kimi-k3). A chat round-trip to `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions` with model `kimi-k3` returned `ModelError: Model kimi-k3 is not supported`.
- **Root cause:** OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go are TWO DISTINCT providers on models.dev — `opencode` (name 'OpenCode Zen', api `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`) and `opencode-go` (name 'OpenCode Go', api `https://opencode.ai/zen/**go**/v1`, nested under /zen/). The `/zen/v1/models` REST endpoint returns ONLY the Zen catalog; Go-only premium models (`kimi-k3`, `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.7-max`) never appear there regardless of auth. The opencode app populates its model selector from models.dev, not from that REST endpoint — which is why the app showed K3 but the probe did not.
- **Fix or rule:** Curate opencode model pins from `https://models.dev/api.json` (read providers `.opencode` and `.["opencode-go"]` `.models`), NEVER from `/zen/v1/models` alone. Tool-call-smoke Go pins against the Go endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` (bare model id, e.g. `kimi-k3`) — verified kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash all emit `tool_calls` there. bkit now ships two providers `opencode-zen` + `opencode-go` (both `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` npm-driver blocks with explicit baseURLs; one `OPENCODE_API_KEY` covers both); the legacy bare `opencode` provider alias-normalises to `opencode-zen`.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** medium
- **Scope:** bkit-repo
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** `.bkit/providers.md` § Models (Per-provider live model lookup recipe); `.bkit/prompts.md` § Models Live model-ID verification.
rootCause: OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go are two distinct models.dev providers (`opencode` at https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 and `opencode-go` at https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1). The /zen/v1/models REST endpoint returns only the Zen catalog, so Go-only premium models (kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.7-max) are invisible to it regardless of auth. The opencode app reads its catalog from models.dev, not that endpoint.
remediation: Curate opencode pins from https://models.dev/api.json (providers .opencode and .['opencode-go']), never from /zen/v1/models alone. Smoke Go pins against https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions. bkit ships two providers opencode-zen + opencode-go; legacy bare `opencode` normalises to opencode-zen.

summary: bkit-runtime.sh's sourced state (RUNTIME, CAN_*, GH_OK, CI_WAIT_*) lives only in the current process — it does NOT survive an orchestrator Bash-tool-call boundary; re-source and re-call per block
description: Each fenced ```bash block in a workflow file runs as a fresh subprocess when invoked by the orchestrator's Bash tool. `bkit_runtime_detect`/`bkit_wait_ci` set plain shell variables (RUNTIME, CAN_WORKTREE, CAN_PUSH_DEV, CAN_SLEEP, GH_OK, WORKTREE_PATH, CI_WAIT_RESULT, CI_WAIT_ATTEMPTS, CI_WAIT_ELAPSED, CI_WAIT_ALL_ERRORED) — none of these survive into a LATER Bash block, even within the same workflow run. A call site that assumes a flag set two steps earlier is still readable will silently see an empty/unset value.
rootCause: Bash-tool-call isolation: the orchestrator invokes each fenced code block as an independent subprocess, not a persistent shell session. Sourcing (`. path/to/script.sh`) only affects the CURRENT subprocess's environment.
remediation: Source `.bkit/scripts/bkit-runtime.sh` and re-call `bkit_runtime_detect`/`bkit_wait_ci` at the start of EVERY block that needs the table or a poll result — do not assume state from an earlier block. The durable, cross-block record is the `runtime-resolved` row (`bkit_runtime_row`) appended to `status.jsonl` — later steps read `GH_OK` etc. back from that row instead of re-probing. `bkit_runtime_assert_resolved` (Flow 1) makes an accidentally-unset flag loud (distinct message) rather than silently defaulting.

summary: [skip ci] can suppress CI on dev by riding in the squash-merge BODY (concatenated intermediate commit subjects), not just the PR title — a title-only assertion misses it
description: Incident: a ship of #703 squash-merged 16 commits into one PR; one intermediate commit subject was `chore(690-header-nav-shell): worktree-setup bkit [skip ci]`. GitHub Actions scans the merge commit's subject AND body for suppression tokens. `gh pr merge --squash` without an explicit `--body ""` defaults to a body that concatenates every commit's subject line, so the token leaked into the merge body even though the PR TITLE carried none. The workflow's only mechanised check at the time was a PR-title grep (never scans the resulting merge body); the backstop was an after-the-fact `gh run list` check, not a preventive assertion.
rootCause: gh's `--squash` default body behaviour (concatenate commit subjects) plus a title-only skip-token assertion that never re-scans the body it actually produces.
remediation: Merge/commit bodies that land work MUST be skip-token-free on every transport (`.agents/rules.md` § Git, CI & Merges — shared invariant, not owned by one call site). `gh pr merge` calls that land onto a CI-gated branch pass an explicit skip-token-free `--body ""` (verified present at `bkit-ship.md` merge call). MCP `merge_pull_request` fallbacks MUST pass an equivalent explicit `commit_message`, never rely on the tool's own default. A title-only pre-merge assertion is NOT sufficient by itself — treat it as one layer, not the guarantee.

summary: git branch names may legally contain shell metacharacters ('$();&) per git check-ref-format; interpolating a captured branch name into a double-quoted/eval'd trap body is command injection at EXIT
rootCause: bkit_close_guard_checkout built its EXIT trap with trap "git checkout '$VAR' ..." EXIT (SC2064-disabled expand-now form) so the captured branch name was re-parsed as shell text when the trap fired -- a branch containing an embedded $(...) payload would execute at process exit.
remediation: Single-quote trap bodies so referenced variables resolve at FIRE time, never at install time: trap 'git checkout "$VAR" ...' EXIT. Applies to any trap/eval that embeds externally-influenced data (branch names, PR titles, etc.) -- never interpolate into a shell-interpreted string (docs/security.md section Shell Injection).

summary: GitHub Actions honours 5 CI-suppression tokens ([skip ci], [ci skip], [no ci], [skip actions], [actions skip], case-insensitive) -- a post-close scan checking only 2 of them is a silent D1-class regression
rootCause: bkit_close_guard_scan_body originally grepped only [skip ci]|[skip actions] (case-sensitive), narrower than the advisory pre-checks elsewhere in the same workflows that already covered all 5 tokens case-insensitively -- the authoritative post-close guard was inconsistent with its own pre-checks.
remediation: Any body/title scan for CI-suppression tokens MUST match the full case-insensitive set: grep -qiE with [skip ci]|[ci skip]|[no ci]|[skip actions]|[actions skip]. Keep every scan site (advisory pre-check + authoritative post-close) on the identical pattern to avoid drift.

summary: GNU coreutils timeout(1) is absent on stock macOS/BSD userlands; a shim that hard-depends on it must resolve the binary once and fall back to a plain sleep, never treat exit 127 as a blocked-sleep condition
rootCause: bkit_wait_ci wrapped every poll sleep in timeout N sleep M unconditionally. On a Mac without homebrew coreutils, timeout is not on PATH, so the wrapper itself fails (exit 127) and was misread as a genuinely blocked/foreground-sleep-restricted runtime (D22 abort) rather than a missing binary.
remediation: Resolve `command -v timeout || command -v gtimeout` once per call, and only wrap sleep with it when found; fall back to a plain unwrapped sleep otherwise. Only classify as a blocked-sleep abort when a real timeout wrapper actually times out.

summary: Any FID resolved from a PR-body marker (bkit-auto D9 marker-primary) must pass a strict slug allowlist before it builds a filesystem path or dispatches downstream
rootCause: PR body is collaborator-trusted, not commit-signed (docs/security.md CI Auto-Route Trust); marker-derived {FID} flows into docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/ and .worktrees/{FID}, so bkit:fid=../../elsewhere redirects writes when unvalidated.
remediation: Assert the canonical per-tracker slug (^[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ github / ^[a-z]+-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ linear / ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ no-tracker+branch-derive) at the resolution site; marker failure falls through to branch-derive, branch-derive failure is a Failure Path. Same guard the five phase workflows apply at FID mint.

summary: Source-to-rendered-mirror diff is non-empty by construction; authoritative drift check is bkit check, not a raw diff
description: A raw `diff .bkit/workflows/<file>.md .claude/commands/<file>.md` is NON-empty because the source carries `<!-- bkit:tracker {github,linear,true} start/end -->` template markers for ALL trackers, which `bkit install` resolves to the configured tracker and strips during render (e.g. 1288-line source -> ~1100-line rendered mirror). The authoritative mirror-drift check is `bkit check` reporting no `bkit-rendered-prompts-stale` advisory AND `bkit install` reporting 0 writes (idempotent render). "Byte-identical" applies ONLY to (a) script root<->template pairs (.bkit/scripts/ <-> .bkit/templates/.bkit/scripts/) and (b) the templates-content snapshot enforcing rendered<->rendered idempotency — NEVER to source<->mirror.
rootCause: tracker template resolution is fundamental to bkit mirror rendering; a Done-when or gate claim that a source<->mirror `diff` is empty is never literally satisfiable.
remediation: Word any mirror-drift Done-when / gate checkbox as: `bkit check` reports no `bkit-rendered-prompts-stale` AND `bkit install` reports 0 writes. Do NOT assert source<->mirror byte-identity.

summary: #384 Tier-3 status-hole detector derives its expected ship-* step set by parsing bkit-ship.md (headings + step:"ship-*" literals), NEVER a hand-maintained parallel table — a table is the second source of truth Finding 7 is exactly that drift signature
rootCause: A hand-maintained expected-step table drifts from bkit-ship.md whenever a step is renamed, added, or reordered. Finding 7 of #384 is agents inventing step names precisely because there was no canonical set; a parallel table reintroduces the same drift surface (the cheapest fix under a table — edit the table to match observed reality — is also the wrong one, papering over a workflow bug as expected behaviour).
remediation: Parse the source: extract `## ... Step N — Name` headings AND the `step:"ship-*"` literals inside fenced status-write blocks. The two sets must agree (the Tier-2 invariant freezes them via CANONICAL_SHIP_STEP_KEYS). Path-conditional sets (Path A skips integrate+re-validate; MERGED-on-entry resume; aborted-at-Failure-Path) are derived from the SAME source by inspecting which steps are path-gated, never re-declared. Renaming a step resets attempt counters across consumer repos and orphans the detector corpus — the frozen set is published in bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts as the single source of truth the detector MUST match.

summary: Running multiple bats files in one `bats tests/a.bats tests/b.bats ...` invocation intermittently fails with `Failed to create BATS_TEST_TMPDIR1: ... File exists` on macOS — run each file in its own invocation, not as a single multi-file arg
rootCause: bats reuses BATS_RUN_TMPDIR across files in a multi-file invocation and the per-test TMPDIR1 numbering collides when test indices overlap across files (the mktemp mkdir hits an already-existing dir). On stock macOS this surfaces as a `mkdir: ... File exists / Failed to create BATS_TEST_TMPDIR1` storm and a final `Executed N instead of expected M tests`, exiting non-zero even though every individual test passed when the file ran alone.
remediation: Invoke one bats file per call (e.g. `bats tests/ship-gate.bats`, then `bats tests/ship-failure-path.bats`) for the seam-verification prelude and any per-file gate check. `pnpm test:bats tests/*.bats` (the glob form) is fine in CI on Linux; the collision is macOS-local. This is a test-harness portability quirk, not a regression in the script under test — confirm by re-running the single failing file in isolation.

summary: Doc content added inside a bkit managed block must also be added to the template source or bkit check reports drift plus a cascading .bkit/version pin write
description: When a build task adds new prose to a root docs file (e.g. docs/deployments.md) INSIDE the <!-- bkit:start --> ... <!-- bkit:end --> managed block, the corresponding .bkit/templates/docs/<file>.md template must receive the same content (with token substitution where needed). If only the root is updated, bkit check reports N write(s) of drift because its core templates pass renders the template and compares the managed block byte-for-byte. A secondary .bkit/version write cascades from this: postDispatch records canonical hashes from ws.writes, and any write populates newCanonicalEntries -> needsWrite=true. Content added OUTSIDE the managed block (bkit dogfood documentation) does NOT require template sync — the template intentionally ships only the managed block, and bkit upgrade (Tier-2) only replaces content between markers. This asymmetry is by design: the root doc can carry bkit-specific dogfood content that is never shipped to consumers.
rootCause: bkit check core templates pass renders the template with token substitution and compares the managed block to the root doc; any content inside the bkit:start/bkit:end markers that exists in the root but not the template is flagged as drift. The .bkit/version pin write cascades from any core-template drift because postDispatch populates canonical hashes from ws.writes entries.
remediation: Mirror any managed-block doc addition into .bkit/templates/docs/<file>.md (applying token substitution for main->{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}, cbartens/bkit->{{REPO_SLUG}} where present). Run pnpm bkit check to verify 0 writes before committing. Verify with pnpm bkit check -> expect 0 write(s). If the content is outside the managed block (dogfood), NO template change is needed.

summary: Documented fail-open empty catches must stay empty; adding console.error to improve them triggers defensive.error-swallowing and turns a GREEN slop:delta RED
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** pnpm slop:delta RED with 4 net-new defensive.error-swallowing findings (net score +4.80) in bkit-modules.ts:2724/:3216 and guardrails.cjs:128 (root + template).
- **Root cause:** A verify step improved three documented fail-open empty catches by replacing the empty-catch-with-comment shape with a console.error log-and-continue, believing logging was safer than silence. But slop-scan.config.json already disables defensive.empty-catch for these exact files (overrides lines 173-193) with written _reason fields stating the empty catch is the implementation of the fail-open contract and each is paired with an advisory emission path. The console.error-and-continue shape is exactly what defensive.error-swallowing flags (catch logs only), so the improvement introduced the only rule NOT overridden for these files.
- **Fix or rule:** When a catch is covered by a defensive.empty-catch config override with a written reason, keep it as an empty catch with a comment; do NOT add console.error. If diagnostics are genuinely needed, surface via the file existing advisory channel (advisories.push) that is not logs-only and matches the documented advisory emission path. Never rethrow inside a fail-open hook (e.g. Cursor PreToolUse) where aborting crashes the editor session; the shipped fallback is correct behaviour, not a swallowed bug.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high (git blame confirmed the regression: commit bac21726 had empty catches; 3c50f02b changed them to console.error; reverting cleared all 4 findings, score 36.40 to 31.60)
- **Severity:** normal (turns a GREEN gate RED with no functional benefit; blocks ship)
- **Source:** #384 build cycle
- **Related:** #384, slop-scan.config.json
rootCause: A verify step replaced documented fail-open empty catches (covered by a defensive.empty-catch config override with written reason) with a console.error log-and-continue, believing logging was safer than silence. But defensive.error-swallowing is the one rule NOT overridden for these files, and console.error-and-continue is exactly what it flags (catch logs only). The override reasons explicitly state empty catch is the fail-open contract.
remediation: Keep catches covered by a defensive.empty-catch override as empty catches with a comment. If diagnostics are needed, use the file existing advisory channel (advisories.push), not console.error that is not logs-only and matches the documented advisory emission path. Never rethrow inside fail-open hooks (Cursor PreToolUse) where aborting crashes the editor session.

summary: Any line in bkit-ship.md mentioning status.jsonl MUST also mention BOOK_ROOT (Tier-2 invariant); editing the workflow also requires syncing ALL FOUR mirrors
description:
- **Category:** testing
- **Symptom:** `pnpm test` fails in `bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts` with a violation from the "every status.jsonl write target carries BOOK_ROOT" assertion, pointing at a COMMENT line that mentions `status.jsonl` but not `BOOK_ROOT`.
- **Root cause:** the Tier-2 invariant test scans EVERY line of `.bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md` for the substring `status.jsonl` and requires `BOOK_ROOT` on the same line — comments included. A new comment like `# ... lands in the canonical status.jsonl ...` trips it. Separately, editing the source workflow requires updating ALL FOUR rendered mirrors (`.claude/commands/bkit-ship.md`, `.cursor/commands/bkit-ship.md`, `.opencode/commands/bkit-ship.md`) or `pnpm bkit check` drift-fails with `bkit-rendered-prompts-stale`.
- **Fix or rule:** when adding comments/lines to bkit-ship.md that mention `status.jsonl`, either include `BOOK_ROOT` on the same line OR reword to avoid the literal `status.jsonl` substring. After any source edit, apply the same change to all four mirror files (claude/cursor/opencode commands).
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** `.bkit/src/bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts`, #384
rootCause: the Tier-2 invariant test scans EVERY line of bkit-ship.md for the substring status.jsonl and requires BOOK_ROOT on the same line (comments included). A comment mentioning status.jsonl without BOOK_ROOT trips it. Separately, editing the source workflow requires updating all four rendered mirrors or bkit check drift-fails.
remediation: when adding comments/lines to bkit-ship.md that mention status.jsonl, include BOOK_ROOT on the same line OR reword to avoid the literal substring. After any source edit, apply the same change to all four mirror files (claude/cursor/opencode commands).

summary: lint:prose treated a gitignored, absent .vale/styles/write-good the same as an absent vale binary, so the pre-commit prose gate silently self-disabled in every worktree and fresh checkout
description:
- **Category:** tooling
- **Symptom:** commits made from a git worktree passed pre-commit, then the SAME content failed prose linting the moment it was committed from the main clone. A write-good error rode along in three worktree commits undetected.
- **Root cause:** `lint:prose` gated on `command -v vale && [ -d .vale/styles/write-good ]` and, on failure, echoed one quiet line and exited 0. `.vale/styles/write-good` is gitignored (`vale sync` downloads it), so it is absent in every fresh checkout AND every `git worktree add` — `.vale/styles/House` IS tracked, so the parent dir exists and nothing looks wrong. The guard conflated two conditions: an absent vale binary (unrecoverable, skip is correct) and unsynced styles (fully recoverable). bkit's own five workflows already copied write-good into `.worktrees/{FID}` at worktree-setup, which hid the hole for bkit-created worktrees; harness worktrees (`.claude/worktrees/*`), manual `git worktree add`, and plain clones had no such cover.
- **Fix or rule:** a gate whose enabling data is gitignored must self-heal or fail loudly, never skip quietly. lint:prose now copies write-good from the main worktree (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, zero network), falls back to `vale sync`, and warns on stderr if vale is present but neither worked. Skip stays silent ONLY when the vale binary itself is missing.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** BAR-138 (F9 guard), `.bkit/src/bkit-package-json.ts`
rootCause: lint:prose treated absent gitignored .vale/styles/write-good identically to an absent vale binary and soft-skipped with exit 0. The styles dir is missing in every fresh checkout and worktree, so the pre-commit prose gate reported success while enforcing nothing.
remediation: self-heal the recoverable case (copy write-good from the main worktree via git rev-parse --git-common-dir, then vale sync as fallback) and warn LOUDLY on stderr when vale is present but self-heal failed. Reserve the silent skip for a genuinely absent vale binary. Generally: a gate whose enabling data is gitignored must self-heal or fail loudly.

summary: A bash-syntax variable reference (${LABELS:-}) written in a *.bkit/workflows/*.md prompt is NOT auto-populated by an earlier MCP call in the same numbered step tree unless the SAME Bash tool-call sets it — an intervening tool-call boundary (MCP read, or an earlier numbered step) resets the shell
rootCause: *.bkit/workflows/*.md files are natural-language instructions executed by an LLM agent turn-by-turn; each fenced bash block the agent runs is typically its own subprocess/tool-call with no persisted state from a prior tool-call. Writing `echo "${LABELS:-}"` in a bash fence several steps after a `LABELS` value was extracted via an MCP call (a separate tool-call) silently expands to empty every time, because the variable was never assigned IN that shell invocation.
remediation: Two idioms fix it, matching bkit-build.md/bkit-debug.md precedent: (1) re-derive the value in the SAME bash fence it is used (e.g. gh CLI call), or (2) materialise it into a mktemp handoff file immediately adjacent to the original read (same numbered step) and pass the file path forward via GITHUB_ENV / an explicit variable, then read-and-fallback at the point of use (`if [ -f "$HANDOFF_FILE" ]; then ...; else <same-block re-derive>; fi`). Never write bare `${VAR:-}` in a bash fence and assume an earlier step (even a few lines above) populated it — verify the SAME fenced bash block both sets and uses it, or that a handoff file/GITHUB_ENV var carries it forward.

summary: A guard test that asserts a doc CONTAINS an internal label makes the citation mandatory and blocks the doctrine that removes it
description: bkit-ci-dispatch-gate-alignment.test.ts asserted workflows.md must contain the literal KN-11 as proof the non-push doctrine was documented. Removing internal identifiers from shipped docs turned that green assertion red, and the only ways to satisfy both were to keep the label or to weaken the doctrine.
rootCause: the test asserted the CITATION rather than the MECHANISM it points at. A label is a stable string and therefore an easy assertion target, which is exactly why it silently becomes a requirement.
remediation: assert the described behaviour, not its record: the rule now matches /\[skip ci\][^.]*empt(y|ies)[^.]*rollup/i. When a doc-content test must anchor on text, anchor on words that state the rule — a doc passes only by still explaining itself.

summary: The no-dead-MAX_* audit counted references inside comments, so a cap enforced nowhere in the scanned corpus passed on a rationale comment alone
description: MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS is enforced in .github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml, outside the .bkit/workflows/*.md corpus the audit scans. The corpus contained the name only in a bkit-ship.md rationale comment; deleting that comment (workflow files carry no rationale) turned the rule red on a cap that was never dead.
rootCause: the audit matched the constant anywhere inside a fenced block, comments included, so a comment mentioning a constant read as enforcement.
remediation: count executable lines only (drop /^\s*#/) and include the real enforcement surfaces (bkit-cloud.yml + its template) in the scanned set. A constant named solely in a comment can no longer satisfy the rule.

summary: bkit-upgrade.ts sniffs a template for its marker style with its own detectMarkerStyle, separate from bkit-install.ts — adding a marker style to only the install engine leaves upgrade silently unable to manage files using it
rootCause: bkit-upgrade.ts detects a TEMPLATE managed-block marker style independently of bkit-install.ts (it cannot import the install-time detector, which operates on already-known style names, not raw content). Adding a new marker style constant to bkit-install.ts alone leaves bkit-upgrade.ts returning null for that style, which falls back to html-comment, finds no html markers in the template, and writeTier2 returns early with no write and no warning.
remediation: when adding a marker style, update BOTH detectMarkerStyle implementations (bkit-install.ts is style-name-based; bkit-upgrade.ts is template-content-based) in the same change, and add a regression test that installs, tampers a probe INSIDE the managed block, then upgrades and asserts the probe is gone — a silent no-op would let it survive.

summary: Slash-command argument substitution rewrites $0 inside workflow bash before the model reads it, turning awk programs into syntax errors that fail silently
description: Invoking /bkit-plan with an issue argument replaced every literal $0 in the rendered command body with that argument. The file on disk was correct; the corruption is host-side argument expansion, where $N is documented shorthand for $ARGUMENTS[N], zero-based. The clobbered ledger scan in bkit-plan.md wrote None. to related-deferrals.md while docs/deferrals.jsonl held 16 matching rows.
rootCause: awk field references and the host placeholder syntax share the $-digit token, and the call site M=$(awk ...) discards awk's exit status, so the dead program produced an empty capture that read as no matches. $1 to $9 carried the same latent hazard: an index with no matching argument is left unchanged, so awk '{print $2}' survived one-argument invocations and would break on three.
remediation: Rewrite every awk field reference in .bkit/workflows/*.md as $(N) — POSIX, identical behaviour, no $-digit sequence for any host to rewrite. The host's backslash escape was rejected: it is Claude-Code-specific and would render verbatim into .cursor/commands/ and .opencode/commands/. Gated by bkit-slash-arg-expansion.test.ts, which bans $0-$9 and $ARGUMENTS across the workflow corpus. Scope excludes .bkit/scripts/*.sh and .github/workflows/*.yml, which execute as files and whose $1 is a real positional parameter with no $(N) equivalent.

summary: mcp__github__issue_read sanitises issue and comment bodies before returning them, deleting every HTML comment — so every <!-- bkit:* --> marker is invisible to any workflow step that reads through it
description: GitHub stores the marker correctly and writes are unaffected; the loss is read-side only. Confirmed by reading one comment both ways: gh api returns the generated marker as the first body line, mcp__github__issue_read returns the same comment starting at its first heading. Angle-bracket spans are eaten the same way (a Failures: <integer >= 0> example returned as `Failures: = 0>`) and quotes come back HTML-escaped. Backticks are not an escape hatch — the sanitiser runs on the raw markdown, so a code-spanned marker returns as empty backticks. Three shipped mechanisms depended on it: the bkit:generated comment filter, the bkit:ignore-earlier context cut, and the bkit:blocked-by dependency gate; none of them could ever fire on the GitHub tracker path, and the design blocked-by encode read a body through the MCP and wrote it back, destroying whatever the read had dropped.
rootCause: Marker detection is deliberately marker-only with no shape fallback, so the whole mechanism rests on the marker surviving the read — but no test covered the read. The existing guard asserts that every workflow step names the filters at its point of use, which stays green over input that can never contain a marker. Nothing failed loudly: a run still produced a plausible-looking trimmed artifact.
remediation: GitHub issue body and comment TEXT read with raw gh api at every point of use (issue path and related-issues sweep, including the sweep search hit body, which is sanitised too); mcp__github__issue_read retained for structured fields only (state, labels, milestone). Rule recorded in .agents/rules.md as Tracker text reads. Guard added to bkit-generated-marker.test.ts: no method: "get_comments" anywhere in the workflows, and no surviving issue_read call extracts body. Verification for this class must be a live read-back through the actual tool, never another assertion about workflow text.

summary: Workflow bookkeeping staging built its pathspec with shell word-splitting and an ls glob that aborts under zsh, silently dropping ledgers and swallowing a failed git add into a false success
description: The host shell for .bkit/workflows/*.md fenced bash blocks is not guaranteed to be bash -- confirmed zsh (5.9) on stock macOS Claude Code, $0=/bin/zsh, BASH_VERSION unset. BOOK_PATHS was built with unquoted $BOOK_PATHS interpolation (word-splits differently per shell) and an `ls docs/plans/*/logs/*/*.jsonl docs/*.jsonl .bkit/*.jsonl` sweep whose glob ABORTS under zsh when a component matches nothing, dropping the whole sweep silently in a fresh consumer repo (bash just passes the unmatched literal pattern through). Nothing in these blocks sets `set -e`, so a failed `git add` (exit 128, e.g. a locked index) fell through the subsequent `git diff --cached --quiet` check into `no bookkeeping delta to record -- nothing committed, nothing pushed`: a loud failure disguised as a legitimate no-op.
rootCause: Two independent host-shell dependencies stacked: (1) unquoted variable interpolation for the pathspec, word-split differently per shell and unsafe with paths containing spaces; (2) an `ls a/*/b` glob sweep, which bash passes through unmatched but zsh aborts. Neither failure path was distinguishable from success because the workflow blocks never check `git add`'s own exit code before concluding there was nothing to commit.
remediation: Bookkeeping stage/commit now routes through bkit-book-commit.sh (.bkit/scripts/, invoked with an explicit `bash` prefix so host shell never matters). It builds the pathspec with `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` against quoted globs (git does the matching, so an unmatched glob is empty output, never an abort) and stages/commits via `--pathspec-from-file --pathspec-file-nul` instead of a re-interpolated string. `git add` failures are checked explicitly and exit non-zero (never swallowed), and an empty pathspec list refuses to reach `commit` (exit 6) -- `git commit --pathspec-from-file=<empty file>` does not commit nothing, it silently commits whatever is already staged in the index, which is a worse trap than the original bug. General rule recorded in .agents/rules.md: workflow bash blocks must not rely on shell word-splitting or unmatched-glob passthrough; anything needing bash-only features goes in .bkit/scripts/*.sh.

summary: Roadmap cadence must count since the last ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE row, never since the last analysis refresh -- a refresh-anchored counter resets every ship and never fires
description: The analysis block (roadmap-analysis marker) refreshes at EVERY ship close. If the cadence threshold were measured from the last refresh instead of a dedicated fire counter row, the count would reset to zero on every ship and the audit/ledger injection would never cross threshold. Anchor on a separate ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE counter row (rebaselined only when it actually fires) instead.
rootCause: Conflating the per-ship analysis-refresh event with the rarer cadence-fire event when choosing a counter anchor.
remediation: Count distinct BUILT-status FIDs in docs/roadmap.jsonl since the last ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE row (not since the last analysis refresh); rebaseline only on fire.

summary: bkit telemetry migrate is deliberately NOT auto-run at bkit upgrade (DE-39); an unmigrated or empty docs/roadmap.jsonl yields an EMPTY board, not a wrong one, with a fold hint naming the command
description: There is no legacy docs/completed.md grep fallback in the fold -- the reader is deleted with the file at migration time. Before a consumer runs bkit telemetry migrate, docs/roadmap.md shows no shipped history (correctly empty, not silently wrong); an install advisory plus the fold's own hint are the only rollout signal, since the migrator cannot be wired to bkit upgrade.
rootCause: DE-39 forbids wiring any md-to-jsonl migrator to bkit upgrade (explicit-invocation-only, mechanically enforced).
remediation: Treat an empty active-phase board on a freshly-upgraded consumer as expected pre-migration state; run bkit telemetry migrate once to backfill and bootstrap-seed in-flight FIDs.

summary: Tracker enrichment for the roadmap board uses list_issues, never search_issues -- an empty or zero result from search_issues on a private repo is inconclusive, not proof of zero issues
description: mcp github search_issues has a known failure mode of silently returning total_count 0 for every query on some private repos, including a bare control query (github-mcp-search-issues-silently-returns-zero-private-repo, still OPEN). The roadmap fold's tracker enrichment therefore uses the bounded list_issues read exclusively; a failed or empty list_issues read still falls back to the on-disk board (never blank, never gates).
rootCause: search_issues total_count 0 on a private repo can mean either truly zero matches or search unavailable; there is no way to disambiguate from the response alone.
remediation: Never use search_issues for roadmap tracker enrichment; use list_issues (bounded, best-effort, additive only when a tracker is wired).

summary: build/debug roadmap close-hooks are a FOURTH distinct staging shape (dev-lock ledger append) beyond design/plan's dev-or-PR commit and ship's BOOK_PATHS commit -- per-shape assertion is mandatory, a single grep would miss it
description: design/plan close-hooks commit docs/roadmap.md and docs/roadmap.jsonl via a normal dev or PR-branch commit (widened STRAY allowlist). ship closes stage the same paths through the frozen BOOK_PATHS allow-list. build/debug closes commit to feat/{FID} via the existing git add -A AND separately append the same merge=union ledger line to dev under the ship dev-lock idiom (design Addendum C) -- a fourth, structurally different staging path. bkit-roadmap-staging.integration.test.ts and bkit-roadmap-devwrite.integration.test.ts assert each shape independently.
rootCause: Four workflows commit the roadmap artifacts through three structurally different git operations (dev-or-PR commit, BOOK_PATHS commit, git add -A plus dev-lock append); asserting only one shape leaves the other three unverified.
remediation: When touching any close-hook staging logic, assert all four shapes independently (design/plan dev+PR STRAY widen, build/debug git add -A + dev-lock append, ship BOOK_PATHS) -- never assume one grep pattern covers all four.

summary: A full-regenerate projection over an append-only merge=union ledger sidesteps the KN-42 duplicate-collapse invariant class entirely -- there is no dedupe invariant to maintain
description: KN-42 (kn-42-pre-release-main-dev-backmerge-with-x-ours-duplicate) documents a duplicate-line hazard from -X ours merges against an upserted file. Because docs/roadmap.md is now a full regenerate from docs/roadmap.jsonl on every fold (never an upserted target), a duplicate ledger line (e.g. from a re-run or a merge artifact) simply folds to its last-wins value during the regenerate -- there is no board-side dedupe invariant to write or maintain, because the board is never the thing merged.
rootCause: Upserting a target file directly (rather than projecting it from an append-only source) makes every merge or conflict path a potential duplicate-line hazard requiring its own dedupe invariant.
remediation: Prefer full-regenerate-from-ledger over direct-upsert for any future generated-board artifact that can be concurrently written; it removes an entire class of merge-duplicate bugs by construction.

summary: A settled DEBUGGED-status FID is permanently outside reverse tracker-label sync's reach -- deliberate trade-off, not a gap
description: The reverse-sync status-to-label map (DESIGNED->bkit:design, PLANNED->bkit:plan, BUILT->bkit:build, SHIPPED->bkit:merged) has no entry for DEBUGGED. bkit:debug is an ADDITIVE label layered on top of whatever phase label is already there (per the debug workflow's own header contract), never a replacement -- mapping DEBUGGED to bkit:debug in this REPLACE-one-phase-label sync would collapse an existing {bkit:build, bkit:debug} pair down to just {bkit:debug}, destroying the real phase label. So a settled DEBUGGED FID is simply skipped as unmapped (same path as ABANDONED), forever, by construction: the next ledger append for that FID (BUILT again, or SHIPPED) is what actually advances its label, not a future reverse-sync pass. This is accepted, not a bug: the existing phase label plus additive bkit:debug are already correct on the tracker; reverse-sync has nothing to fix.
rootCause: Reverse-sync replaces exactly one phase label per pass; DEBUGGED status maps to an additive, not phase-replacing, label, so no replacement mapping can exist for it without destroying the additive label's independence from the phase label.
remediation: Do not add a DEBUGGED entry to the reverse-sync status-to-label map. If a settled-DEBUGGED FID's tracker labels are ever found to be wrong, fix it at the debug workflow's own label-write step (Step 10 idiom), not in reverse-sync.

summary: Ship Step 5 fired a second, duplicate CI run on every head move because it dispatched unconditionally instead of probing first
description: Every ship that took Path B (rebase / gh pr update-branch) produced TWO completed CI runs on the SAME commit, seconds apart: one from the pull_request event the push itself fired, one from ship's own gh workflow run. Observed five times on feat/380-roadmap-analysis-refresh -- e.g. head 1b51b989 ran pull_request at 21:07:21 (run 33013836266) and workflow_dispatch at 21:07:52 (run 33013876939); same shape at ea6f17f7 (5s apart), ea37e5c8 (3s), bb981805 (3s), 11a74fd4 (9s). Doubled CI minutes and wall-clock on every rebase-integrating ship.
rootCause: bkit-ship.md Step 5 re-validate carried the comment 'Head moved -- dispatch CI unconditionally' and called gh workflow run ci.yml with no check for a run already at that head, so the pull_request run the force-push had just triggered was ignored. The CI-Dispatch Gate that fixed exactly this class for build and debug (bounded bkit_wait_ci presence poll, dispatch only on none) was never extended to ship -- ship was recorded as OUT of scope on the grounds that a dispatch-outcome verdict would mask 'essential tests skipped', which is a valid objection to the gate's pass semantics but not to its probe. ci.yml concurrency could not absorb the duplicate either: pull_request runs group by head_ref while workflow_dispatch runs group by run_id, so the two land in different groups and neither cancels the other.
remediation: Ship Step 5 now calls bkit_wait_ci (60s/10s, presence-only) before dispatching and skips gh workflow run when a run already exists at the head; probe err (incl. blocked sleep) still dispatches, preserving the pre-fix safety property. The probe is never a pass condition -- the completion poll and bkit-ship-gate.sh assert at Gate 6 still own the verdict. The completion poll was made head-anchored (select(.headSha == $h)) at the same time, because without a guaranteed-fresh dispatch an unfiltered gh run list --limit 1 can return a completed run from a superseded head.

summary: Any agent output that merely names the ignore-earlier token ships a live cut marker; the next run's cut fires on bkit's own text and silently deletes the human context above it
description: Near-miss on a consumer repo: a Step 2 Worktree Setup comment explained which comments it had kept and named the token in backticked prose while doing so. That comment carried the bkit:generated stamp, so the comment filter removed it before the cut ran and no context was lost. Nothing about that outcome is structural. The generated filter drops COMMENTS only: it never touches an issue body (which the design blocked-by encode rewrites in place), and the sweep accumulator RELATED_ISSUES is by design never filtered and never cut. A marker written into either path is a live cut. The cut is also performed by an agent reading prose, not by a regex, so the bare token without its HTML-comment wrapper is not reliably inert.
rootCause: The marker was documented as human-placed but never prohibited as agent output, and the prohibition had no guard. Workflow comment templates carry free-text lines where an orchestrator naturally narrates what it filtered, which is exactly the sentence that reproduces the token. Failure is silent in both directions: the cut produces a plausibly-trimmed artifact, and the run that wrote the marker looks entirely normal.
remediation: Prohibition recorded in .agents/rules.md (and the shipped template) as Never self-cut: never emit the token wrapped, bare, backticked or fenced into a tracker comment, issue body, PR body, commit message, artifact or doc; refer to it in prose as "the ignore-earlier marker". Guard added to bkit-generated-marker.test.ts: total token occurrences across the workflow files pinned to the sanctioned cut steps (5 ISSUE_TEXT + 6 RELATED_ISSUE_TEXT), every occurrence must match the cut-step sentence, and .bkit/prompts/*.md held at zero.

summary: Every permissions.allow row in .claude/settings.json was inert in cloud sessions because Claude Code applies allow rules only after a workspace trust dialog that a -p/SDK session never shows
description: A cloud /bkit-debug run prompted once per Bash call and stalled at the fetch-context step. The whole Claude permission strategy was one blanket Bash(*) allow row, and it was doing nothing: allow rules and additionalDirectories GRANT capability, so Claude Code holds them until the workspace trust dialog is accepted, and it never shows that dialog in a claude -p or SDK session. deny and ask were unaffected, which is why destructive-op gating still looked healthy. The only signal was one stderr line ('Ignoring 32 permissions.allow entries from .claude/settings.json: this workspace has not been trusted') that no cloud session surfaces, so the config read as configured and did nothing. Verified in a cloud container on Claude Code 2.1.265: flipping the key produced empty stderr and all 32 entries applied.
rootCause: bkit configured permissions only in the repo and assumed repo config was sufficient everywhere. Nothing in the cloud path ever set projects[<repo root>].hasTrustDialogAccepted, and no gate or test asserted that the shipped allow list was in effect at runtime rather than merely present on disk. Committing the config could never have fixed it: a git-tracked .claude/settings.local.json is treated as repository-supplied and held behind the same gate.
remediation: The generated cloud setup script now writes projects[<repo path>].hasTrustDialogAccepted into ~/.claude.json via a jq merge, placed after the jq install. That is the only reliable point: it runs as root, pre-clone, pre-Claude, and is snapshotted, whereas settings resolve before SessionStart and .claude/ is a protected path an in-session write cannot take. The container clone path is an observation rather than a contract, so .claude/hooks/cloud-bootstrap.sh re-checks the discovered git root each session and warns loudly on mismatch. It diagnoses only and does not write: a SessionStart hook that grants workspace trust on any path it discovers is broader capability than the fix needs, and it could not help the current session anyway. A jq probe on the same key is in the cloud verify step.

summary: Auto mode suspends broad allow rules that grant arbitrary code execution, so a permission strategy built on blanket Bash(*) carries no load in an auto-mode session
description: On entering auto mode Claude Code drops blanket Bash(*) and PowerShell(*), wildcarded interpreters, package-manager run commands, and Agent and Monitor allow rules; narrow rules such as Bash(npm test) stay in effect and are restored on leaving auto mode. Fixing the workspace trust gate therefore does not help an auto-mode session at all: what carries the load there is the classifier plus autoMode.environment. By default the classifier trusts only the working repo and its configured remotes, so every context-fetch host is external to it and a candidate block, and Host containment defaults to an ordinary open-internet developer machine, which is wrong for a sandbox behind an egress allowlist. Separately, content-scoped ask rules are evaluated before the classifier and always force a prompt even in auto mode, beating a matching allow.
rootCause: The permission surface was designed for local interactive sessions, where a single wildcard allow row is enough, and was never re-checked against the two cloud permission modes. Nothing surfaced the gap in-session.
remediation: The cloud setup script now seeds autoMode.environment into ~/.claude/settings.json, always emitting the literal $defaults first because omitting it discards the entire built-in list for that section. It adds a Host containment entry naming the sandbox and its egress allowlist, plus the network-allowlist hosts, reusing the same resolver the Cursor allowlist artifact and the OpenCode curl allows use so the three cannot diverge. It must be written host-side: the classifier deliberately does not read autoMode from .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json, so bkit cannot ship it in-repo.

summary: Plan file:line anchors are coordinates against the plan's own baseSha, and every sub-plan anchor additionally assumes its predecessors landed, so a stale plan is re-pointed by symbol and never renumbered
description: A plan artifact's file:line anchors resolve against the baseSha in its bkit:anchor header, not against dev. Sub-plans carry a second implicit baseline on top: their anchors describe the tree their predecessor sub-plans leave behind, stated in the artifacts' own PRE-Task coordinate banners, so a sub-plan's numbers can be wrong against the current tree and right against the tree it will execute on. Mapping every anchor forward to HEAD converts a detectably stale plan into an undetectably wrong one. Bare backtick line refs compound it: they attach to a filename earlier in the sentence, frequently with unrelated paths in between, so nearest-preceding-path attribution silently reassigns them to the wrong file. Path and marker-vocabulary renames are the separable safe half, carrying no line semantics.
rootCause: A plan is written against one tree and built against another, with nothing gating the interval. The anchor header records the baseline but no check compares it against the current tree, and sub-plan drift stays invisible because each sub-plan's numbers are correct relative to a predecessor state rather than to anything the reader can observe.
remediation: Apply the mechanical renames in full across every artifact including the design and the parent plan, not only the sub-plans the drift was noticed in. Add a coordinate banner to each in the artifacts' existing PRE-Task idiom naming what was renamed, listing every cited file changed since the baseline, and instructing resolve-by-symbol-marker-or-heading. Leave the line numbers untouched and leave the anchor header's baseSha at its original value; it records what the plan was written against, and forging it forward tells the runtime that reads it the plan is current. Re-locate confirmed-dead anchors by their quoted prose rather than their number before editing at that position.

summary: build/debug roadmap close-hooks are a FOURTH distinct staging shape (dev-lock ledger append) beyond design/plan's dev-or-PR commit and ship's BOOK_PATHS commit -- per-shape assertion is mandatory, a single grep would miss it
description: design/plan close-hooks commit docs/roadmap.md and docs/roadmap.jsonl via a normal dev or PR-branch commit (widened STRAY allowlist). ship closes stage the same paths through the frozen BOOK_PATHS allow-list. build/debug closes commit to feat/{FID} via the existing git add -A AND separately append the same merge=union ledger line to dev under the ship dev-lock idiom (design Addendum C) -- a fourth, structurally different staging path. bkit-roadmap-staging.integration.test.ts and bkit-roadmap-devwrite.integration.test.ts assert each shape independently. Update at f3e1d49e: only `.bkit/src/bkit-roadmap-devwrite.integration.test.ts` survives; `bkit-roadmap-staging.integration.test.ts` was deleted with the roadmap-sync retirement, so the design/plan and ship shapes are no longer independently asserted, and the board's ledger is now `.bkit/issues.jsonl` (`docs/roadmap.jsonl` is deleted).
rootCause: Four workflows commit the roadmap artifacts through three structurally different git operations (dev-or-PR commit, BOOK_PATHS commit, git add -A plus dev-lock append); asserting only one shape leaves the other three unverified.
remediation: When touching any close-hook staging logic, assert all four shapes independently (design/plan dev+PR STRAY widen, build/debug git add -A + dev-lock append, ship BOOK_PATHS) -- never assume one grep pattern covers all four.

summary: RETIRED — A settled DEBUGGED-status FID is permanently outside reverse tracker-label sync's reach -- deliberate trade-off, not a gap
description: RETIRED at f3e1d49e (#464 retired the tracker-fed roadmap sync). Reverse tracker-label sync no longer exists (`.bkit/src/bkit-roadmap-sync.integration.test.ts` deleted; no reverse-sync in `.bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md`). Original: The reverse-sync status-to-label map (DESIGNED->bkit:design, PLANNED->bkit:plan, BUILT->bkit:build, SHIPPED->bkit:merged) has no entry for DEBUGGED. bkit:debug is an ADDITIVE label layered on top of whatever phase label is already there (per the debug workflow's own header contract), never a replacement -- mapping DEBUGGED to bkit:debug in this REPLACE-one-phase-label sync would collapse an existing {bkit:build, bkit:debug} pair down to just {bkit:debug}, destroying the real phase label. So a settled DEBUGGED FID is simply skipped as unmapped (same path as ABANDONED), forever, by construction: the next ledger append for that FID (BUILT again, or SHIPPED) is what actually advances its label, not a future reverse-sync pass. This is accepted, not a bug: the existing phase label plus additive bkit:debug are already correct on the tracker; reverse-sync has nothing to fix.
rootCause: Reverse-sync replaces exactly one phase label per pass; DEBUGGED status maps to an additive, not phase-replacing, label, so no replacement mapping can exist for it without destroying the additive label's independence from the phase label.
remediation: No live code path — reverse tracker-label sync was removed.

summary: A full-regenerate projection over an append-only merge=union ledger sidesteps the KN-42 duplicate-collapse invariant class entirely -- there is no dedupe invariant to maintain
description: KN-42 (kn-42-pre-release-main-dev-backmerge-with-x-ours-duplicate) documents a duplicate-line hazard from -X ours merges against an upserted file. Because docs/roadmap.md is now a full regenerate from .bkit/issues.jsonl on every fold (never an upserted target), a duplicate ledger line (e.g. from a re-run or a merge artifact) simply folds to its last-wins value during the regenerate -- there is no board-side dedupe invariant to write or maintain, because the board is never the thing merged. Update at f3e1d49e: `.bkit/issues.jsonl` is the SOLE input to the board (`.bkit/scripts/bkit-roadmap-fold.sh:6-7`); `docs/roadmap.jsonl` is deleted.
rootCause: Upserting a target file directly (rather than projecting it from an append-only source) makes every merge or conflict path a potential duplicate-line hazard requiring its own dedupe invariant.
remediation: Prefer full-regenerate-from-ledger over direct-upsert for any future generated-board artifact that can be concurrently written; it removes an entire class of merge-duplicate bugs by construction.

summary: A zero `total_count` from GitHub MCP `search_issues` on a private repo is inconclusive — prefer `list_issues`
description: The roadmap fold no longer does tracker enrichment (`.bkit/scripts/bkit-roadmap-fold.sh:11-12` — tracker issues are not rendered; a wired tracker already shows them). Surviving lesson (upstream MCP behaviour): mcp github search_issues has a known failure mode of silently returning total_count 0 for every query on some private repos, including a bare control query (github-mcp-search-issues-silently-returns-zero-private-repo, still OPEN). The roadmap fold's tracker enrichment therefore uses the bounded list_issues read exclusively; a failed or empty list_issues read still falls back to the on-disk board (never blank, never gates).
rootCause: search_issues total_count 0 on a private repo can mean either truly zero matches or search unavailable; there is no way to disambiguate from the response alone.
remediation: Where a tracker read must be conclusive, use `list_issues`; treat a zero from `search_issues` on a private repo as unknown, not zero.

summary: RETIRED — Roadmap cadence must count since the last ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE row, never since the last analysis refresh -- a refresh-anchored counter resets every ship and never fires
description: RETIRED at f3e1d49e (#464 retired the tracker-fed roadmap sync). `.bkit/scripts/bkit-roadmap-cadence.sh` and `tests/roadmap-cadence.bats` are deleted and nothing reads `ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE`. General lesson kept: anchor a cadence counter on its own fire event, never on a per-cycle refresh. Original: The analysis block (roadmap-analysis marker) refreshes at EVERY ship close. If the cadence threshold were measured from the last refresh instead of a dedicated fire counter row, the count would reset to zero on every ship and the audit/ledger injection would never cross threshold. Anchor on a separate ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE counter row (rebaselined only when it actually fires) instead.
rootCause: Conflating the per-ship analysis-refresh event with the rarer cadence-fire event when choosing a counter anchor.
remediation: No live code path. For any future cadence counter: count since its own last fire row; rebaseline only on fire.

summary: bkit telemetry migrate is deliberately NOT auto-run at bkit upgrade (DE-39); an unmigrated or empty .bkit/issues.jsonl yields an EMPTY board, not a wrong one, with a fold hint naming the command
description: There is no legacy docs/completed.md grep fallback in the fold -- the reader is deleted with the file at migration time. Before a consumer runs bkit telemetry migrate, docs/roadmap.md shows no shipped history (correctly empty, not silently wrong); an install advisory plus the fold's own hint are the only rollout signal, since the migrator cannot be wired to bkit upgrade. rootCause: DE-39 forbids wiring any md-to-jsonl migrator to bkit upgrade (explicit-invocation-only, mechanically enforced).
remediation: Treat an empty active-phase board on a freshly-upgraded consumer as expected pre-migration state; run bkit telemetry migrate once to backfill and bootstrap-seed in-flight FIDs.

summary: Running multiple bats files in one `bats tests/a.bats tests/b.bats ...` invocation intermittently fails with `Failed to create BATS_TEST_TMPDIR1: ... File exists` on macOS — run each file in its own invocation, not as a single multi-file arg
rootCause: bats reuses BATS_RUN_TMPDIR across files in a multi-file invocation and the per-test TMPDIR1 numbering collides when test indices overlap across files (the mktemp mkdir hits an already-existing dir). On stock macOS this surfaces as a `mkdir: ... File exists / Failed to create BATS_TEST_TMPDIR1` storm and a final `Executed N instead of expected M tests`, exiting non-zero even though every individual test passed when the file ran alone.
remediation: Invoke one bats file per call (e.g. `bats tests/ship-gate.bats`, then `bats tests/ship-failure-path.bats`) for the seam-verification prelude and any per-file gate check. `pnpm test:bats tests/*.bats` (the glob form) is fine in CI on Linux; the collision is macOS-local. This is a test-harness portability quirk, not a regression in the script under test — confirm by re-running the single failing file in isolation.

summary: #384 Tier-3 status-hole detector derives its expected ship-* step set by parsing bkit-ship.md (headings + step:"ship-*" literals), NEVER a hand-maintained parallel table — a table is the second source of truth Finding 7 is exactly that drift signature
rootCause: A hand-maintained expected-step table drifts from bkit-ship.md whenever a step is renamed, added, or reordered. Finding 7 of #384 is agents inventing step names precisely because there was no canonical set; a parallel table reintroduces the same drift surface (the cheapest fix under a table — edit the table to match observed reality — is also the wrong one, papering over a workflow bug as expected behaviour).
remediation: Parse the source: extract `## ... Step N — Name` headings AND the `step:"ship-*"` literals inside fenced status-write blocks. The two sets must agree (the Tier-2 invariant freezes them via CANONICAL_SHIP_STEP_KEYS). Path-conditional sets (Path A skips integrate+re-validate; MERGED-on-entry resume; aborted-at-Failure-Path) are derived from the SAME source by inspecting which steps are path-gated, never re-declared. Renaming a step resets attempt counters across consumer repos and orphans the detector corpus — the frozen set is published in bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts as the single source of truth the detector MUST match.

summary: pnpm v7.20+ silently ignores entire `.npmrc` when `${VAR}` env-var is unset
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** `pnpm install` fails with opaque 401 against npmjs.org (NOT `npm.pkg.github.com`). Error reads as generic auth failure — no "token missing" language. `@cbartens/bkit` not found on npmjs.org.
- **Root cause:** Any `${VAR}` in `.npmrc` resolving to an unset env-var causes pnpm v7.20+ to silently ignore the entire `.npmrc` and fall back to defaults. `@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` is dropped; pnpm hits npmjs.org; npmjs.org has no `@cbartens/bkit`; 401.
- **Fix or rule:** Ensure `BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL` is: (1) exported in maintainer's shell before local `pnpm install`; (2) set as a GHA secret on the consumer repo; (3) set as a Vercel env var (preview + production) for Vercel-deployed consumers. Verify with `echo "${BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL:-MISSING}"` before `pnpm install` when troubleshooting. **Superseded by KN-CORE-7 (#274):** as of pnpm >=10.34.3 the project-`.npmrc` `${VAR}` auth path is no longer used at all (it 401s on download even with the token set); the token now lives in pnpm's user-level config via `pnpm config set`.

- **Severity:** critical
- **Source:** phase

summary: bkit install never populated canonicalHashes until after first upgrade
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** After `bkit install`, `.bkit-version` had `canonicalHashes: {}`. On `bkit upgrade`, `isConsumerModified` always returned `false` for all paths (no recorded hashes), so drift detection was ineffective until after the first upgrade pass.
- **Root cause:** `writeBkitVersion` was only called from `bkit-upgrade.ts:updateCanonicalHashesAfterUpgrade`. The `runCoreModule` postDispatch wrote `.bkit-version` via `fs.writeFileSync(versionFile, pkgVersion + "\n")` — plain text, no canonicalHashes. Consumer key survival was preserved by `writeTier2Json` deep-merge regardless, but drift detection via `canonicalHashes` was broken on fresh installs.
- **Fix or rule:** `runCoreModule` postDispatch now uses `writeBkitVersion` (JSON format) and populates `canonicalHashes` from `ws.writes` entries (files written in this run, excluding `.agents/` internal paths). Write is guarded: only when pinnedVersion changed or new canonical entries were recorded (preserves idempotence — 3rd run of install produces zero writes).
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-131, build-challenge C3, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts` (`runCoreModule` postDispatch), `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts` (`writeBkitVersion`)

summary: PR `statusCheckRollup` stays empty when `[skip ci]` is HEAD on push
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** PR opens with no Actions runs visible — `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returns empty. Ship Step 2's CI fail-fast gate (`if ANY failures → Failure Path`) admits the PR despite no CI verification. First observed on PR #7 (BAR-131 consumer-friction suite) — CI only triggered after manually pushing an empty commit without `[skip ci]`.
- **Root cause:** GitHub suppresses both `pull_request` and `push` workflow runs when HEAD commit message contains `[skip ci]` (or `[skip actions]`). Build's Step 15 summary push left `summary status [skip build] [skip ci]` as remote HEAD, so when `gh pr create` opened the PR (Step 16), no `pull_request` event fired. Same shape in debug Step 7 summary push, which would overwrite a previously-clean HEAD with `[skip ci]` and silently empty the PR's rollup. Build Step 17 / debug Step 11 close-workflow commits also never reached remote — no explicit `git push` in either step. Recurs intermittently when the clean final commit does not end up as the dispatched HEAD (e.g. EC-2: Failure Path pushes a `[skip ci]` abort commit onto a live PR).
- **Fix or rule:** Final commit before `git push` in build / debug close-workflow renamed to `chore({FID}): close-workflow status trigger CI` (no skip tags). Explicit `git push` added to close-workflow (also fixes the missing-push side bug). Ship Step 6 (Merge Gate + Merge PR) uses `gh pr merge --body ""` (empty body strips `[skip ci]` from the squash subject). The **CI-Dispatch Gate** (`docs/plans/202606/261-ci-trigger-gate-plan.md`, #261) closes the residual gap: after the final loud push it polls `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` for a `bkit-decide` run, self-heals once with a clean `re-trigger` commit if none appears, and terminates with a named verdict (`dispatched`/`self-healed`/`no-ci`/`unresolved`). The outcome-verification gate is now the enforcement mechanism — not just the pre-push string clause. EC-2 abort-guard prevents Failure-Path abort commits from pushing a `[skip ci]` HEAD onto a live PR.

- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-146, BAR-131 (PR #7 first observation), #261 (CI-Dispatch Gate — outcome-based verification), `.bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md` Step 18 Gate 18, `.bkit/workflows/bkit-debug.md` Step 10 Gate 10, `.bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md` Step 6 + Gate 6, `.bkit/workflows.md` § CI-Dispatch Gate

summary: Transactional install via staging dir — zero-overwrite mid-failure guarantee
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom (design goal):** A crash mid-install (after some modules write but before all complete) would leave partial consumer files in place — no way to distinguish "partial bkit write" from "consumer customisation".
- **Root cause:** Pre-v0.9.0, modules wrote directly to consumer destinations. Any error after the first module's writes left a partially-updated consumer repo with no rollback path.
- **Fix or rule:** v0.9.0+ staging contract: (1) Each module writes to `.bkit-staging/<module>/` (not the real destination). (2) After ALL modules complete, `commitStaging` renames staged files to consumer destinations (atomic per file). (3) On any error (throw, crash, SIGTERM), `discardAllStaging` removes `.bkit-staging/` entirely — consumer files untouched. Test this contract: seed consumer files, simulate mid-install failure via `discardAllStaging`, assert consumer files byte-identical to pre-install state (`fs.readFileSync` equality).
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** critical
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A4, DE-9, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts` (`getStagingDir`, `commitStaging`, `discardAllStaging`), `.bkit/src/bkit-install.integration.test.ts` (Scenario 9)

remediation: v0.9.0+ staging contract: (1) Each module writes to `.bkit-staging/<module>/` (not the real destination). (2) After ALL modules complete, `commitStaging` renames staged files to consumer destinations (atomic per file). (3) On any error (throw, crash, SIGTERM), `discardAllStaging` removes `.bkit-staging/` entirely — consumer files untouched. Test this contract: seed consumer files, simulate mid-install failure via `discardAllStaging`, assert consumer files byte-identical to pre-install state (`fs.readFileSync` equality).

summary: `canonicalHashes` vs `tier3Hashes` — distinct purposes, shared schema
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom (design clarification):** Two sha256 hash maps in `.bkit/version` serve different purposes; conflating them causes logic errors.
- **Root cause / design:** `tier3Hashes` (v0.7.x+): hash of Tier-3 file content AT install time → used by `bkit uninstall` to decide safe-delete (hash match = bkit installed it, no consumer edit → delete; mismatch = consumer edited → preserve). `canonicalHashes` (v0.9.x+): hash of EVERY bkit-managed file content at install time → used by `bkit upgrade` to detect consumer drift (hash mismatch = consumer modified since install → conflict, do not overwrite).
- **Fix or rule:** Do NOT use `tier3Hashes` for upgrade drift detection (covers Tier-3 only; Tier-1/Tier-2 also need drift detection). Do NOT use `canonicalHashes` for uninstall safe-delete (covers all files; safe-delete semantics are Tier-3-only). Keep them separate.
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A5, DE-10, `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts` (`BkitVersion` interface), `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.ts`
rootCause: `tier3Hashes` (v0.7.x+): hash of Tier-3 file content AT install time → used by `bkit uninstall` to decide safe-delete (hash match = bkit installed it, no consumer edit → delete; mismatch = consumer edited → preserve). `canonicalHashes` (v0.9.x+): hash of EVERY bkit-managed file content at install time → used by `bkit upgrade` to detect consumer drift (hash mismatch = consumer modified since install → conflict, do not overwrite).
remediation: Do NOT use `tier3Hashes` for upgrade drift detection (covers Tier-3 only; Tier-1/Tier-2 also need drift detection). Do NOT use `canonicalHashes` for uninstall safe-delete (covers all files; safe-delete semantics are Tier-3-only). Keep them separate.

summary: Helper-action additions to seeded templates are additive, not replacement
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** Four assertions in `templates.test.ts` and `bkit-install.test.ts` fail — substring `BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL: ${{ secrets.BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL }}` not found in seeded `ci.yml` template.
- **Root cause:** Sub-plan P4.T8 added `cbartens/bkit/.github/actions/setup-auth@v1` to `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml` but simultaneously deleted the inline `env: BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL` block under `Install Dependencies`. The plan marked that block RETAIN-WITH-REASON (kill-date v1.1.0). The implementer treated the composite action as a replacement, not an addition.
- **Fix or rule:** When a sub-plan adds a composite GitHub Action alongside an existing inline auth pattern marked RETAIN-WITH-REASON in the Supersession Inventory, the inline pattern MUST be preserved verbatim until its declared kill-date. The addition is strictly additive. After editing any seeded `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/*.yml` file, re-run `pnpm vitest run .bkit/src/bkit-templates.content.test.ts .bkit/src/bkit-install.test.ts` and regenerate the snapshot with `-u`.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** critical
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-131, BAR-138, `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `bar-131-related-bars-suite-plan-4.md` §P4.T8, `build-failure-diagnose-1.md`
- **Token names:** renamed in the token-scheme split (values unchanged). Live names: `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` (fine-grained write token — GitHub MCP, self-hosted Renovate platform auth) and `BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL` (classic `read:packages` — GitHub Packages install auth). The old `GH_BKIT_TOKEN*` names are retired; the postinstall advisory at `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts:1815` flags a `.bkit/.env` still using them.

The plan marked that block RETAIN-WITH-REASON (kill-date v1.1.0). The implementer treated the composite action as a replacement, not an addition.
remediation: When a sub-plan adds a composite GitHub Action alongside an existing inline auth pattern marked RETAIN-WITH-REASON in the Supersession Inventory, the inline pattern MUST be preserved verbatim until its declared kill-date.
