summary: Playwright artifacts via `actions/upload-artifact` are invisible to `gh run view --log-failed` — fetch separately
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** `@bkit-debug-failure-diagnose` on an e2e failure reads `debug-logs-ci-{DEBUG_ATTEMPT}.md` and sees only the bare `pnpm test:e2e` exit code + final summary line ("3 failed"). Per-test stack traces, expected/received diffs, console-capture, screenshots, video, and `trace.zip` are all missing. Diagnose attempts cycle on the same hypothesis (test runner config / Playwright version) because the actual failure context never reaches the agent.
- **Root cause:** `gh run view --log-failed` returns the stdout/stderr of the failing GHA step only. Playwright's rich failure artifacts (per-test output under `test-results/`, the HTML viewer under `playwright-report/`, embedded traces / screenshots / videos) are uploaded via `actions/upload-artifact@v4` in a _separate_ GHA step that runs `if: failure() && steps.e2e.conclusion == 'failure'`. Artifacts live behind the `gh run download -n <name>` API and never appear in `--log-failed` output.
- **Fix or rule:** Three coupled pieces:
  1. **Consumer-side template** — `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml` ships `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts` immediately after `bkit-stub:e2e`. Stub body uploads `playwright-report/` + `test-results/` to an artifact named `playwright-report`, 14-day retention, `if-no-files-found: ignore`. Both stubs must be uncommented together — `bkit-stub:e2e` without `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts` produces no fetchable artifact; `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts` without `bkit-stub:e2e` produces nothing to upload.
  2. **Fetch path** — the e2e artifact fetch runs as a `context-fetch` block declared in `.agents/context.md` (mechanism at `.agents/context.md:17`), executed by debug Step 4 — Fetch Context (`.bkit/workflows/bkit-debug.md:572`).
  3. **Artifact name is a knob** — `E2E_ARTIFACT="${E2E_ARTIFACT:-playwright-report}"` (`.agents/context.md:135`). A consumer that renames the upload artifact must set `E2E_ARTIFACT` to match; otherwise the fetch comes back empty, and `if-no-files-found: ignore` keeps CI silent too.
- **Conditional gating chain:** e2e step gates on `should_run_full || needs_e2e` (`should_run_full` ← the `[force full]` marker; #291 renamed it from `should_run_e2e`). If neither fires (e.g. KN-26 scenario — `decide` demoted to `partial`), e2e step is `skipped`, `steps.e2e.conclusion != 'failure'`, upload step also skipped, no artifact. Symmetric with the BAR-200 ship-side regression gate that catches the upstream cause (skipped previously-failing step).
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-201, KN-26 (sibling — same milestone, closes both ends of the e2e-debug loop), `.bkit/workflows/bkit-debug.md` Step 4 — Fetch Context, `.agents/context.md` (`E2E_ARTIFACT`), `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`bkit-stub:e2e` + `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts`)
rootCause: `gh run view --log-failed` returns the stdout/stderr of the failing GHA step only. Playwright's rich failure artifacts (per-test output under `test-results/`, the HTML viewer under `playwright-report/`, embedded traces / screenshots / videos) are uploaded via `actions/upload-artifact@v4` in a _separate_ GHA step that runs `if: failure() && steps.e2e.conclusion == 'failure'`. Artifacts live behind the `gh run download -n <name>` API and never appear in `--log-failed` output.
remediation: Uncomment `bkit-stub:e2e` and `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts` together in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and keep the uploaded artifact name equal to `E2E_ARTIFACT` (default `playwright-report`) so the `.agents/context.md` fetch block finds it.

references: KN-23 (CI is the only authoritative gate — but only over the files it actually lints)
summary: Lint the artifacts you ship with the config you ship — bkit's own `lint:prose` must cover every shipped `.md`
description:
- **Category:** tooling
- **Rule:** The consumer `lint:prose` bkit ships (`LINT_PROSE_SCRIPT`, `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts`) lints every `*.md` outside `node_modules`. bkit's repo `lint:prose` (`package.json`) feeds vale an explicit list: `.agents/*.md`, `.bkit/*.md`, `.bkit/workflows/**`, `.bkit/prompts/**`, `docs/*.md`, `.bkit/templates/docs/**/*.md`, root `*.md`. Any shipped prose outside that list can fail consumers' pre-commit, pre-push and CI while bkit stays green. Commit, push and CI all run the same `pnpm lint:prose` — one file list, not three independent defences.
- **Keep:** `write-good.So` at `error`; fix canonical prose, never loosen the rule. Managed-block prose can only be fixed upstream — a consumer rewording it drifts a canonical file.
- **Vale config:** `.bkit/templates/.vale.ini` exempts `[**/docs/plans/**/*.md]` from slop/hedging/write-good rules (plan artefacts quote those tokens). `.vale.ini` is Tier 3 `seedOrPrint` — only new installs get template changes; existing consumers merge by hand. Vale merges `BasedOnStyles` across matching scopes and an empty `BasedOnStyles =` inherits rather than disables, so turn rules off with `<Style>.<Rule> = NO`. Prefix scope globs with `**/` so lint-staged's absolute paths match.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** consumer-friction
- **Related:** #195, #179, KN-23, `package.json` (`lint:prose`), `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts` (`LINT_PROSE_SCRIPT`), `.bkit/templates/.vale.ini`
rootCause: A repo gate narrower than the shipped gate: files bkit ships but never lints reach consumers unchecked.
remediation: When bkit starts shipping a new `.md` location, add it to the repo `lint:prose` file list in the same change.

summary: bkit-cloud CI path never ran end-to-end: D1 OIDC boot failure, D2 mid-build router fire, D3 concurrency race
description:
- **Category:** tooling
- **Symptom:** (D1) A live dispatch of `bkit-cloud.yml` failed ~26s in with "Could not fetch an OIDC token … add `id-token: write`". `claude-code-action@v1` in `mode: agent` calls `getOidcToken` at boot — `github.token` passed only as `env: GH_TOKEN` is NOT consumed for the action's own auth. The CI cloud path had never completed. (D2) On a re-build with an open PR, the `worktree-setup` and `create-pr` commits (neither carried `[skip ci]`) triggered a `pull_request: synchronize` CI event → the cloud auto-router fired mid-build. (D3) Dispatched build `bkit-cloud.yml` runs (issue `inputs.issue=50` → group `bkit-cloud-50`) and CI-completion runs (branch `head_branch=feat/50-slug` → group `bkit-cloud-feat/50-slug`) resolved to different concurrency groups → `cancel-in-progress` could not serialize a dispatched build against the ship it triggered.
- **Root cause:** (D1) `bkit-cloud.yml` was designed on the assumption that `github.token` handles all repo git/gh access — the App's OIDC requirement was not surfaced until a live dispatch. (D2) The `worktree-setup` and `create-pr` commits lacked `[skip ci]` tags (documented in `deployments.md` for `create-pr` but not implemented; `worktree-setup` was a genuinely NEW contract entry). (D3) The concurrency key mixed `inputs.issue` (numeric FID) with `head_branch` (`feat/50-slug`) across the two trigger paths — different strings, no cancel.
- **Fix or rule:** (D1) Add `id-token: write` to `bkit-cloud.yml` permissions; require the Claude GitHub App via `/install-github-app`. (D2) Add `bkit [skip ci]` to `worktree-setup` and `create-pr` commit messages; add `bkit [auto route]` to the close-workflow commit (and debug re-trigger commit) only when the issue carries `bkit:auto` at close time. (D3 — revised after structural analysis): Full cross-surface token equality in the `concurrency.group` expression is NOT achievable via GHA expression functions. GitHub evaluates `concurrency.group` from trigger-payload context only, before any step runs. The dispatch payload exposes only the bare issue number (`inputs.issue`, e.g. `141`); the `workflow_run` payload exposes only `head_branch` (= `feat/{FID-with-slug}`, e.g. `feat/141-cloud-app`). GHA expression functions have no regex, no split, and no `replace()` that can reduce a slugged FID to the bare issue number — `replace('feat/141-cloud-app','feat/','')` = `141-cloud-app`, not `141`. The shipped approach (`replace()` to strip `feat/`) was invalid for the actual bkit branch convention (FIDs carry a slug). Corrected design: serialise WITHIN each surface separately — dispatch keys on `inputs.issue`; CI-completion keys on `head_branch`. Cross-boundary races between a dispatched build and the auto-ship it triggers are handled by the orchestrator stale-run guard. See also: DE-21 (full architectural decision), `docs/deployments.md` § "CI trigger on final workflow push", `.bkit/workflows.md` § "HEAD-Subject Assertion".
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high (D1 confirmed live; D2/D3 confirmed by code analysis)
- **Severity:** high (D1 blocked all cloud CI usage; D2 mid-build fires caused confirmed CI run #202/PR #102 phantom; D3 latent race)
- **Source:** live-dispatch
- **Related:** #141, #184, DE-21, KN-11 (`[skip ci]` HEAD → empty rollup)

(D3) The concurrency key mixed `inputs.issue` (numeric FID) with `head_branch` (`feat/50-slug`) across the two trigger paths — different strings, no cancel.

Corrected design: serialise WITHIN each surface separately — dispatch keys on `inputs.issue`; CI-completion keys on `head_branch`. summary: Post-install Phase 3 runs in BOTH install and check — detectors are read-only
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** n/a (design rule — not a bug)
- **Rule:** Phase 3 post-install re-detection runs unconditionally for `bkit install` and `bkit check` alike. Every detector is read-only, so check emits the same advisory set install would emit against the same filesystem state (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:3103-3105`; call at `:3117`).
- **Mechanism:** `runPostInstallCheck(preflightAdvisories, ws, modules, cwd)` takes four parameters and has no `dryRun` (`.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts:2590-2595`). `dryRun` changes only the Done-banner wording and the advisories-artifact `mode` field. Zero-advisory runs print no banner (`formatChecklist([])` returns `""`).
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, DE-4, `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts`
rootCause: `bkit check` must stay read-only. Every Phase 3 detector is read-only, so running them in check keeps install/check advisory parity with no side effects.
remediation: Expect Phase 3 advisories from both `bkit install` and `bkit check`. Never add a side-effecting detector to Phase 3 — it would break check's read-only contract. `runPostInstallCheck` has no `dryRun` parameter; do not reintroduce one to suppress check-mode output.

summary: Pin OpenCode models from models.dev — never the `/docs/zen` page
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Rule:** The `https://opencode.ai/docs/zen` page runs ahead of the deployed gateway and can list ids that do not exist yet; a pinned non-existent id fails at runtime. Curate OpenCode pins (Zen and Go) from `https://models.dev/api.json` — see `opencode-go-models-not-on-zen-v1-models-endpoint-modelsdev-is-truth`. Same class as the Cursor model-id lesson: probe the live catalog, never the docs.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #245, DE-28, `.bkit/providers.md` § Models, `.bkit/prompts.md` § Models, Cursor-live-API analog (#205)

summary: Ownership-mixed JSON is Tier-2 deep containment — never Tier-1 full-overwrite
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Rule:** JSON files holding both bkit-owned and consumer-owned keys (`.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, …) are Tier 2, written via deep containment — `writeTier2JsonContained` in `.bkit/src/bkit-tiers.ts`. The template JSON tree is bkit's scope; consumer keys outside it are never touched. Never write these files as Tier-1 full-overwrite.
- **Detail:** `kn-17-deep-containment-is-canonical-for-ownership-mixed-json`.
- **Type:** rule
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** `.bkit/src/bkit-tiers.ts`, `.bkit/templates/.claude/settings.json`, `.bkit/templates/.cursor/hooks.json`
rootCause: Tier-1 full-overwrite replaces the whole file, so consumer-added keys in an ownership-mixed JSON file are lost on every install and upgrade.
remediation: Register ownership-mixed JSON as Tier 2 and write it with `writeTier2JsonContained`; never Tier-1.

summary: Read `.bkit/version` via `readBkitVersion().pinnedVersion` — never raw `readFileSync().trim()`
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Rule:** `.bkit/version` is JSON (`pinnedVersion` + `canonicalHashes`). A raw `readFileSync(...).trim()` yields the whole JSON blob, and a semver comparison on it (`semverLte`) silently returns false. Read it via `readBkitVersion(path).pinnedVersion` (or `parseBkitVersion(content).pinnedVersion`) in `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts` — it parses JSON, falls back to plain-text semver, and returns null for absent or empty files.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-131, `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts` (`readBkitVersion`, `parseBkitVersion`)
rootCause: The version file is JSON; treating its raw contents as a semver string makes every comparison silently false.
remediation: Always read `.bkit/version` via `readBkitVersion(path).pinnedVersion` or `parseBkitVersion(content).pinnedVersion`; never raw `readFileSync(...).trim()`.

summary: GitHub MCP / `gh` 401 immediately after token rotation
description:
- **Category:** integrations
- **Symptom:** 401 from the GitHub MCP server or `gh` despite a freshly-rotated, valid, correctly-scoped PAT in `.bkit/.env`.
- **Root cause:** the MCP server captures `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` at process launch, so a mid-session rotation leaves it holding the dead token. Non-interactive shells also miss direnv (`.envrc` re-sources only on interactive prompt/cd), so the shell keeps a stale exported value. For `gh` specifically, an exported `GH_TOKEN` (legacy or manual) overrides the keyring — see KN-CORE-8.
- **Fix or rule:** restart/reload the MCP server after rotating the token; for one-off CLI prefix `direnv exec . gh …`. Confirm the live `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` matches `.bkit/.env` before chasing PAT scopes/approval.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** #137

summary: Mend hosted Renovate OOMs on the 3 GB microvm — offer a self-hosted runner on ubuntu-latest via renovatebot/github-action
description:
- **Category:** integrations
- **Symptom:** Every Mend-hosted Renovate job on a large pnpm-11 monorepo fails `kernel-out-of-memory` (3.0/3.0 GB) during `pnpm update --lockfile-only`, blocking all dependency PRs; the worker-cap + Renovate-side `minimumReleaseAge` (KN-41) mitigate but do not guarantee headroom as the graph grows (consumer-a hit the ceiling 2026-07-04).
- **Root cause:** Mend Community Cloud runs Renovate in a fixed ~3 GB hosted microvm; pnpm-11 lockfile resolution + release-age metadata for a large graph exceeds physical RAM. The constraint is runner size, not config — CI / Vercel (>> 3 GB) never OOM.
- **Fix or rule:** Offer a self-hosted alternative — a bkit-managed `.github/workflows/renovate.yml` running `renovatebot/github-action@<pinned-sha>` on `ubuntu-latest` (~16 GB), reusing the SAME backend-agnostic `renovate.json5`. Correctness points: (1) platform auth MUST be a PAT / GitHub App as `BKIT_GH_TOKEN`, NOT `GITHUB_TOKEN` (its PRs don't trigger CI, so `platformAutomerge` never fires); (2) private-registry auth moves from Mend `{{ secrets.BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL }}` templating to a `RENOVATE_HOST_RULES` env (consumer comments the `token` line in `renovate-local.json5` — an uncommented Mend-style line adds an empty-token rule and 401s); (3) the workflow cron wakes the bot (once daily) while `renovate.json5`'s own `schedule` gates normal PRs and `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` bypasses both — do NOT narrow the cron to Monday-only (CVE PRs must still fire within ~24h); (4) `concurrency: { group: renovate, cancel-in-progress: false }`; (5) the Mend App MUST be suspended for the repo (GitHub UI, no `gh api`) or both open duplicate PRs — surfaced by the `renovate-self-hosted-mend-both-active` advisory (warn-only; App state is off-repo / undetectable); (6) `renovate.yml` goes in `renovate.json5` `ignorePaths` (KN-CORE-5) so consumer Renovate never bumps its own pinned action. OOM mitigations are KEPT, not relaxed. Adopt the existing Dependency Dashboard + open PRs by keeping the default `renovate/` `branchPrefix`. (7) Token scope + repo settings the smoke run surfaced: the `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` fine-grained PAT needs `Dependabot alerts: Read` (else `403` on the alert feed — non-fatal, OSV still covers CVEs), and the repo must have `Dependency graph` + `Dependabot alerts` ENABLED but `Dependabot security updates` + `Dependabot version updates` DISABLED (detection ON, auto-fixing OFF — else Dependabot opens PRs competing with Renovate). (8) Commit author: Renovate reads the token owner's email via the `Email addresses: Read` **Account** permission, which exists ONLY on personal-account tokens — org-owned tokens have no such permission, so set the repo variable `RENOVATE_GIT_AUTHOR` (the shipped workflow reads `${{ vars.RENOVATE_GIT_AUTHOR }}`); otherwise commits show the Mend bot author as `Unverified` (cosmetic). (9) `Commit statuses: Read and write` is REQUIRED on the PAT — Renovate reads `/commits/{sha}/statuses` to open the PR / gate `platformAutomerge` and posts its own `renovate/stability-days` checks; missing it, Renovate creates the `renovate/*` branch but `403`s and opens NO PR (symptom: lone `renovate/*` branch, no PR, no CI run). Fine-grained PATs have NO `Checks` permission (check-run writes are App-only) — commit statuses is the PAT mechanism; do not hunt for a Checks toggle. (10) Config hygiene: `matchPackagePatterns` and `baseBranches` are deprecated in Renovate 41+ and drive the Dependency Dashboard's "Config Migration Needed" prompt; the shipped `renovate.json5` uses `matchPackageNames` (glob) + `baseBranchPatterns`, so consumers never see that prompt — do NOT accept it via the dashboard checkbox (`renovate.json5` is Tier-1 canonical-overwrite; a migration PR is clobbered on the next `bkit install`/`upgrade` — fix such deprecations in the bkit template + ship).
- **Type:** post-mortem
- **Confidence:** high
- **Last-confirmed:** 2026-07-04
- **Severity:** normal
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** KN-41, KN-CORE-3, KN-CORE-5, KN-CORE-8, #308, #123, #325

summary: Opaque 401 from `pnpm install` — one unset `${VAR}` makes pnpm ignore the entire `.npmrc`
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** `pnpm install` (local, CI, or Vercel build) fails with a generic 401 against `registry.npmjs.org` — NOT against `npm.pkg.github.com`. The error reads as a plain auth failure with no "token missing" wording, and `@cbartens/bkit` is reported as not found.

summary: pnpm >=10.34.3 auth rework — project `.npmrc` `${BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL}` 401s on download; use user-level `pnpm config set`
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** `pnpm install` / `pnpm add @cbartens/bkit` fails with `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_401` (`GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@cbartens%2Fbkit: Unauthorized`) on pnpm >=10.34.3 even though `BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL` is correctly set in the environment. Metadata calls (`pnpm view @cbartens/bkit`) still resolve, so "it works locally" via `view` is misleading — only the actual download 401s. pnpm 10.34.1 is unaffected (the regression boundary is between 10.34.1 and 10.34.3).
- **Root cause:** pnpm's auth-handling rework stopped honouring a project-level `.npmrc` env-substitution `//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL}` at install fetch time. The token must instead live in pnpm's user-level auth config. Independently, config precedence is project `.npmrc` > user config, so a leftover project auth line also shadows a correct user-level token.
- **Fix or rule:** Commit ONLY the registry mapping in the project `.npmrc` (`@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`) — NEVER an `_authToken` line. Write the token into pnpm's user-level config with `pnpm config set "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL"` on every surface that runs `pnpm install`: CI (a step before install), local dev (run once), Vercel (`vercel.json` `installCommand: pnpm config set //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL && pnpm install`). `pnpm config set` stores the shell-expanded literal token (the shell resolves `$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL` before pnpm writes it), so the one command is version-proof across pnpm 10.x and 11.x — prefer it over a hand-written `~/.npmrc`. Do NOT "restore" the project `.npmrc` `_authToken` line: it appears to work only on pnpm 10.34.1 (warning + store cache) and 401s again the instant pnpm bumps.

- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** critical
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** KN-CORE-2, `.npmrc`, `deployments.md` (§ Consumer CI auth)

description:

summary: OpenCode Go premium models (kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus) are invisible to the /zen/v1/models REST probe — Zen and Go are two separate models.dev providers with different endpoints; models.dev is the source of truth
description:
- **Category:** provider-integration / model-curation
- **Symptom:** curating bkit's opencode model column against `curl https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` reported Kimi K3 as 'not live on OpenCode Go' when the opencode app's model selector clearly listed 'Kimi K3 (2x usage)' under OpenCode Go. Adding an API key to the same endpoint did NOT change the result (55 ids, no kimi-k3). A chat round-trip to `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions` with model `kimi-k3` returned `ModelError: Model kimi-k3 is not supported`.
- **Root cause:** OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go are TWO DISTINCT providers on models.dev — `opencode` (name 'OpenCode Zen', api `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`) and `opencode-go` (name 'OpenCode Go', api `https://opencode.ai/zen/**go**/v1`, nested under /zen/). The `/zen/v1/models` REST endpoint returns ONLY the Zen catalog; Go-only premium models (`kimi-k3`, `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.7-max`) never appear there regardless of auth. The opencode app populates its model selector from models.dev, not from that REST endpoint — which is why the app showed K3 but the probe did not.
- **Fix or rule:** Curate opencode model pins from `https://models.dev/api.json` (read providers `.opencode` and `.["opencode-go"]` `.models`), NEVER from `/zen/v1/models` alone. Tool-call-smoke Go pins against the Go endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` (bare model id, e.g. `kimi-k3`) — verified kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash all emit `tool_calls` there. bkit ships two providers `opencode-zen` + `opencode-go`, both emitting a minimal `provider.<id>` with only `options.apiKey: "{env:BKIT_OPENCODE_API_KEY}"` — no npm driver, no baseURL; OpenCode resolves the rest from models.dev (`.bkit/providers.md:375`). One `BKIT_OPENCODE_API_KEY` covers both; the legacy bare `opencode` provider alias-normalises to `opencode-zen`.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** medium
- **Scope:** bkit-repo
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** `.bkit/providers.md` § Models (Per-provider live model lookup recipe); `.bkit/prompts.md` § Models Live model-ID verification.
rootCause: OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go are two distinct models.dev providers (`opencode` at https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 and `opencode-go` at https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1). The /zen/v1/models REST endpoint returns only the Zen catalog, so Go-only premium models (kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.7-max) are invisible to it regardless of auth. The opencode app reads its catalog from models.dev, not that endpoint.
remediation: Curate opencode pins from https://models.dev/api.json (providers .opencode and .['opencode-go']), never from /zen/v1/models alone. Smoke Go pins against https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions. bkit ships two providers opencode-zen + opencode-go (minimal provider blocks keyed by BKIT_OPENCODE_API_KEY, no npm driver or baseURL); legacy bare `opencode` normalises to opencode-zen.

summary: Adding a managed-block marker style touches three places: the MarkerStyle union and selectMarkers in bkit-install.ts, and the detectMarkerStyle style list in bkit-tiers.ts — missing one leaves upgrade, uninstall or the .prettierignore marker advisory silently skipping files that use it
rootCause: selectMarkers (bkit-install.ts) is the one marker-pair table, used by the install writers and by stripManagedBlock / detectMarkerStyle in bkit-tiers.ts. detectMarkerStyle is the one content-based detector, shared by bkit-upgrade.ts (template sniffing), bkit-uninstall.ts (consumer files) and bkit-preflight.ts (prettierignore-no-markers); it finds markers through findLineAnchoredMarkers, so only a marker alone on its line (bare or behind `# ` / `// `) counts. A style missing from its list returns null: upgrade then treats a markdown template as whole-file and uninstall preserves the file with the bkit block still in it.
remediation: when adding a marker style, update all three places in the same change, add a detectMarkerStyle case to bkit-tiers.test.ts, and add a regression test that installs, tampers a probe INSIDE the managed block, then upgrades and asserts the probe is gone — a silent no-op would let it survive.

summary: GitHub Apps & CI integrations read config from the DEFAULT branch — land config on `main` before activating
description: A newly added integration config (`renovate.json5`, `dependabot.yml`, a branch-protection-scoped check) appears inert, or the App's onboarding PR opens against the wrong base / ungrouped, because the file was committed on a feature or integration branch but not yet merged to the default branch.
rootCause: GitHub Apps and most CI integrations resolve their configuration from the repository's DEFAULT branch at install/scan time, not from the branch where the file was committed. bkit consumers gate the default branch to PRs-from-integration-branch-only, so the config must travel through to the default branch before the integration can see it. Activating the App first makes it scan a branch that has no config yet.
remediation: Copy the updater example (`.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5` or `.bkit/templates/.github/dependabot.yml`) and own it — bkit installs neither. Land it on the default branch FIRST (integration branch → default), THEN install the Renovate App at https://github.com/apps/renovate (no `gh api` equivalent). Same ordering for Dependabot and any default-branch-scoped integration. Renovate keeps reading config from the default branch for ongoing edits too: the example's `useBaseBranchConfig: "merge"` honours `dev`-side edits for dev-targeted runs, but that option is itself read from the default branch and needs one merge there first. Rule: `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters.

summary: Renovate's hosted lockfile regen ignores `pnpm.overrides` — fence overridden packages in your own `renovate.json5`
description: A package pinned in root `pnpm.overrides` gets its locked version rewritten by Renovate on an eligible bump while the override stays in `package.json`. The resulting `pnpm-lock.yaml` is inconsistent → CI fails `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE … doesn't satisfy range`, `automerge` never fires, and Renovate keeps recreating/rebasing the branch, clobbering any manually-corrected lockfile pushed to it.
rootCause: Renovate's hosted lockfile regeneration does NOT reconcile the bumped version against `pnpm.overrides` (local `pnpm` does). Any `pnpm.overrides`-pinned package can hit it. The fence is repo-specific, so it belongs in the consumer's own Renovate config, never in bkit's shipped example.
remediation: Add `{ matchPackageNames: ["<pkg>"], enabled: false }` to `packageRules` in your own `.github/renovate.json5` (copied from `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`; the copy is the whole config — no local preset). Land it on the default branch; Renovate reads config from there. Rule: `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters (Fence a `pnpm.overrides` pin).

summary: Host mirror writes reach `ws.writes` through `trackMirrorWrite`, not `installFile` — assert mirrors via the writeset or disk, and route any new mirror write through `trackMirrorWrite`
description: `installFile()` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts`) only copies/transforms a file and returns a boolean; it never touches `ctx.ws.writes`. Every mirror renderer (`renderClaudeAgentsCommands`, `renderCursorAgentsCommands`, `renderOpencodeAgentsCommands`, `renderCodexAgentsSkills`) records each write AND each orphan delete with `trackMirrorWrite(ctx, rel, written)`, so `bkit check` exits 1 on mirror content drift and dry-run/install writesets match.
rootCause: `installFile()` returns written/skipped; the writeset entry is pushed by the caller via `trackMirrorWrite` (`bkit-modules.ts:583`). A new mirror path that calls `installFile` without `trackMirrorWrite` is invisible to `bkit check` drift and to dry-run parity.
remediation: When adding a host mirror write or orphan prune, pair every `installFile` / `removeOrphans` hit with `trackMirrorWrite`. Tests may assert mirror paths through `ws.writes` (dry-run parity in `bkit-dry-run-parity.integration.test.ts`) or by `fs.readdirSync` on the destination; both see the same set.

summary: Tier-3 seed-or-print upgrade-reach gap — deleting `bkit-mode.sh` does NOT reach seeded consumer copies
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** After upgrading bkit to a version that no longer ships `.bkit/scripts/bkit-mode.sh`, every prior consumer still has the file on disk. The upgrade silently leaves the orphan in place. Worse, the file's shell-function shim (`bkit()`) is still sourced from `~/.zshrc` / `~/.bashrc`, causing a broken `source` error in every new terminal after the file is eventually deleted.
- **Root cause:** `.bkit/scripts/bkit-mode.sh` was Tier-3 seed-or-print. Tier-3 files are written once when absent; on upgrade, bkit skips a file whose template is gone. There is no deletion step — the consumer copy is abandoned without notice.
- **Fix or rule:** Any retired Tier-3 file is paired with an upgrade-migration advisory in its owning module that: (1) detects the orphan on disk with `fs.existsSync`, independent of any template or copy pass, (2) tells the consumer to delete the file, (3) names the shell-rc source line to remove (if applicable), and (4) points at the replacement. Implemented for `bkit-mode.sh` in `runClaudeModule` (`bkit-modules.ts`) as the `bkit-mode-sh-deletion-required` advisory. `COPY_EXCLUDE` keeps the `bkit-mode.sh` basename as a re-addition guard; it does not gate the advisory.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** critical (broken `source` call in every new shell = user-visible error)
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #245, KN-17, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts` (bkit-mode-sh-deletion-required advisory), DE-27

summary: pnpm 11 + per-install `minimumReleaseAge` gate OOMs Mend's Renovate microvm on large monorepos
description:
- **Category:** ci
- **Symptom:** On a large **pnpm 11** monorepo, every Mend-hosted Renovate job fails with `Status: FAILED / Error: kernel-out-of-memory` immediately after `Spawning pnpm install to create pnpm-lock.yaml` → `pnpm update --no-save <deps> --lockfile-only --recursive --ignore-scripts --ignore-pnpmfile`. Blocks **all** lockfile-touching PRs (every dependency PR + weekly `lockFileMaintenance`). CVE / `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` PRs are on a separate path and keep working.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #308, `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters, KN-CORE-10
rootCause: `kernel-out-of-memory` is a **physical** OOM (not a V8 heap limit). `pnpm update --lockfile-only` resolves the whole graph, and the pnpm-level `minimumReleaseAge` gate (in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) verifies publish timestamps for every lockfile entry (~1287) — the combined resolution + metadata footprint exceeds the microvm's RAM. The same verification passes in GHA CI / Vercel because those runners have far more memory. pnpm 11's lockfile regen is heavier than pnpm 10's. Note: `--lockfile-only` does NOT extract/link `node_modules`, so pnpm's worker pool (governed by `PNPM_WORKERS`) is barely engaged — the spike is resolution + release-age metadata, not worker concurrency.
remediation: The Renovate example `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5` (copy-and-own; bkit installs no updater and emits no install advisory for this) carries two Renovate-scoped mitigations: **(A)** `env: { PNPM_WORKERS: "1", PNPM_MAX_WORKERS: "1" }` — bounds pnpm's worker-pool memory; both vars are in Mend's `global:safeEnv` allow-list; may not clear a metadata-driven OOM. **(B)** `minimumReleaseAge: "1 day"` — freshness enforced in Renovate itself; security PRs bypass it. **(B) only clears the OOM once the consumer sets `minimumReleaseAge: 0` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`** — pnpm 11 defaults the gate to 1440, so DELETING the key leaves it active (and strips any `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`); only `0` short-circuits the per-entry check. Safe for `--frozen-lockfile`: pnpm does not record `minimumReleaseAge` in `pnpm-lock.yaml` `settings:`. Trade-off: Renovate-only freshness gates only what Renovate proposes. `PNPM_CONFIG_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE` cannot be set on Mend hosted (not in `global:safeEnv`; `allowedEnv` is admin-only). summary: A prune gated on identity destroys rows the dedup fold dropped — friction keys truncate to ~68 chars and collide, so two distinct entries share one identity and only one is ever stored
description: Found while making bkit harvest MOVE consumer friction (#343). fold() is last-write-wins per identity(), so colliding rows collapse to ONE stored row. An identity-gated prune then deletes EVERY colliding row from the consumer while the store kept one — the loser exists nowhere. Reproduced against live consumer-a data: 'Plan Step 11: close-workflow STRAY guard rejects protocol-mandated docs/pending.md edit' (ts 1783944967776) and a different entry about docs/decisions.md + docs/pending.md edits truncate to the byte-identical key 'friction-plan-step-11-close-workflow-stray-guard-rejects-protocol-ma'; the first was destroyed. Harmless under the old copy-only harvest, fatal the moment harvest deletes. Second instance of the same shape: identity() has no default branch, so rows whose kind is outside VALID_KINDS all collide on undefined — live data has kind:'tool-failure' and kind:'agent-rework' rows in consumer-a friction, and the newer evicted the older from the store.
rootCause: identity() is a lossy projection of a row (kind+repo+key, or ts when key is absent), and fold() treats an identity match as an upsert. Anything gating a DELETE on that projection deletes rows the projection cannot distinguish. Two independent sources of collision: (1) friction keys are truncated at write time, so distinct content yields identical keys; (2) identity() returns undefined for kinds outside VALID_KINDS, mapping every unknown-kind row onto a single fold slot.
remediation: Gate any destructive drain on byte-for-byte row CONTENT read back off disk, never on identity, and keep a store of every DISTINCT row (content dedup), never of fold winners — `bkit-harvest.ts` header invariants. A fold loser is then stored and safe to prune; consumer lines not in the store stay and are logged (`kept N line(s) not in the store`). Migrated friction keys append a sha256 suffix so truncated titles stay distinct (`stableKey`, `bkit-telemetry-migrate.ts`). `identity()` still has no branch for kinds outside VALID_KINDS — never gate a delete on it. General rule: an identity used for dedup/upsert is NOT safe as a delete gate.

summary: Any line in bkit-ship.md mentioning status.jsonl MUST also mention BOOK_ROOT (Tier-2 invariant); regenerate host mirrors with `bkit install`, never by hand
description:
- **Category:** testing

summary: mcp__github__issue_read sanitises issue and comment bodies, deleting every HTML comment — markers that cross a tracker API are h6 heading lines, never HTML comments
description: GitHub stores HTML-comment markers correctly; the loss is read-side only. `mcp__github__issue_read` strips HTML comments, eats angle-bracket spans (`<integer >= 0>` returns as `= 0>`), HTML-escapes quotes, and returns a code-spanned marker as empty backticks. A sanitised read comes back starting at the comment's first heading. Any marker a workflow must detect after a tracker read (`bkit:generated`, `bkit:ignore-earlier`, `bkit:blocked-by`) therefore cannot be an HTML comment.
rootCause: Marker detection is marker-only with no shape fallback, so the mechanism rests on the marker surviving the read. HTML comments do not survive the MCP sanitiser; a guard that asserts workflow text names the filters stays green over input that can never contain a marker.
remediation: Emit tracker-crossing markers as whole-line h6 headings (`###### bkit:generated`, `###### bkit:ignore-earlier`, `###### bkit:blocked-by start` / `end`); detect them whole-line, heading form only. GitHub body and comment text is read through `mcp__github__issue_read` (`get` / `get_comments`) with the shared `sort oldest to newest` step; `gh api` is backup only (`.bkit/workflows.md` § Tracker Blocks). Guard: `bkit-generated-marker.test.ts` (template stamping, point-of-use filters, sort step, no `gh api …/comments?per_page=100` read). File-only markers (`bkit:start` / `bkit:end`, `bkit:tracker`, `bkit:roadmap-*`) stay HTML comments — nothing sanitises them. Verify any new tracker-crossing marker with a live read-back through the actual tool.

summary: Any agent output that carries a whole-line ignore-earlier marker arms the next run's cut on bkit's own text and silently deletes the human context above it
description: The cut fires on a whole-line `###### bkit:ignore-earlier` heading in an issue body or comment. The generated filter drops COMMENTS only: it never touches an issue body (which the design blocked-by encode rewrites in place), and the sweep accumulator RELATED_ISSUES is never filtered and never cut. A marker line written by bkit into either path is a live cut on the next run. Inline prose mentions of the token are inert under whole-line detection.
rootCause: The marker is human-placed by design; a workflow template or prompt that emits it on its own line reproduces a real marker, and the failure is silent both ways — the cut produces a plausibly trimmed artifact and the run that wrote it looks normal.
remediation: Never emit `###### bkit:ignore-earlier` on its own line in any tracker comment, issue body, PR body, commit message, artifact or doc unless the human asked for it (`.agents/rules.md` § Tracker context cut). Guard: `bkit-generated-marker.test.ts` pins the sanctioned cut steps (5 ISSUE_TEXT + 6 RELATED_ISSUE_TEXT) and fails on any whole-line cut marker in the workflow files, `.bkit/workflows.md`, or `.bkit/prompts/*.md`.

summary: `bkit install` dispatch is NOT transactional — a mid-dispatch failure leaves earlier modules' files written; re-run install to complete
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** A failure mid-dispatch (after some modules wrote) leaves those modules' files on disk and `.bkit/version` not re-pinned, so the consumer tree is a partial install.
- **Root cause:** Dispatch writes module files directly to their destinations; `.bkit-staging/<module>/` is only a per-run scratch area for derived files (e.g. `opencode.json`), cleaned by `discardAllStaging()` in a `finally` after every dispatch. `commitStaging` / `discardStaging` / `initStagingDir` are atomic-rename primitives that are NOT on the install path.
- **Fix or rule:** Do not rely on a zero-overwrite guarantee. Recover a partial install by re-running `bkit install` (idempotent). `.bkit/version` is written last in core's `postDispatch`, only after all modules succeed. Wiring `commitStaging` into the install path would be a new per-module transactional design, not a fix.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A4, DE-9, #255, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts` (staging helpers), `.bkit/src/bkit-install.integration.test.ts` (Scenario 9)
rootCause: Dispatch writes module files directly to their destinations; `.bkit-staging/<module>/` is only a per-run scratch area for derived files, and the atomic-rename primitives (`commitStaging`, `discardStaging`, `initStagingDir`) are not on the install path (`bkit-install.ts` staging-helpers comment).
remediation: Do not rely on a zero-overwrite guarantee. Recover a partial install by re-running `bkit install` (idempotent). `.bkit/version` is written last in core's `postDispatch`, only after all modules succeed. Scenario 9 exercises the staging primitives in isolation, not the install path.

summary: GitHub Actions `@v4` floating tags on publishing workflows — pin to commit SHAs
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** OpenSSF Scorecard flags floating action major-version refs (e.g. `actions/checkout@v4`) in publishing workflows. A compromised upstream action or malicious tag re-point executes attacker code in a job with `packages: write` on `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- **Root cause:** `@v4` resolves to whichever commit the upstream `v4` tag points to at run time. Tag re-pointing is possible for any action maintainer and is the primary supply-chain vector.
- **Fix or rule:** Pin `uses:` to a full 40-character commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment. Use `git ls-remote https://github.com/<org>/<action>.git 'refs/tags/vX.Y.Z'` to get the tag SHA. Re-pin manually, or pair the pins with an updater by copying one example and owning it: `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5` (`github-actions` with `pinDigests: true`) or `.bkit/templates/.github/dependabot.yml`. Use one, not both; bkit installs neither. Applies to every third-party ref, especially jobs with elevated permissions (`packages: write`, `id-token: write`, etc.). Rule: `docs/deployments.md` § GitHub Actions pinning / § Dependency updaters.
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-138, `.github/workflows/release.yml`

summary: pnpm v7.20+ silently ignores entire `.npmrc` when `${VAR}` env-var is unset
description:
- **Symptom:** `pnpm install` fails with opaque 401 against npmjs.org (NOT `npm.pkg.github.com`). Error reads as generic auth failure — no "token missing" language. `@cbartens/bkit` not found on npmjs.org.
- **Root cause:** Any `${VAR}` in `.npmrc` resolving to an unset env-var causes pnpm v7.20+ to silently ignore the entire `.npmrc` and fall back to defaults. `@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` is dropped; pnpm hits npmjs.org; npmjs.org has no `@cbartens/bkit`; 401.
- **Fix or rule:** bkit's project `.npmrc` carries ONLY the registry mapping (`@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`) — no `${VAR}` line — and the token goes into pnpm's user-level config via `pnpm config set "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL"` on every surface that runs `pnpm install` (KN-CORE-7, `docs/deployments.md` § Consumer CI auth). The trap only bites a project `.npmrc` that still carries an `${VAR}` auth line: delete that line (`npmrc-legacy-authtoken` advisory, `detectNpmrcLegacyAuthToken` in `bkit-postinstall.ts`). Never write `${VAR:-default}` anywhere pnpm reads — pnpm does not parse the POSIX fallback and sends no auth (asserted by the B6 block in `bkit-preflight.test.ts`). Diagnose a 401 against `registry.npmjs.org` by checking the project `.npmrc` for any `${VAR}` line first.

- **Severity:** normal
- **Related:** BAR-138, DE-3, KN-CORE-2, KN-CORE-7, `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts`, `docs/deployments.md`

summary: Mend hosted Renovate OOMs on the 3 GB microvm — copy the self-hosted `renovate.yml` example onto `ubuntu-latest`
description:
- **Symptom:** Every Mend-hosted Renovate job on a large pnpm-11 monorepo fails `kernel-out-of-memory` (3.0/3.0 GB) during `pnpm update --lockfile-only`, blocking all dependency PRs; the worker-cap + Renovate-side `minimumReleaseAge` (KN-41) mitigate but do not guarantee headroom as the graph grows.
- **Related:** KN-41, KN-CORE-3, KN-CORE-5, KN-CORE-8, #308, #123, #325, `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters
rootCause: Mend Community Cloud runs Renovate in a fixed ~3 GB hosted microvm; pnpm-11 lockfile resolution + release-age metadata for a large graph exceeds physical RAM. The constraint is runner size, not config — CI / Vercel (>> 3 GB) never OOM.
remediation: Copy `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/renovate.yml` (renovatebot/github-action at a pinned SHA, `ubuntu-latest` ~16 GB) and own it — bkit installs no updater; edit `runs-on` in the copy. It reuses the same `renovate.json5`. Correctness points (`docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters): (1) platform auth is a repo secret `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT: Contents / Pull requests / Workflows / Commit statuses / Issues read-write, Dependabot alerts read), NEVER `GITHUB_TOKEN` (its PRs do not trigger CI, so required checks and automerge never fire); (2) private-registry auth comes from `RENOVATE_HOST_RULES` set by the workflow — leave the Mend-style `hostRules` `token` line in `renovate.json5` commented (uncommented, it adds an empty-token rule and 401s); (3) the daily cron wakes the bot while `renovate.json5` `schedule` gates normal PRs and `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` bypasses both — never narrow the cron to weekly; (4) suspend the Mend App for the repo (GitHub UI, no `gh api`) or both open `renovate/*` PRs — nothing detects this for you; (5) keep your copied `renovate.yml` OUT of `ignorePaths` so its own action pins refresh; (6) repo settings: Dependency graph + Dependabot alerts ON, Dependabot security + version updates OFF; (7) org-owned tokens cannot read the owner email — set the Actions variable `RENOVATE_GIT_AUTHOR`. OOM mitigations stay as they are.

summary: GateGuard subagent-exemption mechanism differs between Claude and opencode
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** On Claude, GateGuard's subagent-exemption (skip advisory when `agent_id` is present) fires correctly. On opencode, the equivalent exemption may not fire — GateGuard runs against every file edit including sub-agent dispatches.
- **Root cause:** Claude's PreToolUse hook payload includes `agent_id` when the hook fires inside a subagent context; `gateguard.cjs` reads this field to suppress the advisory. opencode's plugin API provides a different event payload shape — the field name (if any) that indicates subagent context is not the same as Claude's. The opencode plugin (`gateguard.js`) must use the opencode-specific mechanism, which may not be present in all plugin API versions.
- **Fix or rule:** Validate the opencode plugin's subagent-detection against the installed opencode version's plugin API spec before relying on it. If the opencode API lacks a reliable subagent indicator, gate the advisory behind a more conservative heuristic (e.g. trust file count per session as a proxy). Do not assume parity with Claude's payload shape.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** medium (identified from spec review; not yet empirically verified post-spike)
- **Severity:** low (advisory suppression failure = extra noise, not a functional regression)
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #245, `.opencode/plugin/gateguard.js`, `.claude/hooks/gateguard.cjs`

summary: A cadence counter must count since its own last fire event, never since a per-cycle refresh
description: A threshold counter anchored on an event that recurs every cycle (e.g. a per-ship refresh) resets every cycle and never crosses its threshold. Anchor it on a dedicated fire row, rebaselined only when it fires.
rootCause: Conflating the per-cycle refresh event with the rarer fire event when choosing the counter anchor.
remediation: Count since the counter's own last fire row; rebaseline only on fire.

summary: Sentinel-file cleanup must bracket the write — stale sentinels cause false Failure Path
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** After manually resolving a `git rebase` conflict outside the workflow, re-invoking `/bkit-build` or `/bkit-debug` immediately routes to the Failure Path even though the rebase is complete.
- **Root cause:** `bkit-build.md` / `bkit-debug.md` Step 2 — Worktree Setup `touch .rebase-failed` sentinel is never removed on success or retry. The sub-step 3a existence check fires on the stale file from the prior failed run.
- **Fix or rule:** Bracket every sentinel with explicit cleanup: (1) `rm -f` at the START of the bash block that writes the sentinel (clears stale-from-prior-run before any new attempt), and (2) `rm -f` in the Failure Path step after the sentinel is no longer needed. Pattern: create-write only inside the failure branch; delete-unconditionally at start of each attempt and at Failure Path exit. See `bkit-build.md` / `bkit-debug.md` Step 2 — Worktree Setup bash block.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** build-challenge

summary: Multi-section output format — EOF-append landing section must be last
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** Agent appends gap findings at EOF of output file; entries land inside `## Notes` instead of `## Identified Gaps Log`, breaking downstream consumer parsing.
- **Root cause:** `bkit-build-plan-verify.md` Output format had `## Identified Gaps Log` in the middle of a six-section skeleton. The Fix 1b `echo {finding} >> {output}` directive appends at EOF, which is after `## Notes` (the last section). Downstream gap-remediate consumers grep for `## Identified Gaps Log` and find gaps mixed into Notes.
- **Fix or rule:** When an agent uses flat-append-at-EOF for a specific section, that section MUST be last in the Output format skeleton. Reorder so the append-target section is last. Same reason `bkit-build-challenge-tests.md`'s `## Bugs Discovered` must come after `## Blockers`.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** build-challenge
- **Related:** BAR-155, `.bkit/prompts/bkit-build-plan-verify.md`, `.bkit/prompts/bkit-build-challenge-tests.md`
rootCause: `bkit-build-plan-verify.md` Output format had `## Identified Gaps Log` in the middle of a six-section skeleton. The Fix 1b `echo {finding} >> {output}` directive appends at EOF, which is after `## Notes` (the last section). Downstream gap-remediate consumers grep for `## Identified Gaps Log` and find gaps mixed into Notes.
remediation: When an agent uses flat-append-at-EOF for a specific section, that section MUST be last in the Output format skeleton. Reorder so the append-target section is last. Same reason `bkit-build-challenge-tests.md`'s `## Bugs Discovered` must come after `## Blockers`.

summary: opencode spec churn — pin the probed version, not a naive next-digit bump
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** After upgrading opencode or updating `opencode.json`, agents fail to launch or plugin API calls are rejected with schema errors.
- **Root cause:** opencode's plugin spec, frontmatter fields (`reasoningEffort`, provider config shape), and command-file syntax change between releases without a stable semver contract. Naively bumping a version number or copying from release notes produces configs that may never have existed in the actual binary.
- **Fix or rule:** Probe the installed opencode binary for its supported field names and plugin API shape before updating `opencode.json`. Read `.opencode/opencode.json` against the opencode docs for the version that `opencode --version` reports. When in doubt, copy from a fresh `opencode init` output with that version, not from examples in issues or READMEs that may lag the release.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** medium (observed during #245 spike; spec drift confirmed across minor releases)
- **Severity:** normal
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #245, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts` (applyOpencodeAgent transform), `docs/plans/202606/logs/245-opencode-provider-host/spike-verdict.md`
rootCause: opencode's plugin spec, frontmatter fields (`reasoningEffort`, provider config shape), and command-file syntax change between releases without a stable semver contract. Naively bumping a version number or copying from release notes produces configs that may never have existed in the actual binary.
remediation: Probe the installed opencode binary for its supported field names and plugin API shape before updating `opencode.json`. Read `.opencode/opencode.json` against the opencode docs for the version that `opencode --version` reports. summary: Pre-release `main`->`dev` backmerge with `-X ours` duplicates the `bkit:managed` version marker
description:
- **Category:** release
- **Symptom:** After the release cutter's step-6 pre-release backmerge (`chore: backmerge main into dev pre-release`), an unpredictable subset of managed docs gains a DUPLICATE `<!-- bkit:managed vX ... -->` line — the new version marker immediately followed by the prior release's marker (e.g. `v4.1.10` then `v4.1.9`). Recurs on most releases (4.1.6 / 4.1.7 / 4.1.8 / 4.1.9 / 4.1.10 each needed a manual "remove duplicate bkit:managed marker after backmerge" fix); hits the frequently-edited living docs (`completed` / `decisions` / `knowledge` / `pending`) more than static ones. If unnoticed it ships two markers, and `bkit check`'s version-marker drift detection then flags the stale one.
- **Root cause:** The backmerge used `git merge origin/main -X ours`. Relative to the merge base, BOTH sides changed the single marker line (dev: base->new version; main: base->prior version), which should conflict (and `-X ours` would pick dev). It does NOT register as a conflict: the two marker lines share an identical long prefix (`<!-- bkit:managed v4.1.`) and identical suffix, surrounded by identical blank-line / `# Title` context, so git's 3-way alignment treats dev's and main's marker lines as two INDEPENDENT insertions rather than one contested line. No conflict fires, so `-X ours` never resolves it and both lines survive. The hit subset varies because the alignment depends on each file's divergent body. Reproduced deterministically: `git merge-tree --write-tree -X ours <dev-tip> <main-release-squash>` emits the duplicate.
- **Fix or rule:** Backmerge with `git merge origin/main -s ours`, NEVER `-X ours`. The pre-release precondition already requires everything on `origin/dev..origin/main` to be content-equivalent in dev (main carries only the prior `chore(release):` squash; dev is strictly ahead), so `-s ours` keeps dev's tree verbatim, records main as merged (so `origin/dev..origin/main` -> 0), and imports zero lines — removing the marker-alignment artifact entirely. Guard first: confirm `git log origin/dev..origin/main --oneline` lists ONLY prior release squash(es), and STOP if anything else appears (a real main-only change is the one thing `-s ours` would silently drop). Fixed in `.claude/agents/utility-new-release.md` step 6.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** medium
- **Scope:** bkit-repo
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** `utility-new-release.md` step 6; prior manual fixes 18e6fc73 / 1b69002f / 4c944bb8 / ae31f8a0 / 1ace7521 / a263e3ab.
rootCause: The backmerge used `git merge origin/main -X ours`. Relative to the merge base, BOTH sides changed the single marker line (dev: base->new version; main: base->prior version), which should conflict (and `-X ours` would pick dev). It does NOT register as a conflict: the two marker lines share an identical long prefix (`<!-- bkit:managed v4.1.`) and identical suffix, surrounded by identical blank-line / `# Title` context, so git's 3-way alignment treats dev's and main's marker lines as two INDEPENDENT insertions rather than one contested line. No conflict fires, so `-X ours` never resolves it and both lines survive. The hit subset varies because the alignment depends on each file's divergent body. Reproduced deterministically: `git merge-tree --write-tree -X ours <dev-tip> <main-release-squash>` emits the duplicate.
remediation: Backmerge with `git merge origin/main -s ours`, NEVER `-X ours`. The pre-release precondition already requires everything on `origin/dev..origin/main` to be content-equivalent in dev (main carries only the prior `chore(release):` squash; dev is strictly ahead), so `-s ours` keeps dev's tree verbatim, records main as merged (so `origin/dev..origin/main` -> 0), and imports zero lines — removing the marker-alignment artifact entirely. Fixed in `.claude/agents/utility-new-release.md` step 6.

summary: Ship Step 9 — Re-validate fired a second, duplicate CI run on every head move because it dispatched unconditionally instead of probing first
description: Every ship that took Path B (rebase / gh pr update-branch) produced TWO completed CI runs on the SAME commit, seconds apart: one from the pull_request event the push itself fired, one from ship's own gh workflow run. Observed five times on feat/380-roadmap-analysis-refresh -- e.g. head 1b51b989 ran pull_request at 21:07:21 (run 33013836266) and workflow_dispatch at 21:07:52 (run 33013876939); same shape at ea6f17f7 (5s apart), ea37e5c8 (3s), bb981805 (3s), 11a74fd4 (9s). Doubled CI minutes and wall-clock on every rebase-integrating ship.
rootCause: bkit-ship.md Step 9 — Re-validate carried the comment 'Head moved -- dispatch CI unconditionally' and called gh workflow run ci.yml with no check for a run already at that head, so the pull_request run the force-push had just triggered was ignored. The CI-Dispatch Gate that fixed exactly this class for build and debug (bounded bkit_wait_ci presence poll, dispatch only on none) was never extended to ship -- ship was recorded as OUT of scope on the grounds that a dispatch-outcome verdict would mask 'essential tests skipped', which is a valid objection to the gate's pass semantics but not to its probe. ci.yml concurrency could not absorb the duplicate either: pull_request runs group by head_ref while workflow_dispatch runs group by run_id, so the two land in different groups and neither cancels the other.
remediation: Ship Step 9 — Re-validate now runs an inline `gh run list` presence probe at the validated head (`SHIP_PROBE_ATTEMPTS` x `SHIP_PROBE_INTERVAL_S` = 6 x 10s, `.bkit/scripts/bkit-ship-timeouts.sh`) before dispatching and skips gh workflow run when a run already exists at the head; probe err (incl. blocked sleep) still dispatches, preserving the pre-fix safety property. The probe is never a pass condition -- the completion poll and `bkit-ship-gate.sh assert --validated` at Gate 10 — Merge Gate + Merge PR still own the verdict. The completion poll was made head-anchored (select(.headSha == $h)) at the same time, because without a guaranteed-fresh dispatch an unfiltered gh run list --limit 1 can return a completed run from a superseded head.

summary: dist/ staleness — `pnpm build` must run before push for `.bkit/src/*.ts` changes
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** Local pre-commit/pre-push hooks pass green (`typecheck`, `test`, `format:check`, `lint:slop`, `lint:prose`) but CI's `run-tests` job fails on "Verify dist/ is fresh" with a diff showing `dist/*.js` missing latest source changes.
- **Root cause:** Pre-commit/pre-push hooks invoke `tsc --noEmit` (typecheck only) and `vitest run` (no compile) — do NOT run `pnpm build`. CI runs `pnpm build && git diff --exit-code dist/` to ensure shipped artefacts match source. Source-only commits leave `dist/` stale; CI catches it.
- **Fix or rule:** Any TS edit under `.bkit/src/*.ts` MUST be accompanied by `pnpm build && git add dist/` in the same commit. Hook-level enforcement landed in BAR-131 PR #7 — `.husky/pre-push` now runs `pnpm bkit:check:dist` (source-repo only, outside the bkit:start..bkit:end block so `bkit install` doesn't strip it), so a stale dist/ fails the push locally rather than waiting for CI. Fired twice before enforcement: BAR-141 PR #5 (commit `edbd891` broke, `7ab6bff` fixed) and BAR-131/139/142 PR #7 (~2.6k lines of new TS across 13 files with zero dist/ updates; required a separate rebuild commit).
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, BAR-131, PR #5, PR #7, commits `edbd891` (broke), `7ab6bff` (fixed), `.husky/pre-push`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/deployments.md` § `dist/` commit policy
