description: Incident: a ship of #703 squash-merged 16 commits into one PR; one intermediate commit subject was `chore(690-header-nav-shell): worktree-setup bkit [skip ci]`. GitHub Actions scans the merge commit's subject AND body for suppression tokens. `gh pr merge --squash` without an explicit `--body ""` defaults to a body that concatenates every commit's subject line, so the token leaked into the merge body even though the PR TITLE carried none. The workflow's only mechanised check at the time was a PR-title grep (never scans the resulting merge body); the backstop was an after-the-fact `gh run list` check, not a preventive assertion.
rootCause: gh's `--squash` default body behaviour (concatenate commit subjects) plus a title-only skip-token assertion that never re-scans the body it actually produces.
remediation: Merge/commit bodies that land work MUST be skip-token-free on every transport (`.agents/rules.md` § Git, CI & Merges — shared invariant, not owned by one call site). Ship merges through `bkit prs merge`, which runs `gh pr merge --squash --subject <skip-token-free subject> --body ""` (`mergePr`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/prs.ts:421`). The MCP `merge_pull_request` fallback passes the printed subject as `commit_message` with an empty body, never the tool's default. A title-only pre-merge assertion is NOT sufficient by itself — treat it as one layer, not the guarantee.

summary: The no-dead-MAX_* audit counted references inside comments, so a cap enforced nowhere in the scanned corpus passed on a rationale comment alone
description: MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS is enforced in .github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml, outside the .bkit/core/workflows/*.md corpus the audit scans. The corpus contained the name only in a bkit-ship.md rationale comment; deleting that comment (workflow files carry no rationale) turned the rule red on a cap that was never dead.
rootCause: the audit matched the constant anywhere inside a fenced block, comments included, so a comment mentioning a constant read as enforcement.
remediation: count executable lines only (drop /^\s*#/) and include the real enforcement surfaces (bkit-cloud.yml + its template) in the scanned set. A constant named solely in a comment can no longer satisfy the rule.

summary: GitHub Actions honours 5 CI-suppression tokens ([skip ci], [ci skip], [no ci], [skip actions], [actions skip], case-insensitive) -- a post-close scan checking only 2 of them is a silent D1-class regression
rootCause: A scan site that carries its own hand-written token list drifts from the others; a list narrower than GitHub's five tokens, or a case-sensitive match, lets a CI-suppressing token through the authoritative post-close scan while the advisory pre-checks catch it.
remediation: Match the full case-insensitive set at every site. Every site is TypeScript and shares one regex, `SKIP_CI_TOKEN` in `.bkit/core/engine/commands/lib.ts:478` (used by `bkit prs`, `bkit runs`, `bkit branches`, and `bkit ci`'s `.husky/pre-push` CI-suppressor guard) — never add a local copy or a shell grep in a workflow file.

summary: Documented fail-open empty catches must stay empty; adding console.error to improve them triggers defensive.error-swallowing and turns a GREEN slop:delta RED
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** pnpm slop:delta RED with 4 net-new defensive.error-swallowing findings (net score +4.80) in bkit-modules.ts:2724/:3216 and guardrails.cjs:128 (root + template).
- **Root cause:** A verify step improved three documented fail-open empty catches by replacing the empty-catch-with-comment shape with a console.error log-and-continue, believing logging was safer than silence. But slop-scan.config.json already disables defensive.empty-catch for these exact files (overrides lines 173-193) with written _reason fields stating the empty catch is the implementation of the fail-open contract and each is paired with an advisory emission path. The console.error-and-continue shape is exactly what defensive.error-swallowing flags (catch logs only), so the improvement introduced the only rule NOT overridden for these files.
- **Fix or rule:** When a catch is covered by a defensive.empty-catch config override with a written reason, keep it as an empty catch with a comment; do NOT add console.error. If diagnostics are genuinely needed, surface via the file existing advisory channel (advisories.push) that is not logs-only and matches the documented advisory emission path. Never rethrow inside a fail-open hook (e.g. Cursor PreToolUse) where aborting crashes the editor session; the shipped fallback is correct behaviour, not a swallowed bug.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high (git blame confirmed the regression: commit bac21726 had empty catches; 3c50f02b changed them to console.error; reverting cleared all 4 findings, score 36.40 to 31.60)
- **Severity:** normal (turns a GREEN gate RED with no functional benefit; blocks ship)
- **Source:** #384 build cycle
- **Related:** #384, slop-scan.config.json
rootCause: A verify step replaced documented fail-open empty catches (covered by a defensive.empty-catch config override with written reason) with a console.error log-and-continue, believing logging was safer than silence. But defensive.error-swallowing is the one rule NOT overridden for these files, and console.error-and-continue is exactly what it flags (catch logs only). The override reasons explicitly state empty catch is the fail-open contract.
remediation: Keep catches covered by a defensive.empty-catch override as empty catches with a comment. If diagnostics are needed, use the file existing advisory channel (advisories.push), not console.error that is not logs-only and matches the documented advisory emission path. Never rethrow inside fail-open hooks (Cursor PreToolUse) where aborting crashes the editor session.

summary: Any FID resolved from a PR-body marker (bkit-auto D9 marker-primary) must pass a strict slug allowlist before it builds a filesystem path or dispatches downstream
rootCause: PR body is collaborator-trusted, not commit-signed (docs/security.md CI Auto-Route Trust); marker-derived {FID} flows into docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/ and .worktrees/{FID}, so bkit:fid=../../elsewhere redirects writes when unvalidated.
remediation: Assert the canonical per-tracker slug (^[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ github / ^[a-z]+-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ linear / ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ no-tracker+branch-derive) at the resolution site; marker failure falls through to branch-derive, branch-derive failure is a Failure Path. Same guard the five phase workflows apply at FID mint.

summary: Adding a managed-block marker style touches three places: the MarkerStyle union, selectMarkers, and the detectMarkerStyle style list, all in managed-block.ts — missing one leaves upgrade or uninstall silently skipping files that use it
rootCause: selectMarkers (`.bkit/core/engine/install/managed-block.ts:21`) is the one marker-pair table, used by the install writers and by stripManagedBlock / detectMarkerStyle in the same file. detectMarkerStyle (`managed-block.ts:134`) is the one content-based detector, shared by upgrade.ts (template sniffing), uninstall.ts (consumer files) and checks/after/managed.ts; it finds markers through findLineAnchoredMarkers, so only a marker alone on its line (bare or behind `# ` / `// `) counts. A style missing from its list returns null: upgrade then treats a markdown template as whole-file and uninstall preserves the file with the bkit block still in it.
remediation: when adding a marker style, update all three places in managed-block.ts in the same change, add a detectMarkerStyle case to `.bkit/core/engine/install/write.test.ts`, and add a regression test that installs, tampers a probe INSIDE the managed block, then upgrades and asserts the probe is gone — a silent no-op would let it survive.

summary: mcp__github__issue_read sanitises issue and comment bodies, deleting every HTML comment — markers that cross a tracker API are h6 heading lines, never HTML comments
description: GitHub stores HTML-comment markers correctly; the loss is read-side only. `mcp__github__issue_read` strips HTML comments, eats angle-bracket spans (`<integer >= 0>` returns as `= 0>`), HTML-escapes quotes, and returns a code-spanned marker as empty backticks. A sanitised read comes back starting at the comment's first heading. Any marker a workflow must detect after a tracker read (`bkit:generated`, `bkit:ignore-earlier`, `bkit:blocked-by`) therefore cannot be an HTML comment.
rootCause: Marker detection is marker-only with no shape fallback, so the mechanism rests on the marker surviving the read. HTML comments do not survive the MCP sanitiser; a guard that asserts workflow text names the filters stays green over input that can never contain a marker.
remediation: Emit tracker-crossing markers as whole-line h6 headings (`###### bkit:generated`, `###### bkit:ignore-earlier`, `###### bkit:blocked-by start` / `end`); detect them whole-line, heading form only. GitHub body and comment text is read through `mcp__github__issue_read` (`get` / `get_comments`) with the shared `sort oldest to newest` step; `gh api` is backup only (`.bkit/workflows.md` § Tracker Blocks). Guard: `bkit-generated-marker.test.ts` (template stamping, point-of-use filters, sort step, no `gh api …/comments?per_page=100` read). File-only markers (`bkit:start` / `bkit:end`, `bkit:tracker`, `bkit:roadmap-*`) stay HTML comments — nothing sanitises them. Verify any new tracker-crossing marker with a live read-back through the actual tool.

summary: A guard test that asserts a doc CONTAINS an internal label makes the citation mandatory and blocks the doctrine that removes it
description: A doc-content test once asserted `workflows.md` must contain the literal KN-11 as proof the non-push doctrine was documented. Removing internal identifiers from shipped docs turned that green assertion red, and the only ways to satisfy both were to keep the label or to weaken the doctrine.
rootCause: the test asserted the CITATION rather than the MECHANISM it points at. A label is a stable string and therefore an easy assertion target, which is exactly why it silently becomes a requirement.
remediation: Assert the mechanism, not its record or the prose around it (`docs/testing.md` § shape guards: "Pin the mechanism, not the wording", lines 184-194). Text is a valid assertion target only when the text is the deliverable (a rules file an agent reads, a CLI help string, an advisory message).

summary: A prune gated on identity destroys rows the dedup fold dropped — friction keys truncate to ~68 chars and collide, so two distinct entries share one identity and only one is ever stored
description: Found while making bkit harvest MOVE consumer friction (#343). fold() is last-write-wins per identity(), so colliding rows collapse to ONE stored row. An identity-gated prune then deletes EVERY colliding row from the consumer while the store kept one — the loser exists nowhere. Reproduced against live consumer-a data: 'Plan Step 11: close-workflow STRAY guard rejects protocol-mandated docs/pending.md edit' (ts 1783944967776) and a different entry about docs/decisions.md + docs/pending.md edits truncate to the byte-identical key 'friction-plan-step-11-close-workflow-stray-guard-rejects-protocol-ma'; the first was destroyed. Harmless under the old copy-only harvest, fatal the moment harvest deletes. Second instance of the same shape: identity() has no default branch, so rows whose kind is outside VALID_KINDS all collide on undefined — live data has kind:'tool-failure' and kind:'agent-rework' rows in consumer-a friction, and the newer evicted the older from the store.
rootCause: identity() is a lossy projection of a row (kind+repo+key, or ts when key is absent), and fold() treats an identity match as an upsert. Anything gating a DELETE on that projection deletes rows the projection cannot distinguish. Two independent sources of collision: (1) friction keys are truncated at write time, so distinct content yields identical keys; (2) identity() returns undefined for kinds outside VALID_KINDS, mapping every unknown-kind row onto a single fold slot.
remediation: Gate any destructive drain on byte-for-byte row CONTENT read back off disk, never on identity, and keep a store of every DISTINCT row (content dedup), never of fold winners — `.bkit/core/engine/commands/harvest.ts` header invariants. A fold loser is then stored and safe to prune; consumer lines not in the store stay and are logged (`kept N line(s) not in the store`). `identity()` (`.bkit/core/engine/ledgers/telemetry.ts`) still has no branch for kinds outside VALID_KINDS — never gate a delete on it. General rule: an identity used for dedup/upsert is NOT safe as a delete gate.

summary: pnpm v7.20+ silently ignores entire `.npmrc` when `${VAR}` env-var is unset
description:
- **Symptom:** `pnpm install` fails with opaque 401 against npmjs.org (NOT `npm.pkg.github.com`). Error reads as generic auth failure — no "token missing" language. `@cbartens/bkit` not found on npmjs.org.
- **Root cause:** Any `${VAR}` in `.npmrc` resolving to an unset env-var causes pnpm v7.20+ to silently ignore the entire `.npmrc` and fall back to defaults. `@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` is dropped; pnpm hits npmjs.org; npmjs.org has no `@cbartens/bkit`; 401.
- **Fix or rule:** bkit's project `.npmrc` carries ONLY the registry mapping (`@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`) — no `${VAR}` line — and the token goes into pnpm's user-level config via `pnpm config set "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL"` on every surface that runs `pnpm install` (KN-CORE-7, `docs/deployments.md` § Consumer CI auth). The trap only bites a project `.npmrc` that still carries an `${VAR}` auth line: delete that line (`npmrc-legacy-authtoken` advisory, `detectNpmrcLegacyAuthToken` in `bkit-postinstall.ts`). Never write `${VAR:-default}` anywhere pnpm reads — pnpm does not parse the POSIX fallback and sends no auth (asserted by the B6 block in `bkit-preflight.test.ts`). Diagnose a 401 against `registry.npmjs.org` by checking the project `.npmrc` for any `${VAR}` line first.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Severity:** normal
- **Related:** BAR-138, DE-3, KN-CORE-2, KN-CORE-7, `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts`, `docs/deployments.md`
rootCause: Any `${VAR}` in `.npmrc` resolving to an unset env-var causes pnpm v7.20+ to silently ignore the entire `.npmrc` and fall back to defaults. `@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` is dropped; pnpm hits npmjs.org; npmjs.org has no `@cbartens/bkit`; 401.
remediation: bkit's project `.npmrc` carries ONLY the registry mapping (`@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`) — no `${VAR}` line — and the token goes into pnpm's user-level config via `pnpm config set "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL"` on every surface that runs `pnpm install` (KN-CORE-7, `docs/deployments.md` § Consumer CI auth). The trap only bites a project `.npmrc` that still carries an `${VAR}` auth line: delete that line (`npmrc-legacy-authtoken` advisory, `detectNpmrcLegacyAuthToken` in `bkit-postinstall.ts`). Never write `${VAR:-default}` anywhere pnpm reads — pnpm does not parse the POSIX fallback and sends no auth (asserted by the B6 block in `bkit-preflight.test.ts`). Diagnose a 401 against `registry.npmjs.org` by checking the project `.npmrc` for any `${VAR}` line first.

summary: `bkit install` must record `canonicalHashes` on first install, not only after upgrade
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Rule:** `runCoreModule` postDispatch (`.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/core.ts`) writes `.bkit/version` via `writeBkitVersion` (JSON) and fills `canonicalHashes` from the files written in this run (`ws.writes`). A path with no recorded hash makes `isConsumerModified` return `true` (`.bkit/core/engine/install/version-file.ts:141`), so with no hashes every existing file looks consumer-modified: upgrade reports a conflict instead of applying a changed template (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/upgrade.ts:230`) and uninstall preserves owned files instead of deleting them (`skip-unknown`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/uninstall.ts:392`).
- **Idempotence:** the write happens only when the pinned version changed or new canonical entries were recorded — a repeat install produces zero writes.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-131, `.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/core.ts` (`runCoreModule` postDispatch), `.bkit/core/engine/install/version-file.ts` (`writeBkitVersion`)
rootCause: Upgrade and uninstall compare files against `canonicalHashes`; an install that records none makes every file look consumer-modified, so upgrade turns every template change into a conflict and uninstall deletes nothing it owns.
remediation: Every code path that writes `.bkit/version` uses `writeBkitVersion` and populates `canonicalHashes` — never a plain-text version write.

summary: PR `statusCheckRollup` stays empty when `[skip ci]` is HEAD on push
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** PR opens with no Actions runs — `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returns empty, so nothing verifies the PR.
- **Root cause:** GitHub suppresses both `pull_request` and `push` runs when the HEAD commit message contains `[skip ci]` (or `[skip actions]`). bkit pushes `[skip ci]` commits mid-workflow by design, so whenever one is HEAD when the PR opens or the final push lands, no CI fires.
- **Fix or rule:** The CI-Dispatch Gate (`.bkit/workflows.md` § CI-Dispatch Gate) runs after each workflow's final CI-triggering push: it asserts the HEAD subject carries no skip token, polls `statusCheckRollup` for a bkit CI run on the exact pushed HEAD, self-heals once with a clean empty `re-trigger` commit, and ends with a named verdict (`dispatched` / `self-healed` / `no-ci` / `unresolved`). Ship squash-merges with `gh pr merge --body ""` so no skip token reaches the squash subject.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-146, #261, `.bkit/workflows.md` § CI-Dispatch Gate, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-build.md` Step 18, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md` Step 10, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-ship.md` Step 10
rootCause: GitHub suppresses `pull_request` and `push` runs when the HEAD commit message contains `[skip ci]` / `[skip actions]`; bkit pushes such commits mid-workflow by design.
remediation: Rely on the CI-Dispatch Gate after the final CI-triggering push (HEAD-subject assertion + poll + one clean `re-trigger` self-heal + named verdict); squash-merge with an empty body.

summary: `bkit install` dispatch is NOT transactional — a mid-dispatch failure leaves earlier modules' files written; re-run install to complete
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** A failure mid-dispatch (after some modules wrote) leaves those modules' files on disk and `.bkit/version` not re-pinned, so the consumer tree is a partial install.
- **Root cause:** Dispatch writes module files directly to their destinations and is not atomic across modules; `.bkit-staging/` is only a per-run scratch area for derived files (e.g. `opencode.json`), cleaned by `discardAllStaging()` in a `finally` after every dispatch (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/install.ts:43-60`). No atomic-rename staging primitive exists.
- **Fix or rule:** Do not rely on a zero-overwrite guarantee. Recover a partial install by re-running `bkit install` (idempotent). `.bkit/version` is written last in core's `postDispatch`, only after all modules succeed. Making install transactional would be a new per-module design, not a fix.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A4, DE-9, #255, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/install.ts` (staging scratch area)
rootCause: Dispatch writes module files directly to their destinations; `.bkit-staging/` is only a per-run scratch area for derived files, cleaned by `discardAllStaging()` (`install.ts` staging comment). No atomic-rename staging primitive exists.
remediation: Do not rely on a zero-overwrite guarantee. Recover a partial install by re-running `bkit install` (idempotent). `.bkit/version` is written last in core's `postDispatch`, only after all modules succeed.

summary: Sentinel-file cleanup must bracket the write — stale sentinels cause false Failure Path
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** After manually resolving a `git rebase` conflict outside the workflow, re-invoking `/bkit-build` or `/bkit-debug` immediately routes to the Failure Path even though the rebase is complete.
- **Root cause:** `bkit-build.md` / `bkit-debug.md` Step 2 — Worktree Setup `touch .rebase-failed` sentinel is never removed on success or retry. The sub-step 3a existence check fires on the stale file from the prior failed run.
- **Fix or rule:** Bracket every sentinel with explicit cleanup: (1) `rm -f` at the START of the bash block that writes the sentinel (clears stale-from-prior-run before any new attempt), and (2) `rm -f` in the Failure Path step after the sentinel is no longer needed. Pattern: create-write only inside the failure branch; delete-unconditionally at start of each attempt and at Failure Path exit. See `bkit-build.md` / `bkit-debug.md` Step 2 — Worktree Setup bash block.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** build-challenge
- **Related:** BAR-155, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-build.md`, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md`
rootCause: `bkit-build.md` / `bkit-debug.md` Step 2 — Worktree Setup `touch .rebase-failed` sentinel is never removed on success or retry. The sub-step 3a existence check fires on the stale file from the prior failed run.
remediation: Bracket every sentinel with explicit cleanup: (1) remove it at the START of each attempt that may write it (clears stale-from-prior-run before any new attempt), and (2) remove it on the Failure Path exit once it is no longer needed. Pattern: create only inside the failure branch; delete unconditionally at start of each attempt and at Failure Path exit. Implemented in `bkit worktrees` setup (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/worktrees.ts:431-435`), `bkit branches` rebase `--sentinel` (`branches.ts:1340`), the Failure Path sentinel sweep (`SENTINELS`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/workflows.ts:93,222-232`), and ship Step 1 (`.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-ship.md:161`).

summary: Multi-section output format — EOF-append landing section must be last
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** Agent appends gap findings at EOF of output file; entries land inside `## Notes` instead of `## Identified Gaps Log`, breaking downstream consumer parsing.
- **Root cause:** `bkit-build-plan-verify.md` Output format had `## Identified Gaps Log` in the middle of a six-section skeleton. The Fix 1b `echo {finding} >> {output}` directive appends at EOF, which is after `## Notes` (the last section). Downstream gap-remediate consumers grep for `## Identified Gaps Log` and find gaps mixed into Notes.
- **Fix or rule:** When an agent uses flat-append-at-EOF for a specific section, that section MUST be last in the Output format skeleton. Reorder so the append-target section is last. Same reason `bkit-build-challenge-tests.md`'s `## Bugs Discovered` must come after `## Blockers`.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** build-challenge
- **Related:** BAR-155, `.bkit/core/prompts/bkit-build-plan-verify.md`, `.bkit/core/prompts/bkit-build-challenge-tests.md`
rootCause: `bkit-build-plan-verify.md` Output format had `## Identified Gaps Log` in the middle of a six-section skeleton. The Fix 1b `echo {finding} >> {output}` directive appends at EOF, which is after `## Notes` (the last section). Downstream gap-remediate consumers grep for `## Identified Gaps Log` and find gaps mixed into Notes.
remediation: When an agent uses flat-append-at-EOF for a specific section, that section MUST be last in the Output format skeleton. Reorder so the append-target section is last. Same reason `bkit-build-challenge-tests.md`'s `## Bugs Discovered` must come after `## Blockers`.

summary: Deep containment is canonical for ownership-mixed JSON; MCP configs own one `mcpServers` entry
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Rule:** The template JSON tree IS bkit's declared scope. `deepContains(template, consumer)` checks every template leaf path is present and equal in the consumer; consumer keys outside the template tree are never touched.
- **Write path:** `writeTier2JsonContained` — dest absent → write template as-is; present and contained → no-op; not contained → `deepMergeJson(existing, template)` (template wins on conflict); malformed → throw.
- **Drift:** `detectTier2JsonDrift` advisory fires when `deepContains` fails — drift is checked on key presence and value, not only on `canonicalHashes`.
- **MCP configs:** `.mcp.json` / `.cursor/mcp.json` are the exception — `reconcileMcpJson` (`.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/claude.ts`) owns only bkit's tracker entry under `mcpServers`: install and upgrade reset that whole entry and keep every other server and its order, a malformed file stops install, and uninstall removes the entry only while it is identical to the template's (`MCP_JSON_RELPATHS`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/uninstall.ts`).
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** critical
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-167, DE-18, `.bkit/core/engine/install/write.ts` (`deepContains`, `writeTier2JsonContained`), `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/uninstall.ts` (`stripTier2JsonScope`), `.bkit/core/engine/checks/before/files.ts` (`detectTier2JsonDrift`), `.bkit/shared/.claude/settings.json`, `.bkit/shared/.cursor/hooks.json`
rootCause: Holding two copies of each bkit-owned value lets one go stale undetected. Containment makes the template tree itself the scope — one copy, checked directly.
remediation: Write ownership-mixed JSON with `writeTier2JsonContained`; detect drift with `deepContains` / `detectTier2JsonDrift`. MCP configs: `reconcileMcpJson`, never containment.

summary: Manifest `format` must match the writer install actually calls, not the intended ownership
description:
- **Symptom:** `bkit check` / `bkit uninstall` apply the wrong strip/delete strategy to a file whose manifest `format` names an intended ownership model instead of the writer install calls — e.g. an entry classed `markered-text` for a file written whole-file makes uninstall try to strip a managed block that never existed.
- **Root cause:** Uninstall and check dispatch on the manifest `format` (`.bkit/core/engine/install/manifest.ts`), not on the writer, so a `format` set to intent rather than the actual install function picks the wrong mechanism.
- **Fix:** Set manifest `format` to the install function actually called: `writeTier1` → `byte-equal-text`; `writeTier2` → `markered-text`; `writeTier2JsonContained` → `json`. MCP configs (`.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`) are `json` written by `reconcileMcpJson`; uninstall special-cases them via `MCP_JSON_RELPATHS`. When an install strategy changes, update the module code and the manifest entry in the same change.
- **Type:** incident
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-167, `.bkit/core/engine/install/manifest.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/index.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/write.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/uninstall.ts`
rootCause: Uninstall and check dispatch on the manifest `format`, not on the writer; a `format` set to the intended ownership model rather than the actual install function picks the wrong strip/delete mechanism.
remediation: Set manifest `format` to the writer actually called: `writeTier1` → `byte-equal-text`, `writeTier2` → `markered-text`, `writeTier2JsonContained` → `json` (MCP configs: `json` via `reconcileMcpJson`, special-cased in uninstall by `MCP_JSON_RELPATHS`). Change module code and manifest entry together.

summary: malformed-JSON destination must throw, not silently overwrite
description:
- **Symptom:** `writeTier2JsonContained` silently overwrote a malformed-JSON destination file with the template, destroying any consumer content that was unrecoverable as JSON.
- **Root cause:** Catch branch treated parse failure as "absent" and wrote the template wholesale — same as a fresh install. A corruption or partial write leaving invalid JSON would be permanently lost without warning.
- **Fix:** Throw `[bkit] <path> is malformed JSON — fix manually before running bkit install` when destination exists but fails JSON.parse. Matches the `malformed-package-json` blocker discipline. Fresh install (file absent) path is unchanged.
- **Type:** incident
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-167, KN-8, `.bkit/core/engine/install/write.ts` (`writeTier2JsonContained`)
rootCause: Catch branch treated parse failure as "absent" and wrote the template wholesale — same as a fresh install. A corruption or partial write leaving invalid JSON would be permanently lost without warning.

summary: Workflow state is append-only `status.jsonl` under `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/`; it reaches `dev` only via squash-merge
description:
- **Category:** workflow
- **Rule:** Workflow state lives in `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl` — append-only NDJSON (one event per line; prior lines never mutated), folded to derive current state. Canonical reducer `.bkit/core/engine/ledgers/status.ts` (`fold`). Workflows only; agents MUST NOT read or write it.
- **Placement:** `build` / `debug` write and commit it on `feat/{FID}` via the per-step commits — NO mid-lifecycle `dev` push; state reaches `dev` once, at ship's PR squash-merge. `design` / `plan` do the same on a throwaway `feat/{FID}`; status and generated docs reach `dev` together via the Close-Workflow squash-merge (`docs({FID}): {phase} DONE`). `ship` Steps 1-8 commit on `feat/{FID}`; Steps 9-13 append to dev's copy, and ship's close commit + push is the legitimate `dev` landing.
- **Merge safety:** `docs/plans/**/status.jsonl merge=union` in `.gitattributes` — both branches' lines concatenate; the reader de-dupes on `(workflow, step, parentSha, at)` and orders by `at`.
- **Mechanism:** `parentSha` is captured at step START via `git rev-parse HEAD`, before the step's commit.
- **Type:** rule
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-187, BAR-183, BAR-184, `.bkit/workflows.md` § `status.jsonl` — workflow state SoT, `.bkit/core/engine/ledgers/status.ts`
remediation: Derive state by folding `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl`; never push status to `dev` mid-lifecycle.

summary: Upgrade bkit with `bkit upgrade --latest`, never `pnpm update @cbartens/bkit` — a caret `^X.Y.Z` specifier is expected
description:
- **Canonical:** same lesson as `kn-core-4-pnpm-update-cbartens-bkit-narrows-the-manifest-range-to-a` — maintain that entry, not this one.
- **Category:** install / consumer-upgrade
- **Rule:** `bkit upgrade --latest` bumps via `pnpm add -D @cbartens/bkit@<target>` and re-renders managed files (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/upgrade.ts:593-598`); the caret range pnpm saves is expected. Do not hand-restore a broader range; never upgrade with `pnpm update` / `pnpm add` alone (`.bkit/install.md` § Upgrade).
- **Type:** rule
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** consumer-friction
- **Related:** BAR-155 comment 2026-05-12, BAR-189
rootCause: `bkit upgrade --latest` runs `pnpm add -D @cbartens/bkit@<target>`, which saves a caret range at the new version; a pnpm-only bump skips the managed-file resync.
remediation: Upgrade with `bkit upgrade --latest`; keep the caret specifier; never stop at `pnpm add` / `pnpm update` alone.

summary: Server-side CI is the only quality gate; agent self-verification is informational, not authoritative
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** Debug-loop subagent declares `Verdict: PASS` after `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test --filter='...[origin/dev]'`, then CI fails on `test:integration` / `test:e2e` against the same SHA. Loop closes "successfully" but the underlying failure persists; multiple iterations push status JSON without ever fixing anything.
- **Root cause:** Agent-local verify can only run what's runnable in the agent context. Integration tests need real Supabase + env vars; E2E needs a deployed Vercel preview — neither is available locally. Subagent PASS verdict is structurally narrower than CI PASS. Treating subagent verdict as a gate creates a false-confidence loop.
- **Fix or rule:** Single source of truth for "merge-ready" is the consumer's CI run. Agent-local verify exists to catch trivially broken code before push (typecheck, unit). Subagent PASS means "didn't make it worse on the things I can see locally" — never "ready to merge." When designing CI gates, prefer server-side enforcement (e.g., adding `test:integration` to partial CI on push to dev) over expanding agent verify suites. Bkit ci.yml template ships the structural gate; agent prompts run the narrower verify with `--continue` to surface multiple failures per run.
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-192, BAR-195, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md` Step 6, `.bkit/core/prompts/bkit-debug-failure-remediate.md`, `.bkit/core/prompts/bkit-debug-failure-diagnose.md`, `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml`

Bkit ci.yml template ships the structural gate; agent prompts run the narrower verify with `--continue` to surface multiple failures per run.

summary: Turbo content-keyed cache replays across SHAs — declare external-state proxies in `inputs` to avoid ghost-greens
description:
- **Category:** testing
- **Symptom:** CI reports `test:integration` green on a dev push, but the same test would fail when actually executed because external state (DB migration, RLS policy, fixture data) changed since the cache was warmed. Turbo replays a stale-but-input-hash-matching result.
- **Root cause:** Turbo's remote cache key is content-keyed on declared `inputs`. Default `inputs` for a task covers source files in the package only. External dependencies — Supabase migration files, seed/fixture data, env templates — are invisible to the hash, so a change there does NOT bust the cache. PR-merge-to-dev typically replays the PR's cached green correctly; concurrent migrations from another PR landing on dev between PR-CI and merge-CI are the failure mode.
- **Fix or rule:** For tasks that touch external state (`test:integration`, `test:e2e`), declare external-state proxies in the consumer's `turbo.json` task `inputs` — `supabase/migrations/**`, fixture files, env templates. Cache replay then only fires when inputs that affect the test outcome are truly unchanged. Defence in depth: bkit ci.yml template ships direct-push-to-dev detection that sets `TURBO_FORCE=1` (no PR ancestry → cache always busted). Manual escape hatch: `[force cache]` tag in commit message / PR title. The one residual ghost-green that no automation catches: direct edits to the dev DB without a migration file (out-of-band schema drift).
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-192, BAR-195, `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (Detect Direct Push step), consumer `turbo.json` `inputs` declaration
rootCause: Turbo's remote cache key is content-keyed on declared `inputs`. Default `inputs` for a task covers source files in the package only. External dependencies — Supabase migration files, seed/fixture data, env templates — are invisible to the hash, so a change there does NOT bust the cache. PR-merge-to-dev typically replays the PR's cached green correctly; concurrent migrations from another PR landing on dev between PR-CI and merge-CI are the failure mode.
remediation: For tasks that touch external state (`test:integration`, `test:e2e`), declare external-state proxies in the consumer's `turbo.json` task `inputs` — `supabase/migrations/**`, fixture files, env templates. Cache replay then only fires when inputs that affect the test outcome are truly unchanged. Defence in depth: bkit ci.yml template ships direct-push-to-dev detection that sets `TURBO_FORCE=1` (no PR ancestry → cache always busted). Manual escape hatch: `[force cache]` tag in commit message / PR title. The one residual ghost-green that no automation catches: direct edits to the dev DB without a migration file (out-of-band schema drift).

summary: DB schema state persists across code rollback — reset required for schema-aware tests
description:
- **Category:** testing
- **Symptom:** Rolling code back to a known-good SHA leaves the linked dev database carrying migrations from the rolled-out range. Schema-aware tests (e.g. `cdc-schema-assurance`) compare live DB structure against code expectations and fail on the clean rolled-back tree because the DB is ahead of the code.
- **Root cause:** `git revert` rewinds the source tree only. Migrations applied during the rolled-out range stay materialised in the dev DB — there is no "unapply" for code-driven migrations. Any test that introspects the live schema sees columns / tables / RLS the code no longer declares.
- **Fix or rule:** Follow the shipped Dev rollback runbook (`.bkit/shared/docs/deployments.md` § Dev rollback runbook): revert the bad range locally (`git revert`, never `git reset` or force-push `dev`); reset the dev DB by dropping your app-managed schemas `CASCADE` and truncating the migration ledger (`psql "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" ...` for Supabase); push the revert so CI's `bkit-tests-migration` lane re-applies every migration on the reverted tree — never apply by hand (`.agents/rules.md` § Security & Data: Migrations); re-seed fixtures once the lane is green.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-192, BAR-195, `.bkit/shared/docs/deployments.md` (Dev rollback runbook)
rootCause: `git revert` rewinds the source tree only. Migrations applied during the rolled-out range stay materialised in the dev DB — there is no "unapply" for code-driven migrations — so schema-introspecting tests flag drift.
remediation: Follow `.bkit/shared/docs/deployments.md` § Dev rollback runbook: `git revert` the range (never `git reset` / force-push `dev`), drop app-managed schemas `CASCADE` + truncate the migration ledger, push the revert so `bkit-tests-migration` re-applies migrations (never apply by hand), then re-seed.

summary: `^chore:`-prefixed PR HEAD silently skips Vercel preview + demotes CI to partial — regression gate never fires
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** Debug loop closes "successfully"; `/bkit-ship` squash-merges; the regression `/bkit-debug` claimed to fix resurfaces. The Vercel preview for the PR HEAD was cancelled with `Ignored Build Step` and CI ran a reduced lane set — e2e skipped. The CI conclusion still reported `success` because skipped is not failure.
- **Root cause:** Two reinforcing mechanisms. (1) A `chore(...)` subject as PR HEAD: consumer Vercel projects commonly ship an `Ignored Build Step` regex `^chore:`, so Vercel cancels the preview and preview-dependent suites skip. (2) Skipped-step semantics: GitHub Actions reports `conclusion=success` when lanes were skipped, so a gate keyed on failed steps cannot tell "no test ran" from "all tests passed".
- **Fix or rule:** (1) **Debug remediation commits as `fix({FID}): {description}`.** Step 6 — Failure Remediate and Step 7 — Failure Remediate Soak commit through `bkit steps finish --message="fix({FID}): ..."` (`.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md:436,458`); Step 8 — Push Remediation pushes with no intermediate `chore` commit, so `fix(...)` is branch HEAD (Gate 8, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md:489`). (2) **Ship merge gate.** Step 10 — Merge Gate + Merge PR runs `bkit runs gate`, which asserts a run exists at the merge head, completed, not cancelled, and the `bkit-tests-check` capstone is present and green (codes 10-15); it refuses skipped lanes only for those named in `bkit.shipGateRequiredLanes` (code 16, opt-in) — `docs/deployments.md` merge-gate section. Ship Step 2's `ship-regression-guard` row is bookkeeping, not a prior-failed-step comparison.
- **Type:** post-mortem
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** critical
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-200, KN-11, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md` Steps 6–8 + Gate 8, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-ship.md` Step 10, `.bkit/workflows.md` § CI / Vercel commit tags
rootCause: Two reinforcing mechanisms. (1) A `chore(...)` subject as PR HEAD: consumer Vercel projects commonly ship an `Ignored Build Step` regex `^chore:`, so Vercel cancels the preview and CI's `decide` step downgrades to `partial` tier — Playwright/integration suites are skipped. (2) Skipped-step semantics: GitHub Actions reports the CI run `conclusion=success` even when half the steps were tier-capped out, so a gate keyed on failed steps cannot tell "no test ran" from "all tests passed".
remediation: Debug remediation commits as `fix({FID}): {description}` and pushes it as branch HEAD (debug Steps 6-8). Ship Step 10's `bkit runs gate` asserts the capstone is green at the merge head; to refuse a skipped lane, name it in `bkit.shipGateRequiredLanes` (code 16).

summary: Playwright artifacts via `actions/upload-artifact` are invisible to `gh run view --log-failed` — fetch separately
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** `@bkit-debug-failure-diagnose` on an e2e failure reads `debug-logs-ci-{DEBUG_ATTEMPT}.md` and sees only the bare `pnpm test:e2e` exit code + final summary line ("3 failed"). Per-test stack traces, expected/received diffs, console-capture, screenshots, video, and `trace.zip` are all missing. Diagnose attempts cycle on the same hypothesis (test runner config / Playwright version) because the actual failure context never reaches the agent.
- **Root cause:** `gh run view --log-failed` returns the stdout/stderr of the failing GHA step only. Playwright's rich failure artifacts (per-test output under `test-results/`, the HTML viewer under `playwright-report/`, embedded traces / screenshots / videos) are uploaded via `actions/upload-artifact@v4` in a _separate_ GHA step that runs `if: failure() && steps.e2e.conclusion == 'failure'`. Artifacts live behind the `gh run download -n <name>` API and never appear in `--log-failed` output.
- **Fix or rule:** Three coupled pieces:
  1. **Consumer-side template** — `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (copy to `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` and own it) ships `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts` immediately after `bkit-stub:e2e`. Stub body uploads `playwright-report/` + `test-results/` to an artifact named `playwright-report`, 14-day retention, `if-no-files-found: ignore`. Both stubs must be uncommented together — `bkit-stub:e2e` without `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts` produces no fetchable artifact; `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts` without `bkit-stub:e2e` produces nothing to upload.
  2. **Fetch path** — the e2e artifact fetch runs as a `context-fetch` block declared in `.agents/context.md` (mechanism at `.agents/context.md:17`), executed by debug Step 4 — Fetch Context (`.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md:572`).
  3. **Artifact name is a knob** — `E2E_ARTIFACT="${E2E_ARTIFACT:-playwright-report}"` (`.agents/context.md:135`). A consumer that renames the upload artifact must set `E2E_ARTIFACT` to match; otherwise the fetch comes back empty, and `if-no-files-found: ignore` keeps CI silent too.
- **Conditional gating chain:** e2e step gates on `should_run_full || needs_e2e` (`should_run_full` ← the `[force full]` marker; #291 renamed it from `should_run_e2e`). If neither fires (e.g. KN-26 scenario — `decide` demoted to `partial`), e2e step is `skipped`, `steps.e2e.conclusion != 'failure'`, upload step also skipped, no artifact. Symmetric with the BAR-200 ship-side regression gate that catches the upstream cause (skipped previously-failing step).
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-201, KN-26 (sibling — same milestone, closes both ends of the e2e-debug loop), `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md` Step 4 — Fetch Context, `.agents/context.md` (`E2E_ARTIFACT`), `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (`bkit-stub:e2e` + `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts`)
rootCause: `gh run view --log-failed` returns the stdout/stderr of the failing GHA step only. Playwright's rich failure artifacts (per-test output under `test-results/`, the HTML viewer under `playwright-report/`, embedded traces / screenshots / videos) are uploaded via `actions/upload-artifact@v4` in a _separate_ GHA step that runs `if: failure() && steps.e2e.conclusion == 'failure'`. Artifacts live behind the `gh run download -n <name>` API and never appear in `--log-failed` output.
remediation: Uncomment `bkit-stub:e2e` and `bkit-stub:e2e-artifacts` together in your own `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (copied from `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml`; bkit refreshes that reference copy on upgrade and CI never runs it), and keep the uploaded artifact name equal to `E2E_ARTIFACT` (default `playwright-report`) so the `.agents/context.md` fetch block finds it.

references: KN-23 (CI is the only authoritative gate — but only over the files it actually lints)
summary: Lint the artifacts you ship with the config you ship — bkit's own `lint:prose` must cover every shipped `.md`
description:
- **Category:** tooling
- **Rule:** bkit writes no `lint:prose` script to consumers. Core seeds only the `bkit:gate:*` names, add-if-missing (`seedCorePackageJsonScripts`); the tool scripts the gates chain (`lint:prose` among them) are the consumer's, listed in `.bkit/templates.md`, and the `gate-missing-called-scripts` advisory names any that are missing (`.bkit/core/engine/install/manifest.ts:200-215`). bkit's repo `lint:prose` (`package.json`) runs `bkit ci prose` over an explicit glob list: `.agents/*.md`, `.bkit/core/.bkit/*.md`, `.bkit/core/workflows/**`, `.bkit/core/prompts/**`, `.bkit/core/.agents/*.md`, `.bkit/shared/docs/**`, `.bkit/core/docs/**`, `.bkit/templates/**`, `docs/*.md`, root `*.md`. Any shipped prose outside that list can fail a consumer's prose gate while bkit stays green. Commit, push and CI all run the same `pnpm lint:prose`.
- **Keep:** fix canonical prose, never loosen the rule. Managed-block prose can only be fixed upstream — a consumer rewording it drifts a canonical file.
- **Vale config:** `.bkit/templates/.vale.ini` is a template: bkit never writes or overwrites a consumer's `.vale.ini`. A template change reaches consumers only as the refreshed reference copy in their `.bkit/templates/` (`bkit upgrade` lists changed paths); they merge it into their own copy. The template exempts `[**/docs/plans/**/*.md]` and `[**/.bkit/templates/**/*.md]` from slop/hedging/write-good rules. Vale merges `BasedOnStyles` across matching scopes and an empty `BasedOnStyles =` inherits rather than disables, so turn rules off with `<Style>.<Rule> = NO`. Prefix scope globs with `**/` so lint-staged's absolute paths match.
- **Type:** gotcha

summary: `grep -oP` PCRE lookbehind fails under `set -euo pipefail` on non-GNU environments
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** A `bkit-cloud.yml` step using `grep -oP '(?<=bkit:issue=#)\d+'` under `set -euo pipefail` exits with code 1 on a PR body that lacks the marker pattern. The whole step is aborted; the documented fallback (`feat/{FID}` branch extraction) and fail-safe `skip=true` path become dead code. The job shows RED instead of a clean no-op skip.
- **Root cause:** (1) `grep` exits 1 when the pattern has no match; `pipefail` propagates that exit code through the pipe; `set -e` aborts the script at the assignment line. (2) `grep -oP` relies on PCRE (`-P`), unavailable on BSD/macOS grep and some minimal CI runner images. On `ubuntu-latest` GNU grep has `-P` so it works today, but any runner-image change silently falls through to the branch fallback, which may resolve the wrong issue number if the branch slug and issue number diverge.
- **Fix or rule:** Two independent fixes applied together: (a) append `|| true` to each assignment so a no-match exit code does not abort the step — `ISSUE=$(... || true)`; (b) replace PCRE lookbehind with portable POSIX ERE: `grep -oE 'bkit:issue=#[0-9]+'  | sed 's/bkit:issue=#//'` (match the whole token, then strip the prefix with sed). This is robust across GNU grep, BSD grep, and minimal images. Pattern: NEVER use `grep -oP` in shipped CI YAML — always use `grep -oE` + `sed` for portability.

- **Severity:** high (breaks the auto-route fail-safe; any bkit:auto repo with a malformed/missing PR body marker hits a red job)

summary: `slop:delta` (`bkit ci slop`) scans `--head .` (live tree) against a clean base worktree — gitignored build output surfaces as phantom "added" findings
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** A consumer's `pnpm slop:delta` failed on hundreds of phantom "added" findings (707, all from `apps/web/.next/`) before anything shipped. The build output exists in the live tree but not in the base, so the gate read it as net-new slop and FAILed spuriously. After adding `**/.next/**` to the consumer's `slop-scan.config.json` ignores, net dropped to -1 and the gate passed.
- **Root cause:** Two compounding facts. (1) `slop-scan delta --base <wt> --head .` is asymmetric — the base is a detached `git worktree` (a fresh checkout: tracked files only, no untracked or gitignored build output), while `--head .` scans the real working tree (which has `.next/`, `.turbo/`, etc. from local builds). Any path present live but absent from the base checkout reads as added. (2) slop-scan respects only the **root** `.gitignore`, not nested ones; in a monorepo, build output ignored by a package-level `.gitignore` (e.g. `apps/web/.gitignore`) is never excluded. The shipped default ignores compounded it by being root-relative (`dist/**`, which matches only the repo root, not `apps/web/dist/` — confirmed: `dist/**` still flags the nested path, `**/dist/**` does not).
- **Fix or rule:** Ship depth-agnostic, monorepo-safe build-output ignores in the default `slop-scan.config.json` — `**/dist/**`, `**/coverage/**`, `**/node_modules/**`, `**/.next/**`, `**/.turbo/**` (`**/X/**` matches root and nested alike, so bkit's own tracked root `dist/` stays ignored). Never slop-scan build output. Residual: the `--head .`-vs-clean-worktree asymmetry makes any untracked or gitignored build artifact a latent false-positive source, so a consumer with other generated dirs (`.svelte-kit/`, `.nuxt/`, `out/`) still adds them to their own `slop-scan.config.json`. CI checks out a clean tree (no prior build) and never sees this; local pre-push on a built tree does.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high (both mechanisms — glob depth and root-only `.gitignore` — reproduced in isolation)
- **Severity:** medium (spurious local pre-push FAIL for any consumer with build artifacts in the tree; the consumer-side ignore unblocks immediately; never ships bad code)
- **Source:** consumer dogfood feedback
- **Related:** #226, `bkit ci slop` (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/ci/ci.ts`), `slop-scan.config.json`

summary: Host mirror writes reach `ws.writes` through `trackMirrorWrite`, not `installFile` — assert mirrors via the writeset or disk, and route any new mirror write through `trackMirrorWrite`
description: `installFile()` (`.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/core.ts:36`) only copies/transforms a file and returns a boolean; it never touches `ctx.ws.writes`. Every mirror renderer (`renderClaudeAgentsCommands`, `renderCursorAgentsCommands`, `renderOpencodeAgentsCommands`, `renderCodexAgentsSkills`) records each write AND each orphan delete with `trackMirrorWrite(ctx, rel, written)` (`core.ts:316`), so `bkit check` exits 1 on mirror content drift and dry-run/install writesets match.
rootCause: `installFile()` returns written/skipped; the writeset entry is pushed by the caller via `trackMirrorWrite` (`.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/core.ts:316`). A new mirror path that calls `installFile` without `trackMirrorWrite` is invisible to `bkit check` drift and to dry-run parity.
remediation: When adding a host mirror write or orphan prune, pair every `installFile` / `removeOrphans` hit with `trackMirrorWrite`. Tests may assert mirror paths through `ws.writes` (dry-run parity in `bkit-dry-run-parity.integration.test.ts`) or by `fs.readdirSync` on the destination; both see the same set.

summary: opencode spec churn — pin the probed version, not a naive next-digit bump
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** After upgrading opencode or updating `opencode.json`, agents fail to launch or plugin API calls are rejected with schema errors.
- **Root cause:** opencode's plugin spec, frontmatter fields (`reasoningEffort`, provider config shape), and command-file syntax change between releases without a stable semver contract. Naively bumping a version number or copying from release notes produces configs that may never have existed in the actual binary.
- **Fix or rule:** Probe the installed opencode binary for its supported field names and plugin API shape before updating `opencode.json`. Read `.opencode/opencode.json` against the opencode docs for the version that `opencode --version` reports. When in doubt, copy from a fresh `opencode init` output with that version, not from examples in issues or READMEs that may lag the release.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** medium (observed during #245 spike; spec drift confirmed across minor releases)
- **Severity:** normal
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #245, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/install.ts` (applyOpencodeAgent transform), `docs/plans/202606/logs/245-opencode-provider-host/spike-verdict.md`

remediation: Probe the installed opencode binary for its supported field names and plugin API shape before updating `opencode.json`. Read `.opencode/opencode.json` against the opencode docs for the version that `opencode --version` reports. summary: Retiring a file bkit wrote once and never updated does not reach consumer copies — `bkit-mode.sh` needs its own deletion advisory
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** After upgrading bkit to a version that no longer ships `.bkit/scripts/bkit-mode.sh`, every prior consumer still has the file on disk. The upgrade silently leaves the orphan in place. Worse, the file's shell-function shim (`bkit()`) is still sourced from `~/.zshrc` / `~/.bashrc`, causing a broken `source` error in every new terminal after the file is eventually deleted.
- **Root cause:** `.bkit/scripts/bkit-mode.sh` was written once when absent and never overwritten, so consumers edited it freely. When bkit stopped shipping it, nothing deleted or flagged the consumer copy.
- **Fix or rule:** A dropped owned file goes in `RETIRED_OWNED_FILES` (`.bkit/src/bkit-retire.ts`): deleted while it still matches its `canonicalHashes` entry, otherwise kept with an advisory naming the replacement. A once-written file the consumer is expected to edit — `bkit-mode.sh`, or a create-if-missing file (`.agents/context.md`, `.agents/skills.md`; never hashed) — needs an upgrade-migration advisory in its owning module that: (1) detects the orphan on disk with `fs.existsSync`, independent of any template or copy pass, (2) tells the consumer to delete the file, (3) names the shell-rc source line to remove (if applicable), and (4) points at the replacement. Implemented for `bkit-mode.sh` in `runClaudeModule` (`bkit-modules.ts`) as the `bkit-mode-sh-deletion-required` advisory. `COPY_EXCLUDE` keeps the `bkit-mode.sh` basename as a re-addition guard; it does not gate the advisory.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** critical (broken `source` call in every new shell = user-visible error)
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #245, KN-17, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts` (bkit-mode-sh-deletion-required advisory), `.bkit/src/bkit-retire.ts` (`RETIRED_OWNED_FILES`), DE-27

summary: Orphan-cleanup must be gated on replacement presence
description:
- **Category:** infra

summary: CI tool downloads flake on transient CDN blips — retry one-shot fetches, loop subcommand fetches
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** `bkit-tests` goes red on a transient network/CDN hiccup while downloading a CI tool (vale tarball, actionlint binary, opencode installer) — a one-off failure with no code cause; a re-run is green.
- **Root cause:** A one-shot `curl` with no retry dies on the first blip. For a fetch buried inside a tool subcommand (`vale sync` pulling styles) or a third-party installer script (`download-actionlint.bash` fetching the binary), there is no curl flag to harden — the bare invocation has no retry at all.
- **Fix or rule:** One-shot `curl` → add `--retry 3 --retry-all-errors` (needs curl ≥ 7.71; ubuntu-latest 8.x and the Debian Dockerfile base are clear). Fetch inside a subcommand / 3rd-party script → wrap in a 3× retry-loop that `exit 1`s loudly after the last attempt (never a bare loop that swallows a persistent outage). Applied to `ci.yml`, `.cursor/Dockerfile`, `bkit-cloud.yml` (own + template) and the `cloud.md` setup script. Do NOT "simplify" the loops back to a single call.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #236, `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml`, `.bkit/templates/.cursor/Dockerfile`
rootCause: A one-shot `curl` with no retry dies on the first blip. For a fetch buried inside a tool subcommand (`vale sync` pulling styles) or a third-party installer script (`download-actionlint.bash` fetching the binary), there is no curl flag to harden — the bare invocation has no retry at all.
remediation: One-shot `curl` → add `--retry 3 --retry-all-errors` (needs curl ≥ 7.71; ubuntu-latest 8.x and the Debian Dockerfile base are clear). summary: Post-install Phase 3 runs in BOTH install and check — detectors are read-only
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** n/a (design rule — not a bug)
- **Rule:** Phase 3 post-install re-detection runs unconditionally for `bkit install` and `bkit check` alike (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/install.ts:540`, not gated on `dryRun`). Every detector is read-only, so check emits the same advisory set install would emit against the same filesystem state.
- **Mechanism:** `runPostInstallCheck(preflightAdvisories, cwd, suppressed)` has no `dryRun` parameter (`.bkit/core/engine/checks/after/index.ts:341-345`). `dryRun` changes only banner wording and drift reporting. Zero-advisory runs print no banner (`formatChecklist([])` returns `""`).
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, DE-4, `.bkit/core/engine/checks/after/index.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/install.ts`
rootCause: `bkit check` must stay read-only. Every Phase 3 detector is read-only, so running them in check keeps install/check advisory parity with no side effects.
remediation: Expect Phase 3 advisories from both `bkit install` and `bkit check`. Never add a side-effecting detector to Phase 3 — it would break check's read-only contract. `runPostInstallCheck` has no `dryRun` parameter; do not reintroduce one to suppress check-mode output.

summary: pnpm 11 + per-install `minimumReleaseAge` gate OOMs Mend's Renovate microvm on large monorepos
description:
- **Category:** ci
- **Symptom:** On a large **pnpm 11** monorepo, every Mend-hosted Renovate job fails with `Status: FAILED / Error: kernel-out-of-memory` immediately after `Spawning pnpm install to create pnpm-lock.yaml` → `pnpm update --no-save <deps> --lockfile-only --recursive --ignore-scripts --ignore-pnpmfile`. Blocks **all** lockfile-touching PRs (every dependency PR + weekly `lockFileMaintenance`). CVE / `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` PRs are on a separate path and keep working.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #308, `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters, KN-CORE-10
rootCause: `kernel-out-of-memory` is a **physical** OOM (not a V8 heap limit). `pnpm update --lockfile-only` resolves the whole graph, and the pnpm-level `minimumReleaseAge` gate (in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) verifies publish timestamps for every lockfile entry (~1287) — the combined resolution + metadata footprint exceeds the microvm's RAM. The same verification passes in GHA CI / Vercel because those runners have far more memory. pnpm 11's lockfile regen is heavier than pnpm 10's. Note: `--lockfile-only` does NOT extract/link `node_modules`, so pnpm's worker pool (governed by `PNPM_WORKERS`) is barely engaged — the spike is resolution + release-age metadata, not worker concurrency.
remediation: The Renovate example `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5` (copy-and-own; bkit installs no updater and emits no install advisory for this) carries two Renovate-scoped mitigations: **(A)** `env: { PNPM_WORKERS: "1", PNPM_MAX_WORKERS: "1" }` — bounds pnpm's worker-pool memory; both vars are in Mend's `global:safeEnv` allow-list; may not clear a metadata-driven OOM. **(B)** `minimumReleaseAge: "7 days"` — freshness enforced in Renovate itself; security PRs bypass it. **(B) only clears the OOM once the consumer sets `minimumReleaseAge: 0` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`** — pnpm 11 defaults the gate to 1440, so DELETING the key leaves it active (and strips any `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`); only `0` short-circuits the per-entry check. Safe for `--frozen-lockfile`: pnpm does not record `minimumReleaseAge` in `pnpm-lock.yaml` `settings:`. Trade-off: Renovate-only freshness gates only what Renovate proposes. `PNPM_CONFIG_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE` cannot be set on Mend hosted (not in `global:safeEnv`; `allowedEnv` is admin-only). Headroom fix when the graph outgrows Mend's runner: the self-hosted example (KN-CORE-10). Rule: `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters (pnpm 11 on Mend's runner).

summary: Prettier forces blank lines around top-level `<!-- bkit:tracker -->` markers (unremovable at source); two-digit steps silently escape their list item
description:
- **Category:** tooling
- **Symptom:** `.bkit/core/workflows/*.md` carry blank lines around every `<!-- bkit:tracker ... -->` marker. Stripping them and running `pnpm format` puts them straight back (verified: 82 removed from `bkit-build.md` -> prettier re-added exactly 82, restoring the file byte-for-byte). The render strips the marker LINES but leaves the surrounding blanks, so the `.claude` / `.cursor` / `.opencode` command mirrors get doubled blank lines AND the single `> [!CAUTION]` execution-protocol blockquote is split into three separate blockquotes - only the first keeps the CAUTION admonition. `.claude/` etc are in `.prettierignore`, so nothing downstream cleans it up. Separately, under two-digit steps (`10.`) the step body silently escapes its list item.
- **Root cause:** Two independent prettier-markdown behaviours, split by marker indent. **(1) Top-level markers (indent 0, 158 of them):** prettier separates a block-level HTML node from an adjacent blockquote with a blank line and reverts any attempt to close the gap. NOT author style - unremovable at source. Exception: an html node directly after another html node on the very next line keeps its adjacency, which is why `github end` + `linear start` are the one pair that never gets separated. **(2) Indented markers (inside list items):** prettier PRESERVES whatever is there; blanks are author-written. But looseness is per-item and contagious - a list item is loose if it contains a blank line OR is followed by one, and prettier then propagates blank lines to EVERY block boundary inside that item. So ONE blank between step 9 and step 10 (nothing to do with markers) explodes blanks around every marker inside step 9. **(3) Escaped two-digit steps:** when a step number crosses `9.` -> `10.` the required content indent goes 3 -> 4. Body left at indent 3 is no longer part of the item; prettier prints the AST it actually parsed, dedenting the body to column 0 and stranding the `<!-- end -->` markers at indent 3. Step 10's body is not inside step 10 and the ordered list fragments.
- **Fix or rule:** Do NOT try to de-blank top-level markers at source - prettier reverts it; that damage can only be fixed render-side (collapse orphaned blanks when stripping a marker line). DO tighten indented markers: drop blanks inside marker-bearing list items AND the blanks BETWEEN their numbered steps (a tight list still renders each step on its own numbered line - this is not a wall of text). Gate any such sweep on an AST diff that normalises `spread`/`loose` away and compares everything else - blank-line edits can silently merge paragraphs. Two traps when automating: a body-boundary scan must be FENCE-AWARE (a `### heading` inside a ```comment block will otherwise terminate the scan mid-fence and corrupt the fence), and a marker predicate must match markers that sit AFTER a list bullet (`9. <!-- bkit:... -->`), not just at line start - missing that leaves the item loose and prettier re-adds everything. Applied 2026-07-15: indented blank-adjacent markers 124 -> 42, 143 blank lines removed, 6 escaped two-digit steps in `bkit-build.md` re-indented 3 -> 4; content verified identical (every text / inline-code / fenced-block / marker value, in document order) across all 8 files; 1 blank deliberately kept in `bkit-design.md` where removal merged a paragraph into a nested list.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** medium
- **Scope:** bkit-repo
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** `.bkit/core/workflows/*.md` (source of the `.claude`/`.cursor`/`.opencode` command mirrors); `.prettierignore` managed block; render-side blank-collapse fix still OPEN (the 158 top-level markers + the CAUTION split).
rootCause: Two independent prettier-markdown behaviours, split by marker indent. **(1) Top-level markers (indent 0, 158 of them):** prettier separates a block-level HTML node from an adjacent blockquote with a blank line and reverts any attempt to close the gap. NOT author style - unremovable at source. Exception: an html node directly after another html node on the very next line keeps its adjacency, which is why `github end` + `linear start` are the one pair that never gets separated. **(2) Indented markers (inside list items):** prettier PRESERVES whatever is there; blanks are author-written. But looseness is per-item and contagious - a list item is loose if it contains a blank line OR is followed by one, and prettier then propagates blank lines to EVERY block boundary inside that item. So ONE blank between step 9 and step 10 (nothing to do with markers) explodes blanks around every marker inside step 9. **(3) Escaped two-digit steps:** when a step number crosses `9.` -> `10.` the required content indent goes 3 -> 4. Body left at indent 3 is no longer part of the item; prettier prints the AST it actually parsed, dedenting the body to column 0 and stranding the `<!-- end -->` markers at indent 3. Step 10's body is not inside step 10 and the ordered list fragments.
remediation: Do NOT try to de-blank top-level markers at source - prettier reverts it; that damage can only be fixed render-side (collapse orphaned blanks when stripping a marker line). DO tighten indented markers: drop blanks inside marker-bearing list items AND the blanks BETWEEN their numbered steps (a tight list still renders each step on its own numbered line - this is not a wall of text). Gate any such sweep on an AST diff that normalises `spread`/`loose` away and compares everything else - blank-line edits can silently merge paragraphs. Two traps when automating: a body-boundary scan must be FENCE-AWARE (a `### heading` inside a ```comment block will otherwise terminate the scan mid-fence and corrupt the fence), and a marker predicate must match markers that sit AFTER a list bullet (`9. <!-- bkit:... -->`), not just at line start - missing that leaves the item loose and prettier re-adds everything. Applied 2026-07-15: indented blank-adjacent markers 124 -> 42, 143 blank lines removed, 6 escaped two-digit steps in `bkit-build.md` re-indented 3 -> 4; content verified identical (every text / inline-code / fenced-block / marker value, in document order) across all 8 files; 1 blank deliberately kept in `bkit-design.md` where removal merged a paragraph into a nested list.

summary: `parseInt("")` returns NaN — guard version file reads
description:
- **Category:** backend
- **Symptom:** A zero-byte or whitespace-only `.bkit/version` causes `detectBkitVersionMajorDowngrade` to emit a misleading advisory containing `"NaN"` in the detect text.
- **Root cause:** `parseInt("", 10) === NaN`; `NaN <= installingMajor` evaluates to `false`, so the `return null` guard is skipped and the advisory is emitted with a `NaN` major.
- **Fix or rule:** After trimming, guard with `if (!onDisk) return null;` before calling `parseInt`. Follow with `Number.isNaN(onDiskMajor)` check for any further NaN-producing inputs. Apply the same defence to any version-parsing that reads arbitrary on-disk files.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, `.bkit/core/engine/checks/before/version.ts` (`detectBkitVersionMajorDowngrade`)

summary: Use execFileSync over execSync when the argument comes from a variable
description:
- **Category:** security
- **Symptom:** `execSync(\`vercel env ls ${env}\`)` passes type-checked TypeScript, but at runtime nothing prevents shell metacharacters from a future refactor or JS caller from executing unintended commands.
- **Root cause:** `execSync` with a template string passes the full command to the shell; shell metacharacter interpretation applies. Even a TypeScript union type (`"preview" | "production"`) is erased at runtime.
- **Fix or rule:** Use `execFileSync("vercel", ["env", "ls", env])` to bypass shell interpretation entirely. Add a runtime guard (`if (env !== "preview" && env !== "production") return "unknown"`) for defence in depth. Apply to all `execSync` calls that interpolate any variable, even TypeScript-typed ones.
- **Type:** pattern
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, `docs/security.md` § Shell Injection

summary: dist/ staleness — `pnpm build` must run before push for `.bkit/core/engine/**/*.ts` changes
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** Local pre-commit/pre-push hooks pass green (`typecheck`, `test`, `format:check`, `lint:slop`, `lint:prose`) but CI's `run-tests` job fails on "Verify dist/ is fresh" with a diff showing `dist/*.js` missing latest source changes.
- **Root cause:** Pre-commit/pre-push hooks invoke `tsc --noEmit` (typecheck only) and `vitest run` (no compile) — do NOT run `pnpm build`. CI runs `pnpm build && git diff --exit-code dist/` to ensure shipped artefacts match source. Source-only commits leave `dist/` stale; CI catches it.
- **Fix or rule:** Any TS edit under `.bkit/core/engine/**/*.ts` MUST be accompanied by `pnpm build && git add dist/` in the same commit. Hook-level enforcement landed in BAR-131 PR #7 — `.husky/pre-push` runs `pnpm bkit:check:dist` (bkit-repo only; `bkit install` never writes `.husky/pre-push`), so a stale dist/ fails the push locally rather than waiting for CI. Fired twice before enforcement: BAR-141 PR #5 (commit `edbd891` broke, `7ab6bff` fixed) and BAR-131/139/142 PR #7 (~2.6k lines of new TS across 13 files with zero dist/ updates; required a separate rebuild commit).

- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, BAR-131, PR #5, PR #7, commits `edbd891` (broke), `7ab6bff` (fixed), `.husky/pre-push`, `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml`, `docs/deployments.md` § `dist/` commit policy

summary: Ownership-mixed JSON is Tier-2 deep containment (MCP configs: bkit's tracker entry only) — never Tier-1 full-overwrite
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Rule:** JSON files holding both bkit-owned and consumer-owned keys (`.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, …) are Tier 2, written via deep containment — `writeTier2JsonContained` in `.bkit/core/engine/install/write.ts`. The template JSON tree is bkit's scope; consumer keys outside it are never touched. Never write these files as Tier-1 full-overwrite. Exception: MCP configs (`.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`) — bkit owns only its tracker entry under `mcpServers`; `reconcileMcpJson` (`.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/index.ts`) resets that entry and keeps every other server and its order.
- **Detail:** `kn-17-deep-containment-is-canonical-for-ownership-mixed-json`.
- **Type:** rule
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** `.bkit/core/engine/install/write.ts`, `.bkit/shared/.claude/settings.json`, `.bkit/shared/.cursor/hooks.json`
rootCause: Tier-1 full-overwrite replaces the whole file, so consumer-added keys in an ownership-mixed JSON file are lost on every install and upgrade.
remediation: Register ownership-mixed JSON as Tier 2 and write it with `writeTier2JsonContained`; never Tier-1. MCP configs go through `reconcileMcpJson`, which owns only bkit's tracker entry under `mcpServers`.

summary: Read `.bkit/version` via `readBkitVersion().pinnedVersion` — never raw `readFileSync().trim()`
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Rule:** `.bkit/version` is JSON (`pinnedVersion` + `canonicalHashes`). A raw `readFileSync(...).trim()` yields the whole JSON blob, and a semver comparison on it (`semverLte`) silently returns false. Read it via `readBkitVersion(path).pinnedVersion` (or `parseBkitVersion(content).pinnedVersion`) in `.bkit/core/engine/install/version-file.ts` — it parses JSON, falls back to plain-text semver, and returns null for absent or empty files.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-131, `.bkit/core/engine/install/version-file.ts` (`readBkitVersion`, `parseBkitVersion`)
rootCause: The version file is JSON; treating its raw contents as a semver string makes every comparison silently false.
remediation: Always read `.bkit/version` via `readBkitVersion(path).pinnedVersion` or `parseBkitVersion(content).pinnedVersion`; never raw `readFileSync(...).trim()`.

summary: GitHub MCP / `gh` 401 immediately after token rotation
description:
- **Category:** integrations
- **Symptom:** 401 from the GitHub MCP server or `gh` despite a freshly-rotated, valid, correctly-scoped PAT in `.bkit/.env`.
- **Root cause:** the MCP server captures `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` at process launch, so a mid-session rotation leaves it holding the dead token. Non-interactive shells also miss direnv (`.envrc` re-sources only on interactive prompt/cd), so the shell keeps a stale exported value. For `gh` specifically, an exported `GH_TOKEN` (legacy or manual) overrides the keyring — see KN-CORE-8.
- **Fix or rule:** restart/reload the MCP server after rotating the token; for one-off CLI prefix `direnv exec . gh …`. Confirm the live `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` matches `.bkit/.env` before chasing PAT scopes/approval.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** #137

summary: Mend hosted Renovate OOMs on the 3 GB microvm — copy the self-hosted `bkit-renovate.yml` example onto `ubuntu-latest`
description:
- **Symptom:** Every Mend-hosted Renovate job on a large pnpm-11 monorepo fails `kernel-out-of-memory` (3.0/3.0 GB) during `pnpm update --lockfile-only`, blocking all dependency PRs; the worker-cap + Renovate-side `minimumReleaseAge` (KN-41) mitigate but do not guarantee headroom as the graph grows.
- **Related:** KN-41, KN-CORE-3, KN-CORE-5, KN-CORE-8, #308, #123, #325, `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters
rootCause: Mend Community Cloud runs Renovate in a fixed ~3 GB hosted microvm; pnpm-11 lockfile resolution + release-age metadata for a large graph exceeds physical RAM. The constraint is runner size, not config — CI / Vercel (>> 3 GB) never OOM.
remediation: Copy `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-renovate.yml` (renovatebot/github-action at a pinned SHA, `ubuntu-latest` ~16 GB) and own it — bkit installs no updater; edit `runs-on` in the copy. It reuses the same `renovate.json5`. Correctness points (`docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters): (1) platform auth is a repo secret `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT: Contents / Pull requests / Workflows / Commit statuses / Issues read-write, Dependabot alerts read), NEVER `GITHUB_TOKEN` (its PRs do not trigger CI, so required checks and automerge never fire); (2) the daily cron wakes the bot while `renovate.json5` `schedule` gates normal PRs and `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` bypasses both — never narrow the cron to weekly; (3) suspend the Mend App for the repo (GitHub UI, no `gh api`) or both open `renovate/*` PRs — nothing detects this for you; (4) keep your copied `bkit-renovate.yml` OUT of `ignorePaths` so its own action pins refresh; (5) repo settings: Dependency graph + Dependabot alerts ON, Dependabot security + version updates OFF; (6) org-owned tokens cannot read the owner email — set the Actions variable `RENOVATE_GIT_AUTHOR`. OOM mitigations stay as they are.

summary: Opaque 401 from `pnpm install` — one unset `${VAR}` makes pnpm ignore the entire `.npmrc`
description:
- **Symptom:** `pnpm install` (local, CI, or Vercel build) fails with a generic 401 against `registry.npmjs.org` — NOT against `npm.pkg.github.com`. The error reads as a plain auth failure with no "token missing" wording, and `@cbartens/bkit` is reported as not found.
- **Root cause:** pnpm v7.20+ silently discards the ENTIRE `.npmrc` the moment any `${VAR}` in it resolves to an unset env var. The `@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` scope mapping is dropped, pnpm falls back to npmjs.org, which has no `@cbartens/bkit` → 401. The unset variable is almost always `BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL`. Separately, pnpm does NOT parse POSIX fallback syntax: `${VAR:-default}` sends no auth at all and 401s — use bare `${VAR}` only.
- **Fix or rule:** bkit's project `.npmrc` carries ONLY the registry mapping (`@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`) — no `${VAR}` line — and the token goes into pnpm's user-level config via `pnpm config set "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL"` on every surface that runs `pnpm install` (KN-CORE-7, `docs/deployments.md` § Consumer CI auth). The trap only bites a project `.npmrc` that still carries an `${VAR}` auth line: delete that line (`npmrc-legacy-authtoken` advisory, `detectNpmrcLegacyAuthToken` in `bkit-postinstall.ts`). Never write `${VAR:-default}` anywhere pnpm reads — pnpm does not parse the POSIX fallback and sends no auth (asserted by the B6 block in `bkit-preflight.test.ts`). Diagnose a 401 against `registry.npmjs.org` by checking the project `.npmrc` for any `${VAR}` line first.

- **Severity:** normal
- **Related:** KN-CORE-7, `.npmrc`, `package.json`, `security.md`
