summary: GitHub Apps & CI integrations read config from the DEFAULT branch — land config on `main` before activating
description: A newly added integration config (`renovate.json5`, `dependabot.yml`, a branch-protection-scoped check) appears inert, or the App's onboarding PR opens against the wrong base / ungrouped, because the file was committed on a feature or integration branch but not yet merged to the default branch.
rootCause: GitHub Apps and most CI integrations resolve their configuration from the repository's DEFAULT branch at install/scan time, not from the branch where the file was committed. bkit consumers gate the default branch to PRs-from-integration-branch-only, so the config must travel through to the default branch before the integration can see it. Activating the App first makes it scan a branch that has no config yet.
remediation: Copy the updater example (`.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5` or `.bkit/templates/.github/dependabot.yml`) and own it — bkit installs neither. Land it on the default branch FIRST (integration branch → default), THEN install the Renovate App at https://github.com/apps/renovate (no `gh api` equivalent). Same ordering for Dependabot and any default-branch-scoped integration. Renovate keeps reading config from the default branch for ongoing edits too: the example's `useBaseBranchConfig: "merge"` honours `dev`-side edits for dev-targeted runs, but that option is itself read from the default branch and needs one merge there first. Rule: `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters.

summary: Upgrade bkit with `bkit upgrade --latest`, never `pnpm update @cbartens/bkit` — a caret `^X.Y.Z` specifier is the expected result, not a narrowing
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** After a package-manager bump, `package.json` reads `"@cbartens/bkit": "^X.Y.Z"` at the new version and an agent tries to restore a broader range, or a bare `pnpm update` / `pnpm add` leaves managed files stale.
- **Root cause:** `bkit upgrade --latest` bumps by running `pnpm add -D @cbartens/bkit@<target>` (`-w` in a pnpm workspace root) and then re-renders through the new binary (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/upgrade.ts:593-598`); pnpm saves that as a caret range, which still admits every later release of the same major. A bump through pnpm alone refreshes the package without resyncing managed files (`.bkit/install.md` § Upgrade).
- **Fix or rule:** Upgrade with `bkit upgrade --latest` (or `--to=<version>`). Leave the caret specifier pnpm writes; do not hand-restore a broader range. Never stop at `pnpm add` / `pnpm update`.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.bkit/install.md` § Upgrade
rootCause: `bkit upgrade --latest` runs `pnpm add -D @cbartens/bkit@<target>`, which saves a caret range at the new version; that range still admits later releases of the same major. A pnpm-only bump skips the managed-file resync.
remediation: Upgrade with `bkit upgrade --latest` (or `--to=<version>`); keep the caret specifier pnpm writes; never stop at `pnpm add` / `pnpm update` alone.

summary: Renovate's tag→SHA pinning ignores `enabled: false` — keep Renovate off a file via `ignorePaths`
description:
- **Category:** integrations
- **Symptom:** Renovate repeatedly opens a `chore(deps): Pin dependencies` PR pinning the `uses:` action tags of a workflow fenced only by a packageRule `matchFileNames` + `enabled: false`. Closing it — even with the branch deleted — brings it back on the next scan.
- **Root cause:** `enabled: false` suppresses _version updates_, but the `github-actions` manager still SCANS the file and Renovate's tag→SHA `pinDigests` (enabled globally for github-actions) is applied anyway — so the Pin PR keeps getting created.
- **Fix or rule:** List the file in `ignorePaths` — Renovate then does not scan it at all, the only thing that stops the pinning; `enabled: false` is NOT sufficient. The shipped example (`.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`) ignores `**/node_modules/**`, `**/dist/**`, `**/build/**`, `.bkit/templates/**` and `.agents/skills/**`; workflows a consumer copied from `.bkit/templates/` (`bkit-ci.yml`, `bkit-cloud.yml`, `bkit-renovate.yml`) are theirs and stay out of `ignorePaths` so their pins refresh. bkit's own `.github/renovate.json5` uses the same `ignorePaths` (`.github/renovate.json5:83-89`).
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** `docs/deployments.md` (§ GitHub Actions pinning, § Dependency updaters), `.bkit/templates.md` § Dependabot and Renovate, `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`, `.github/renovate.json5`
rootCause: `enabled: false` suppresses _version updates_, but the `github-actions` manager still SCANS the file and Renovate's tag→SHA `pinDigests` (enabled globally for github-actions) is applied anyway — so the Pin PR keeps getting created.
remediation: List the file in `ignorePaths` — the only thing that stops the pinning; `enabled: false` is NOT sufficient. Keep copied workflows (`bkit-ci.yml`, `bkit-cloud.yml`, `bkit-renovate.yml`) out of `ignorePaths` so their pins refresh; bkit's own `.github/renovate.json5` matches the template's `ignorePaths`.

summary: Renovate's hosted lockfile regen ignores `pnpm.overrides` — fence overridden packages in your own `renovate.json5`
description: A package pinned in root `pnpm.overrides` gets its locked version rewritten by Renovate on an eligible bump while the override stays in `package.json`. The resulting `pnpm-lock.yaml` is inconsistent → CI fails `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE … doesn't satisfy range`, `automerge` never fires, and Renovate keeps recreating/rebasing the branch, clobbering any manually-corrected lockfile pushed to it.
rootCause: Renovate's hosted lockfile regeneration does NOT reconcile the bumped version against `pnpm.overrides` (local `pnpm` does). Any `pnpm.overrides`-pinned package can hit it. The fence is repo-specific, so it belongs in the consumer's own Renovate config, never in bkit's shipped example.
remediation: Add `{ matchPackageNames: ["<pkg>"], enabled: false }` to `packageRules` in your own `.github/renovate.json5` (copied from `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`; the copy is the whole config — no local preset). Land it on the default branch; Renovate reads config from there. Rule: `docs/deployments.md` § Dependency updaters (Fence a `pnpm.overrides` pin).

summary: pnpm >=10.34.3 auth rework — project `.npmrc` `${BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL}` 401s on download; use user-level `pnpm config set`
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Symptom:** `pnpm install` / `pnpm add @cbartens/bkit` fails with `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_401` (`GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@cbartens%2Fbkit: Unauthorized`) on pnpm >=10.34.3 even though `BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL` is correctly set in the environment. Metadata calls (`pnpm view @cbartens/bkit`) still resolve, so "it works locally" via `view` is misleading — only the actual download 401s. pnpm 10.34.1 is unaffected (the regression boundary is between 10.34.1 and 10.34.3).
- **Root cause:** pnpm's auth-handling rework stopped honouring a project-level `.npmrc` env-substitution `//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL}` at install fetch time. The token must instead live in pnpm's user-level auth config. Independently, config precedence is project `.npmrc` > user config, so a leftover project auth line also shadows a correct user-level token.
- **Fix or rule:** Commit ONLY the registry mapping in the project `.npmrc` (`@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`) — NEVER an `_authToken` line. Do NOT "restore" the project `.npmrc` `_authToken` line: it appears to work only on pnpm 10.34.1 (warning + store cache) and 401s again the instant pnpm bumps.

- **Source:** human

summary: `GH_TOKEN` in shell overrides `gh auth login` keyring
description:
- **Category:** integrations
- **Symptom:** Agent or human reports "`GH_TOKEN` env var is overriding the keyring token which has proper repo scopes"; `gh` behaves differently from `gh auth status` expectations.
- **Root cause:** `gh` checks `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` before the OS keyring. bkit historically exported `GH_TOKEN` from `.bkit/.env` for both MCP and CLI — direnv put a fine-grained PAT in the shell and shadowed `gh auth login`.
- **Fix or rule:** Use `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` in `.bkit/.env` for the GitHub MCP server only (`Authorization: Bearer ${BKIT_GH_TOKEN}` in `.mcp.json`). Use `gh auth login` for the CLI locally — do not export `GH_TOKEN` from `.bkit/.env`. Cloud dashboards: set `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` for MCP; authenticate `gh` via setup/bootstrap (`gh auth login --with-token`) or cloud-only `GH_TOKEN` if headless CLI requires it. CI keeps `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` in workflow steps (unchanged).
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** #287, KN-CORE-1, `.bkit/.env.example`, `.mcp.json`
rootCause: `gh` checks `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` before the OS keyring. bkit historically exported `GH_TOKEN` from `.bkit/.env` for both MCP and CLI — direnv put a fine-grained PAT in the shell and shadowed `gh auth login`.
remediation: Use `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` in `.bkit/.env` for the GitHub MCP server only (`Authorization: Bearer ${BKIT_GH_TOKEN}` in `.mcp.json`). Use `gh auth login` for the CLI locally — do not export `GH_TOKEN` from `.bkit/.env`. Cloud dashboards: set `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` for MCP; authenticate `gh` via setup/bootstrap (`gh auth login --with-token`) or cloud-only `GH_TOKEN` if headless CLI requires it. CI keeps `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` in workflow steps (unchanged).

summary: lint:prose treated a gitignored, absent .vale/styles/write-good the same as an absent vale binary, so the pre-commit prose gate silently self-disabled in every worktree and fresh checkout
description:
- **Category:** tooling
- **Symptom:** commits made from a git worktree passed pre-commit, then the SAME content failed prose linting the moment it was committed from the main clone. A write-good error rode along in three worktree commits undetected.
- **Root cause:** `lint:prose` gated on `command -v vale && [ -d .vale/styles/write-good ]` and, on failure, echoed one quiet line and exited 0. `.vale/styles/write-good` is gitignored (`vale sync` downloads it), so it is absent in every fresh checkout AND every `git worktree add` — `.vale/styles/House` IS tracked, so the parent dir exists and nothing looks wrong. The guard conflated two conditions: an absent vale binary (unrecoverable, skip is correct) and unsynced styles (fully recoverable).
- **Fix or rule:** a gate whose enabling data is gitignored must self-heal or fail loudly, never skip quietly. `bkit ci prose` (what `lint:prose` runs) copies write-good from the main worktree (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, zero network), falls back to `vale sync`, and warns on stderr if vale is present but neither worked (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/ci/ci.ts:277-360`). Skip stays silent ONLY when the vale binary itself is missing.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** BAR-138 (F9 guard), `.bkit/core/engine/commands/ci/ci.ts`
rootCause: lint:prose treated absent gitignored .vale/styles/write-good identically to an absent vale binary and soft-skipped with exit 0. The styles dir is missing in every fresh checkout and worktree, so the pre-commit prose gate reported success while enforcing nothing.
remediation: self-heal the recoverable case (copy write-good from the main worktree via git rev-parse --git-common-dir, then vale sync as fallback) and warn LOUDLY on stderr when vale is present but self-heal failed. Reserve the silent skip for a genuinely absent vale binary. Generally: a gate whose enabling data is gitignored must self-heal or fail loudly.

summary: Doc content added inside a bkit managed block must also be added to the template source or bkit check reports drift plus a cascading .bkit/version pin write
description: When a build task adds new prose to a root docs file (e.g. docs/deployments.md) INSIDE the <!-- bkit:start --> ... <!-- bkit:end --> managed block, the corresponding .bkit/shared/docs/<file>.md template must receive the same content (with token substitution where needed). If only the root is updated, bkit check reports N write(s) of drift because its core templates pass renders the template and compares the managed block byte-for-byte. A secondary .bkit/version write cascades from this: postDispatch records canonical hashes from ws.writes, and any write populates newCanonicalEntries -> needsWrite=true. Content added OUTSIDE the managed block (bkit dogfood documentation) does NOT require template sync — the template intentionally ships only the managed block, and bkit upgrade (Tier-2) only replaces content between markers. This asymmetry is by design: the root doc can carry bkit-specific dogfood content that is never shipped to consumers.
rootCause: bkit check core templates pass renders the template with token substitution and compares the managed block to the root doc; any content inside the bkit:start/bkit:end markers that exists in the root but not the template is flagged as drift. The .bkit/version pin write cascades from any core-template drift because postDispatch populates canonical hashes from ws.writes entries.
remediation: Mirror any managed-block doc addition into .bkit/shared/docs/<file>.md (applying token substitution for main->{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}, cbartens/bkit->{{REPO_SLUG}} where present). Run pnpm bkit check to verify 0 writes before committing. Verify with pnpm bkit check -> expect 0 write(s). If the content is outside the managed block (dogfood), NO template change is needed.

summary: git branch names may legally contain shell metacharacters ('$();&) per git check-ref-format; interpolating a captured branch name into a double-quoted/eval'd trap body is command injection at EXIT
rootCause: The expand-now trap form `trap "git checkout '$VAR' ..." EXIT` (SC2064 disabled) re-parses the captured branch name as shell text when the trap fires, so a branch name carrying an embedded $(...) payload executes at process exit.
remediation: Keep externally-influenced data out of shell text: pass branch names, PR titles and similar to git / gh as single argv entries from Node (`git(cwd, args)` in `.bkit/core/engine/commands/lib.ts`), never a shell-interpreted string (`docs/security.md` § Shell Injection). Workflow files carry no `trap`; the dev lock is acquired and released inside the `bkit branches` / `bkit locks` commands (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/locks.ts`, `branches.ts` `finally`). Where a shell trap is unavoidable, single-quote its body so variables resolve at fire time, never at install time.

summary: OpenCode Go premium models (kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus) are invisible to the /zen/v1/models REST probe — Zen and Go are two separate models.dev providers with different endpoints; models.dev is the source of truth
description:
- **Category:** provider-integration / model-curation
- **Symptom:** curating bkit's opencode model column against `curl https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` reported Kimi K3 as 'not live on OpenCode Go' when the opencode app's model selector clearly listed 'Kimi K3 (2x usage)' under OpenCode Go. Adding an API key to the same endpoint did NOT change the result. A chat round-trip to `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions` with model `kimi-k3` returned `ModelError: Model kimi-k3 is not supported`.
- **Root cause:** OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go are TWO DISTINCT providers on models.dev — `opencode` ('OpenCode Zen', api `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`) and `opencode-go` ('OpenCode Go', api `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`). The `/zen/v1/models` REST endpoint returns ONLY the Zen catalog; Go-only premium models never appear there regardless of auth. The opencode app populates its model selector from models.dev.
- **Fix or rule:** Curate opencode model pins from `https://models.dev/api.json` (providers `.opencode` and `.["opencode-go"]` `.models`), NEVER from `/zen/v1/models` alone. Tool-call-smoke Go pins against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`. bkit ships two providers `opencode-zen` + `opencode-go`, both emitting a minimal `provider.<id>` with only `options.apiKey: "{env:BKIT_OPENCODE_API_KEY}"` — no npm driver, no baseURL (`.bkit/providers.md:487`). One `BKIT_OPENCODE_API_KEY` covers both. `--opencode=<provider>` is a strict allowlist (`OPENCODE_PROVIDERS`: `openrouter`, `ollama`, `opencode-zen`, `opencode-go` — `.bkit/core/engine/shared/egress.ts:10`); no bare `opencode` alias exists.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** medium
- **Scope:** bkit-repo
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** `.bkit/providers.md` § Models (Per-provider live model lookup recipe); `.bkit/prompts.md` § Models Live model-ID verification.
rootCause: OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go are two distinct models.dev providers (`opencode` at https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 and `opencode-go` at https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1). The /zen/v1/models REST endpoint returns only the Zen catalog, so Go-only premium models (kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.7-max) are invisible to it regardless of auth. The opencode app reads its catalog from models.dev, not that endpoint.
remediation: Curate opencode pins from https://models.dev/api.json (providers .opencode and .['opencode-go']), never from /zen/v1/models alone. Smoke Go pins against https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions. bkit ships two providers opencode-zen + opencode-go (minimal provider blocks keyed by BKIT_OPENCODE_API_KEY, no npm driver or baseURL); the provider flag is a strict allowlist with no bare `opencode` alias.

summary: Plan file:line anchors are coordinates against the plan's own baseSha, and every sub-plan anchor additionally assumes its predecessors landed, so a stale plan is re-pointed by symbol and never renumbered
description: A plan artifact's file:line anchors resolve against the baseSha in its bkit:anchor header, not against dev. Sub-plans carry a second implicit baseline on top: their anchors describe the tree their predecessor sub-plans leave behind, stated in the artifacts' own PRE-Task coordinate banners, so a sub-plan's numbers can be wrong against the current tree and right against the tree it will execute on. Mapping every anchor forward to HEAD converts a detectably stale plan into an undetectably wrong one. Bare backtick line refs compound it: they attach to a filename earlier in the sentence, frequently with unrelated paths in between, so nearest-preceding-path attribution silently reassigns them to the wrong file. Path and marker-vocabulary renames are the separable safe half, carrying no line semantics.
rootCause: A plan is written against one tree and built against another. The anchor header (`bkit branches anchor-stamp`) records the baseline, and the only comparison against the current tree is build Step 4 — Plan Current (`bkit branches anchor-read --against=origin/dev`, then `@bkit-build-plan-current`), which runs when the build starts, not when the plan is edited. Sub-plan drift stays invisible because each sub-plan's numbers are correct relative to a predecessor state rather than to anything the reader can observe.
remediation: Apply the mechanical renames in full across every artifact including the design and the parent plan, not only the sub-plans the drift was noticed in. Add a coordinate banner to each in the artifacts' existing PRE-Task idiom naming what was renamed, listing every cited file changed since the baseline, and instructing resolve-by-symbol-marker-or-heading. Leave the line numbers untouched and leave the anchor header's baseSha at its original value; it records what the plan was written against, and forging it forward tells the runtime that reads it the plan is current. Re-locate confirmed-dead anchors by their quoted prose rather than their number before editing at that position.

summary: Every permissions.allow row in .claude/settings.json was inert in cloud sessions because Claude Code applies allow rules only after a workspace trust dialog that a -p/SDK session never shows
description: A cloud /bkit-debug run prompted once per Bash call and stalled at the fetch-context step. The whole Claude permission strategy was one blanket Bash(*) allow row, and it was doing nothing: allow rules and additionalDirectories GRANT capability, so Claude Code holds them until the workspace trust dialog is accepted, and it never shows that dialog in a claude -p or SDK session. deny and ask were unaffected, which is why destructive-op gating still looked healthy. The only signal was one stderr line ('Ignoring 32 permissions.allow entries from .claude/settings.json: this workspace has not been trusted') that no cloud session surfaces, so the config read as configured and did nothing. Verified in a cloud container on Claude Code 2.1.265: flipping the key produced empty stderr and all 32 entries applied.
rootCause: bkit configured permissions only in the repo and assumed repo config was sufficient everywhere. Nothing in the cloud path ever set projects[<repo root>].hasTrustDialogAccepted, and no gate or test asserted that the shipped allow list was in effect at runtime rather than merely present on disk. Committing the config could never have fixed it: a git-tracked .claude/settings.local.json is treated as repository-supplied and held behind the same gate.
remediation: The generated cloud setup script now writes projects[<repo path>].hasTrustDialogAccepted into ~/.claude.json via a jq merge, placed after the jq install. That is the only reliable point: it runs as root, pre-clone, pre-Claude, and is snapshotted, whereas settings resolve before SessionStart and .claude/ is a protected path an in-session write cannot take. The container clone path is an observation rather than a contract, so .claude/hooks/bkit-cloud-bootstrap.sh re-checks the discovered git root each session and warns loudly on mismatch. It diagnoses only and does not write: a SessionStart hook that grants workspace trust on any path it discovers is broader capability than the fix needs, and it could not help the current session anyway. A jq probe on the same key is in the cloud verify step.

summary: Source-to-rendered-mirror diff is non-empty by construction; authoritative drift check is bkit check, not a raw diff
description: A raw `diff .bkit/core/workflows/<file>.md .claude/commands/<file>.md` is NON-empty because the source carries `<!-- bkit:tracker {github,linear,true} start/end -->` template markers for ALL trackers, which `bkit install` resolves to the configured tracker and strips during render. The authoritative mirror-drift check is `bkit check` exiting 0: host mirrors push would-writes (content drift or orphan delete) into the writeset, and any would-write prints `N write(s) would occur — DRIFT DETECTED` and exits 1 (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/check.ts:38-60`). "Byte-identical" applies ONLY to (a) adopted template copies at the repo root (`scripts/<tool>/` etc.) against `.bkit/templates/`, after the edits `.bkit/core/engine/audits/repo/dogfood-templates.test.ts` lists, and (b) the templates-content snapshot enforcing rendered<->rendered idempotency — NEVER to source<->mirror.
rootCause: tracker template resolution is fundamental to bkit mirror rendering; a Done-when or gate claim that a source<->mirror `diff` is empty is never literally satisfiable.
remediation: Word any mirror-drift Done-when / gate checkbox as: `bkit check` exits 0 with no `DRIFT DETECTED` AND `bkit install` reports 0 writes. Do NOT assert source<->mirror byte-identity.

summary: Ship Step 9 — Re-validate fired a second, duplicate CI run on every head move because it dispatched unconditionally instead of probing first
description: Every ship that took Path B (rebase / gh pr update-branch) produced TWO completed CI runs on the SAME commit, seconds apart: one from the pull_request event the push itself fired, one from ship's own gh workflow run. Observed five times on feat/380-roadmap-analysis-refresh -- e.g. head 1b51b989 ran pull_request at 21:07:21 (run 33013836266) and workflow_dispatch at 21:07:52 (run 33013876939); same shape at ea6f17f7 (5s apart), ea37e5c8 (3s), bb981805 (3s), 11a74fd4 (9s). Doubled CI minutes and wall-clock on every rebase-integrating ship.
rootCause: Step 9 — Re-validate dispatched `gh workflow run` on every head move with no check for a run already at that head, so the pull_request run the force-push had just triggered was ignored. The CI-Dispatch Gate's presence probe (build and debug) was not applied to ship, on the grounds that a dispatch-outcome verdict would mask 'essential tests skipped' -- a valid objection to the gate's pass semantics but not to its probe. ci.yml concurrency cannot absorb the duplicate either: pull_request runs group by head_ref while workflow_dispatch runs group by run_id, so the two land in different groups and neither cancels the other.
remediation: Ship Step 9 — Re-validate runs `bkit runs revalidate`, which probes for a run at the validated head before any dispatch (`--until=present --dispatch-if-absent` internally, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/runs.ts:1622`; `SHIP_PROBE_ATTEMPTS` x `SHIP_PROBE_INTERVAL_S` = 6 x 10s in `.bkit/core/engine/shared/timeouts.ts`) and runs `gh workflow run {bkit.ciWorkflow}` only when no run is found; a blocked sleep (exit 81) or missing `gh` (exit 80) does not dispatch (`runs.ts:1174`) and hands off to the agent turn loop / MCP fallback. The probe is never a pass condition -- `bkit runs gate` at Step 10 — Merge Gate + Merge PR owns the verdict. Run targets are head-anchored (`headSha == head` in `runs.ts`), because without a guaranteed-fresh dispatch the newest run on the branch can be a completed run from a superseded head.

summary: Slash-command argument substitution rewrites $0 inside workflow bash before the model reads it, turning awk programs into syntax errors that fail silently
description: Invoking /bkit-plan with an issue argument replaced every literal $0 in the rendered command body with that argument. The file on disk was correct; the corruption is host-side argument expansion, where $N is documented shorthand for $ARGUMENTS[N], zero-based. The clobbered ledger scan in bkit-plan.md wrote None. to related-deferrals.md while docs/deferrals.jsonl held 16 matching rows.
rootCause: awk field references and the host placeholder syntax share the $-digit token, and the call site M=$(awk ...) discards awk's exit status, so the dead program produced an empty capture that read as no matches. $1 to $9 carried the same latent hazard: an index with no matching argument is left unchanged, so awk '{print $2}' survived one-argument invocations and would break on three.
remediation: Rewrite every awk field reference in .bkit/core/workflows/*.md as $(N) — POSIX, identical behaviour, no $-digit sequence for any host to rewrite. The host's backslash escape was rejected: it is Claude-Code-specific and would render verbatim into .cursor/commands/ and .opencode/commands/. Gated by bkit-slash-arg-expansion.test.ts, which bans $0-$9 and $ARGUMENTS across the workflow corpus. Scope excludes .bkit/scripts/*.sh and .github/workflows/*.yml, which execute as files and whose $1 is a real positional parameter with no $(N) equivalent.

summary: Workflow bookkeeping staging built its pathspec with shell word-splitting and an ls glob that aborts under zsh, silently dropping ledgers and swallowing a failed git add into a false success
description: The host shell for .bkit/core/workflows/*.md fenced bash blocks is not guaranteed to be bash -- confirmed zsh (5.9) on stock macOS Claude Code, $0=/bin/zsh, BASH_VERSION unset. BOOK_PATHS was built with unquoted $BOOK_PATHS interpolation (word-splits differently per shell) and an `ls docs/plans/*/logs/*/*.jsonl docs/*.jsonl .bkit/*.jsonl` sweep whose glob ABORTS under zsh when a component matches nothing, dropping the whole sweep silently in a fresh consumer repo (bash just passes the unmatched literal pattern through). Nothing in these blocks sets `set -e`, so a failed `git add` (exit 128, e.g. a locked index) fell through the subsequent `git diff --cached --quiet` check into `no bookkeeping delta to record -- nothing committed, nothing pushed`: a loud failure disguised as a legitimate no-op.
rootCause: Two independent host-shell dependencies stacked: (1) unquoted variable interpolation for the pathspec, word-split differently per shell and unsafe with paths containing spaces; (2) an `ls a/*/b` glob sweep, which bash passes through unmatched but zsh aborts. Neither failure path was distinguishable from success because the workflow blocks never check `git add`'s own exit code before concluding there was nothing to commit.
remediation: Bookkeeping stage/commit routes through `bkit ledgers commit` (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/ledgers.ts`), a Node command, so the host shell never matters. It builds the pathspec with `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` against quoted globs (git does the matching, so an unmatched glob is empty output, never an abort) and stages/commits via `--pathspec-from-file --pathspec-file-nul` instead of a re-interpolated string. `git add` failures exit 4 (never swallowed), and an empty pathspec list refuses to reach `commit` (exit 6) -- `git commit --pathspec-from-file=<empty file>` does not commit nothing, it silently commits whatever is already staged in the index, which is a worse trap than the original bug. General rule: workflow bash blocks must not rely on shell word-splitting or unmatched-glob passthrough (.agents/rules.md § Workflow bash blocks); workflow files call no `.bkit/scripts/` script, logic beyond plain shell lives in a `bkit` command (.bkit/workflows.md § Workflow commands).

summary: opencode spec churn — pin the probed version, not a naive next-digit bump
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Symptom:** After upgrading opencode or updating `opencode.json`, agents fail to launch or plugin API calls are rejected with schema errors.
- **Root cause:** opencode's plugin spec, frontmatter fields (`reasoningEffort`, provider config shape), and command-file syntax change between releases without a stable semver contract. Naively bumping a version number or copying from release notes produces configs that may never have existed in the actual binary.
- **Fix or rule:** Probe the installed opencode binary for its supported field names and plugin API shape before updating `opencode.json`. Read `.opencode/opencode.json` against the opencode docs for the version that `opencode --version` reports. When in doubt, copy from a fresh `opencode init` output with that version, not from examples in issues or READMEs that may lag the release.
- **Type:** gotcha
- **Confidence:** medium (observed during #245 spike; spec drift confirmed across minor releases)
- **Severity:** normal
- **Scope:** consumer
- **Source:** agent
- **Related:** #245, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/install.ts` (applyOpencodeAgent transform), `docs/plans/202606/logs/245-opencode-provider-host/spike-verdict.md`
rootCause: opencode's plugin spec, frontmatter fields (`reasoningEffort`, provider config shape), and command-file syntax change between releases without a stable semver contract. Naively bumping a version number or copying from release notes produces configs that may never have existed in the actual binary.
remediation: Probe the installed opencode binary for its supported field names and plugin API shape before updating `opencode.json`. Read `.opencode/opencode.json` against the opencode docs for the version that `opencode --version` reports. When in doubt, copy from a fresh `opencode init` output with that version, not from examples in issues or READMEs that may lag the release.

summary: `pnpm test` at default vitest thread concurrency intermittently times out heavy integration suites (bkit-slop-type-suppression, bkit-check-opencode, bkit-upgrade) on resource-constrained machines; not a code regression
rootCause: vitest defaults to CPU-count worker threads; several *.integration.test.ts files spawn real subprocesses (tsx, git, jq) with a 5s per-test timeout. Under full-suite parallel load on a constrained machine, those subprocess spawns intermittently exceed 5s and time out — the failures are non-deterministic and clear when concurrency is reduced.
remediation: Before treating a `pnpm test` failure in one of these integration files as a real regression, re-run just that file in isolation (`npx vitest run <file>`) or the full suite with `--maxWorkers=2`; if it passes there, it is this flake, not a defect in the change under review. Not fixed at the infra level here (no vitest pool/timeout config change) — that is a shared-infra decision out of scope for a single gap-remediation task.

summary: [skip ci] can suppress CI on dev by riding in the squash-merge BODY (concatenated intermediate commit subjects), not just the PR title — a title-only assertion misses it
description: Incident: a ship of #703 squash-merged 16 commits into one PR; one intermediate commit subject was `chore(690-header-nav-shell): worktree-setup bkit [skip ci]`. GitHub Actions scans the merge commit's subject AND body for suppression tokens. `gh pr merge --squash` without an explicit `--body ""` defaults to a body that concatenates every commit's subject line, so the token leaked into the merge body even though the PR TITLE carried none. The workflow's only mechanised check at the time was a PR-title grep (never scans the resulting merge body); the backstop was an after-the-fact `gh run list` check, not a preventive assertion.
rootCause: gh's `--squash` default body behaviour (concatenate commit subjects) plus a title-only skip-token assertion that never re-scans the body it actually produces.
remediation: Merge/commit bodies that land work MUST be skip-token-free on every transport (`.agents/rules.md` § Git, CI & Merges — shared invariant, not owned by one call site). Ship merges through `bkit prs merge`, which runs `gh pr merge --squash --subject <skip-token-free subject> --body ""` (`mergePr`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/prs.ts:421`). The MCP `merge_pull_request` fallback passes the printed subject as `commit_message` with an empty body, never the tool's default. A title-only pre-merge assertion is NOT sufficient by itself — treat it as one layer, not the guarantee.

summary: Running multiple bats files in one `bats tests/a.bats tests/b.bats ...` invocation intermittently fails with `Failed to create BATS_TEST_TMPDIR1: ... File exists` on macOS — run each file in its own invocation, not as a single multi-file arg
rootCause: bats reuses BATS_RUN_TMPDIR across files in a multi-file invocation and the per-test TMPDIR1 numbering collides when test indices overlap across files (the mktemp mkdir hits an already-existing dir). On stock macOS this surfaces as a `mkdir: ... File exists / Failed to create BATS_TEST_TMPDIR1` storm and a final `Executed N instead of expected M tests`, exiting non-zero even though every individual test passed when the file ran alone.
remediation: Invoke one bats file per call (e.g. `bats tests/ship-gate.bats`, then `bats tests/ship-failure-path.bats`) for the seam-verification prelude and any per-file gate check. `pnpm bkit:test:bats` (`bats tests/*.bats`, the glob form) is fine in CI on Linux; the collision is macOS-local. This is a test-harness portability quirk, not a regression in the script under test — confirm by re-running the single failing file in isolation.

summary: A bash-syntax variable reference (${LABELS:-}) written in a *.bkit/core/workflows/*.md prompt is NOT auto-populated by an earlier MCP call in the same numbered step tree unless the SAME Bash tool-call sets it — an intervening tool-call boundary (MCP read, or an earlier numbered step) resets the shell
rootCause: *.bkit/core/workflows/*.md files are natural-language instructions executed by an LLM agent turn-by-turn; each fenced bash block the agent runs is typically its own subprocess/tool-call with no persisted state from a prior tool-call. Writing `echo "${LABELS:-}"` in a bash fence several steps after a `LABELS` value was extracted via an MCP call (a separate tool-call) silently expands to empty every time, because the variable was never assigned IN that shell invocation.
remediation: Two idioms fix it, matching bkit-build.md/bkit-debug.md precedent: (1) re-derive the value in the SAME bash fence it is used (e.g. gh CLI call), or (2) materialise it into a mktemp handoff file immediately adjacent to the original read (same numbered step) and pass the file path forward via GITHUB_ENV / an explicit variable, then read-and-fallback at the point of use (`if [ -f "$HANDOFF_FILE" ]; then ...; else <same-block re-derive>; fi`). Never write bare `${VAR:-}` in a bash fence and assume an earlier step (even a few lines above) populated it — verify the SAME fenced bash block both sets and uses it, or that a handoff file/GITHUB_ENV var carries it forward.

summary: spawnSync output past maxBuffer raises ENOBUFS, but status can still be 0
rootCause: Node raises ENOBUFS when captured output passes maxBuffer and then SIGTERMs the child. If the child has already exited, status is its real exit code, often 0. Timing decides which: a 64 MiB+ probe exited 0 two runs in five on macOS and was SIGTERMed on Linux. A wrapper that reads only status reports cut-off output as success.
remediation: Treat res.error as failure whatever res.status says: `res.error && status === 0 ? 1 : status` (runTool in .bkit/core/engine/commands/lib.ts, gitRaw in .bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/ledgers.ts). Never infer success from status alone after a spawnSync with maxBuffer.

summary: Trivy fs skips npm / pnpm / yarn dev dependencies unless --include-dev-deps is set
rootCause: Trivy treats dev dependencies as not shipped and drops them from JS lockfiles by default. A repo whose lockfile is mostly dev tooling scans zero packages and passes green: bkit read 0 packages without the flag and 193 with it.
remediation: Keep --include-dev-deps in every trivy fs invocation (bkit-trivy.yml template asserts it in templates-content.test.ts). When checking a scanner run, confirm the package count is non-zero, not just the exit code.

summary: A stale docs/capabilities.md reached dev because the pre-push graphify block only printed a NOTE
rootCause: #612 Oxlint template, test-lint tip and #622 merge changed the module graph; nobody rebuilt docs/capabilities.md. bkit-graph-pre-push.sh was warn-only and advised landing the refresh with bkit [skip ci]; graph:check is not in bkit:gate:static → push of 08ecf9b6 went through, CI bkit-tests-static failed on Check Capability Register.
remediation: Pre-push block now blocks a push to dev on drift (check-at on the pushed commit). Fix a red: pnpm graph:refresh, commit. Never run graph:update && graph:rollup in a checkout holding someone else's uncommitted edits: graphify reads the working tree and bakes them into the register.

summary: Roadmap close-hooks stage `.bkit/issues.jsonl` three different ways — assert each shape independently
description: design/plan land through `bkit branches land`: the direct close appends the feature row (`appendFeature`) into the close commit it builds in a throwaway `.worktrees/_land-{FID}` off origin/dev and pushes as dev (`buildClose`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/branches.ts:980-1032`); the PR close (dev push refused) appends the row in the checkout holding the branch and commits it before the merge (`landPr`, `branches.ts:1104-1140`). build/debug close-hooks run `bkit roadmap mirror --workflow=<build|debug> --fid=<FID>`: append the row in the worktree, then the same row on dev under the dev lock, fail-open (skipped in adopt mode, on a busy lock, or on a failed dev checkout / push) (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/roadmap.ts:429`). ship appends the SHIPPED row in the worktree (`bkit roadmap feature --root=<worktree> --workflow=ship --strict`, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-ship.md:384`) and stages it through `bkit ledgers commit`. A single assertion cannot cover all three shapes.
rootCause: Workflows commit the roadmap artifacts through structurally different git operations; asserting one shape leaves the others unverified.
remediation: When touching close-hook staging, assert each shape independently (design/plan `bkit branches land` direct or PR path, build/debug `bkit roadmap mirror`, ship `bkit roadmap feature` + `bkit ledgers commit`).

summary: Roadmap close-hooks stage `.bkit/issues.jsonl` three different ways — assert each shape independently
description: design/plan land through `bkit branches land`: the direct close appends the feature row (`appendFeature`) into the close commit it builds in a throwaway `.worktrees/_land-{FID}` off origin/dev and pushes as dev (`landDirect` / `buildClose` in `.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/branches.ts`); the PR close (dev push refused by the server) appends the row in the checkout holding the branch and commits it before the merge (`landPr`, same file). build/debug close-hooks run `bkit roadmap mirror --workflow=<build|debug> --fid=<FID>` (`mirror` in `.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/roadmap.ts`): append the row in the worktree, then land the same row on dev through the same throwaway origin/dev checkout (`pushToDev`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/land.ts`), fail-open (skipped when the run's checkout is on dev; a refused push, dev moving before every attempt, or a failed fetch / checkout logs and continues). ship appends the SHIPPED row in the worktree (`bkit roadmap feature --root=<worktree> --workflow=ship --strict`, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-ship.md` Step 6) and stages it through `bkit ledgers commit`. A single assertion cannot cover all three shapes.
rootCause: Workflows commit the roadmap artifacts through structurally different git operations; asserting one shape leaves the others unverified.
remediation: When touching close-hook staging, assert each shape independently (design/plan `bkit branches land` direct or PR path, build/debug `bkit roadmap mirror`, ship `bkit roadmap feature` + `bkit ledgers commit`).

summary: git branch names may legally contain shell metacharacters ('$();&) per git check-ref-format; interpolating a captured branch name into a double-quoted/eval'd trap body is command injection at EXIT
rootCause: The expand-now trap form `trap "git checkout '$VAR' ..." EXIT` (SC2064 disabled) re-parses the captured branch name as shell text when the trap fires, so a branch name carrying an embedded $(...) payload executes at process exit.
remediation: Keep externally-influenced data out of shell text: pass branch names, PR titles and similar to git / gh as single argv entries from Node (`git(cwd, args)` in `.bkit/core/engine/commands/lib.ts`), never a shell-interpreted string (`docs/security.md` § Shell Injection). Workflow files carry no `trap`; clean-up that must run on every exit lives inside the `bkit` commands (`try` / `finally` in `.bkit/core/engine/commands/land.ts` `pushToDev`, which removes its throwaway checkout on every path). Where a shell trap is unavoidable, single-quote its body so variables resolve at fire time, never at install time.

summary: Workflow state is append-only `status.jsonl` under `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/`; it reaches `dev` only via squash-merge
description:
- **Category:** workflow
- **Rule:** Workflow state lives in `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl` — append-only NDJSON (one event per line; prior lines never mutated), folded to derive current state. Canonical reducer `.bkit/core/engine/ledgers/status.ts` (`fold`). Workflows only; agents MUST NOT read or write it.
- **Placement:** `build` / `debug` write and commit it on `feat/{FID}` via the per-step commits — NO mid-lifecycle `dev` push; state reaches `dev` once, at ship's PR squash-merge. `design` / `plan` do the same on a throwaway `feat/{FID}`; status and generated docs reach `dev` together via the Close-Workflow squash-merge (`docs({FID}): {phase} DONE`). `ship` books every step in its feature worktree (`BOOK_ROOT` = `{WORKTREE_PATH}`) and never checks out `dev`: pre-merge rows ride the PR, post-merge rows land with the Step 14 close commit built in a throwaway `origin/dev` checkout — the legitimate `dev` landing.
- **Merge safety:** `docs/plans/**/status.jsonl merge=union` in `.gitattributes` — both branches' lines concatenate; the reader de-dupes on `(workflow, step, parentSha, at)` and orders by `at`.
- **Mechanism:** `parentSha` is captured at step START via `git rev-parse HEAD`, before the step's commit.
- **Type:** rule
- **Confidence:** high
- **Severity:** normal
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-187, BAR-183, BAR-184, `.bkit/workflows.md` § `status.jsonl` — workflow state SoT, `.bkit/core/engine/ledgers/status.ts`
remediation: Derive state by folding `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl`; never push status to `dev` mid-lifecycle.

summary: A release squash merge whose message lists the dev commits carries their [skip ci] markers, so neither main CI nor the Release workflow on the tag starts
rootCause: GitHub skips push-triggered workflows when the pushed commit message contains [skip ci] (or [ci skip], [no ci], [skip actions], [actions skip]) anywhere, body included. The repo squash default COMMIT_MESSAGES pasted every dev commit message into the release merge, 48 of them with [skip ci]. The push to main started no bkit-ci run, and the v5.5.0 tag on that commit started no Release run, so nothing published and no run failed to flag it.
remediation: Squash merges take the PR title and body (squash_merge_commit_title=PR_TITLE, squash_merge_commit_message=PR_BODY) on cbartens/bkit, gether-life/app-gether-life and fcte-com-au/visitfrasercoast-com. utility-new-release step 10 stops before tagging when the main merge message carries a skip marker. A tag already on such a commit is fixed by re-cutting through a new release PR and moving the tag, never by re-pushing the tag on the same commit.

summary: A standalone tracker true block placed between a github/linear/jira group and its false block makes the none render print a spurious No tracker connected stub
rootCause: The tracker renderer pairs the github, linear and jira blocks with a false block only when the false block follows the group directly; anything between them leaves the group unpaired and it renders the NONE_STUB line under none, while the false block then renders as a separate standalone block.
remediation: Order a Step 1 tracker region as github, linear, jira, false, then any standalone true block. After editing workflow sources, run the none render baselines (trackers.test.ts) and read the snapshot diff for a stray stub line.

summary: A retired wording that is a prefix of its new text makes pnpm wording:sync re-expand synced lines; a blank line inside a workflow list item makes prettier pad every block in it
rootCause: wording:sync rewrites any line that starts with a retired text into the clause text, so a retired block equal to the first part of the new text appends the new tail again on every run. Separately, one blank line inside a markdown list item makes prettier treat the item as loose and insert blank lines around every block in it, including tracker marker lines that must stay tight.
remediation: When the old clause text is a prefix of the new one, leave the old text out of the retired block. In a tracker-block list item, keep the block free of blank lines (put the else-case in the lead-in sentence or as a Route bullet), then run prettier --check on the workflow files and wording:sync twice to confirm it is idempotent.

summary: A prune gated on identity destroys rows the dedup fold dropped — friction keys truncate to ~68 chars and collide, so two distinct entries share one identity and only one is ever stored
description: Found while making bkit harvest MOVE consumer friction (#343). fold() is last-write-wins per identity(), so colliding rows collapse to ONE stored row. An identity-gated prune then deletes EVERY colliding row from the consumer while the store kept one — the loser exists nowhere. Reproduced against live consumer-a data: 'Plan Step 11: close-workflow STRAY guard rejects protocol-mandated docs/pending.md edit' (ts 1783944967776) and a different entry about docs/decisions.md + docs/pending.md edits truncate to the byte-identical key 'friction-plan-step-11-close-workflow-stray-guard-rejects-protocol-ma'; the first was destroyed. Harmless under the old copy-only harvest, fatal the moment harvest deletes. Second instance of the same shape: identity() has no default branch, so rows whose kind is outside VALID_KINDS all collide on undefined — live data has kind:'tool-failure' and kind:'agent-rework' rows in consumer-a friction, and the newer evicted the older from the store.
rootCause: identity() is a lossy projection of a row (kind+repo+key, or ts when key is absent), and fold() treats an identity match as an upsert. Anything gating a DELETE on that projection deletes rows the projection cannot distinguish. Two independent sources of collision: (1) friction keys are truncated at write time, so distinct content yields identical keys; (2) identity() returns undefined for kinds outside VALID_KINDS, mapping every unknown-kind row onto a single fold slot.
remediation: Gate any destructive drain on byte-for-byte row CONTENT read back off disk, never on identity, and keep a store of every DISTINCT row (content dedup), never of fold winners — `scripts/harvest/ledgers.ts` header invariants (the harvest, `pnpm harvest`). The same gate covers friction rows and the `chat` / `run` rows pruned from `.bkit/stats.jsonl`. A fold loser is then stored and safe to prune; consumer lines not in the store stay and are logged (`kept N line(s) not in the store`). `identity()` (`.bkit/core/engine/ledgers/telemetry.ts`) still has no branch for kinds outside VALID_KINDS — never gate a delete on it. General rule: an identity used for dedup/upsert is NOT safe as a delete gate.

summary: `prettier --check .` fails on a workflow's raw gate log unless the log's name pattern sits in the raw-gate-output block of both `.prettierignore` and `.bkit/templates/.prettierignore`: the current pnpm/vitest runner output starts with a blank line, and prettier's markdown parser then reflows the whole log.
rootCause: That block lists one pattern per log name. `bkit tests red` writes `docs/plans/*/logs/*/build-task-red-*.md`, which was never added, so the format gate reads raw runner output as markdown and every build's static gate fails.
remediation: When a command starts writing a new `docs/plans/*/logs/*/*.md` raw log, add its pattern to the raw-gate-output block of `.prettierignore` and `.bkit/templates/.prettierignore` in the same change, and name it in `.bkit/core/.bkit/workflows.md` § Gate logs plus the `.bkit/workflows.md` mirror.

summary: A unit-tier test file that spawns real child processes needs its own suite-level budget: the load-scaled budget's factor is `loadAverage / cores` floored at 1, so a box at or above capacity scales nothing
description: Symptom: 'Error: Test timed out in 5000ms' on a different child-process-spawning unit test each run, all green in isolation, on a box whose load average is at or above its core count. The repo's load-scaled budget (vitest.timeout-budget.ts, re-read per file by vitest.setup.ts) is wired and does apply to these files, but `loadFactor()` returns `loadAverage / cores` clamped to a floor of 1 — at load average 7.5 on 10 cores it returns 1, and at 13 it returns 1.34 — while contention inflates a spawn-heavy case's wall time about 9x (541ms idle to 5055ms under a full gate). So the factor is inert exactly when it is needed.
rootCause: `loadAverage / cores` reads a machine at full capacity as '1x slower than idle'. A CPU-bound test sharing its core with one other runnable process takes about 2x, and subprocess spawn latency plus memory and IO contention inflate it further, so the measured 1.0-1.34 is a large under-estimate; MAX_LOAD_FACTOR (6) is never reached in practice.
remediation: For a file whose cases spawn child processes, give the spawn-heavy suite its own load-scaled budget rather than relying on the unit base: `describe("…", { timeout: tierTimeouts(true).testTimeout }, …)` in `.bkit/core/engine/audits/repo/resolve-push-base.test.ts` (30s base, scaled by load, CI pinned to 1). `it(…, { timeout }, …)` is the equivalent per-case form, as `audits/templates/ci-scripts.test.ts` uses. Do NOT hard-code a bare number — a fixed 30s also flaked under the full gate for the shipped-suite case. The underlying factor under-scaling is still open (`.bkit/friction.jsonl` `pre-push-gate-flakes-under-concurrent-load-block-workflow-push`); a whole-config fix would raise `loadFactor` above 1 when load average reaches the core count, which would fix every such file at once.
